title: 正德八年福建鄉試錄
text:
福建鄉試録序
我
太祖高皇帝定鼎之三年卽
詔天下開科取士著其事爲令良
法美意傳之
列聖以迄於
皇上皆世守而遵行之是歲癸酉
===
復維其期福建藩司舉行如
例先是白于巡按監察御史
李如圭走幣帛于四方聘尋
等以司考校而御史李如圭
寔柄其事而臨焉乃特悉意
綜理謂作興宜隆固有縟其
儀文者矣謂防範宜密固有
punctuated:
福建鄉試録序

我太祖高皇帝定鼎之三年，卽詔天下開科取士，著其事爲令。良法美意，傳之列聖，以迄於皇上，皆世守而遵行之。是歲癸酉，復維其期，福建藩司舉行如例。先是，白于巡按監察御史李如圭，走幣帛于四方，聘尋等以司考校。而御史李如圭寔柄其事而臨焉，乃特悉意綜理。謂作興宜隆，固有縟其儀文者矣；謂防範宜密，固有
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Fujian Provincial Examination

In the third year after establishing his rule, our Emperor Taizu Gao issued an edict that examinations be held throughout the realm to recruit scholars, and established this practice by statute. This excellent institution and its fine intent were transmitted through successive sage emperors down to His Majesty, each generation preserving and observing them. This year, guiyou [1513], the appointed time came round again, and the Fujian Provincial Administration Commission conducted the examination according to precedent. Before this, it reported to the Regional Inspector, Investigating Censor Li Rugui, and dispatched gifts of silk in all directions to invite Xun [?] and others to oversee the examination and assessment. Censor Li Rugui himself took charge of the undertaking and supervised it, devoting his full attention to its overall management. Holding that the encouragement of learning deserved grand observances, he duly provided elaborate ceremonial forms; holding that safeguards should be stringent, he duly made provision for …

title: 正德八年福建鄉試錄
text:
嚴其科條者矣謂百執事必
皆其人固有選擇而充者矣
于時寇起鄰壤提督三省軍
務右副都御史俞諫巡撫汀
漳諸郡右副都御史周南咸
承
上命會兵於饒武功旣集文事適
===
舉鎮守福建太監崔安奉
命而來提督市舶太監尚春督理
糧餉南京户部主事胡德皆
有事玆土亦莫不崇獎斯文
以勵士氣旣八月入鎖院士
之就試者凡若干人皆提學
副使姚鏌所取以應選者也
punctuated:
嚴其科條者矣。謂百執事必皆其人，固有選擇而充者矣。于時寇起鄰壤，提督三省軍務右副都御史俞諫、巡撫汀漳諸郡右副都御史周南，咸承上命，會兵於饒。武功旣集，文事適舉。鎮守福建太監崔安奉命而來，提督市舶太監尚春、督理糧餉南京户部主事胡德，皆有事玆土，亦莫不崇獎斯文，以勵士氣。
旣八月，入鎖院。士之就試者凡若干人，皆提學副使姚鏌所取以應選者也。
translation_en:
…made its regulations strict. Holding that every functionary must be suited to his task, he duly selected men to fill the posts. At this time, bandits rose in neighboring territory. Yu Jian, Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and Superintendent of Military Affairs in the Three Provinces, and Zhou Nan, Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and Grand Coordinator of Tingzhou, Zhangzhou, and the other prefectures, both received imperial orders and assembled their forces at Rao. Military success had been achieved just as the literary undertaking began. Cui An, the eunuch Grand Director stationed in Fujian, came under imperial orders. Shang Chun, the eunuch Grand Director supervising maritime trade, and Hu De, a Secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue overseeing provisions and military pay, also had duties in this region. All honored and encouraged this literary enterprise to hearten the scholars.
When the eighth month arrived, we entered the examination compound and were secluded within it. The candidates who presented themselves for the examination numbered so many in all [the number is unspecified]. All had been selected to compete by Yao Mo, the Education Intendant serving as Vice Commissioner.

title: 正德八年福建鄉試錄
text:
御史李如圭復謂去取之法
宜公宜愼乃偕昪等焚香誓
戒而始事事凡三試之考試
爲昪與敎諭沈璋同考試爲
學正陳則敎諭羅幹尹孔常
方一德訓導劉文詔方準劉
芳王尚忠提調則左布政使
===
陳珂右參政孫燧監試則按
察使劉遜僉事胡鐸賛襄防
範於外則右布政使鄒文盛
左參政王子言左參議彭夔
副使湯沐僉事蔡天祐查約
胡璉而署都指揮僉事楊勲
崔灝亦相與協力焉事竣拔
punctuated: 御史李如圭復謂去取之法宜公宜愼，乃偕昪等焚香誓戒而始事。事凡三試之考試，爲昪與敎諭沈璋；同考試爲學正陳則、敎諭羅幹、尹孔常、方一德、訓導劉文詔、方準、劉芳、王尚忠。提調則左布政使陳珂、右參政孫燧；監試則按察使劉遜、僉事胡鐸。賛襄防範於外，則右布政使鄒文盛、左參政王子言、左參議彭夔、副使湯沐、僉事蔡天祐、查約、胡璉，而署都指揮僉事楊勲、崔灝亦相與協力焉。事竣，拔
translation_en:
Censor Li Rugui further declared that the procedures for rejecting or accepting candidates must be impartial and cautious. He therefore joined Bian and the others in burning incense and taking an oath of vigilance before beginning their work. The Examiners for the three examination sessions [?] were Bian and Instructor Shen Zhang. The Associate Examiners were Instructor Chen Ze; Instructors Luo Gan, Yin Kongchang, and Fang Yide; and Assistant Instructors Liu Wenzhao, Fang Zhun, Liu Fang, and Wang Shangzhong.

The Proctors were Provincial Administration Commissioner of the Left Chen Ke and Provincial Administration Vice Commissioner of the Right Sun Sui. The Examination Monitors were Provincial Surveillance Commissioner Liu Xun and Surveillance Assistant Commissioner Hu Duo. Providing assistance and maintaining safeguards outside were Provincial Administration Commissioner of the Right Zou Wensheng, Provincial Administration Vice Commissioner of the Left Wang Ziyan, Provincial Administration Assistant Commissioner of the Left Peng Kui, Surveillance Vice Commissioner Tang Mu, and Surveillance Assistant Commissioners Cai Tianyou, Zha Yue, and Hu Lian. Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioners Yang Xun and Cui Hao also joined in these efforts. When the work was completed, they selected…

title: 正德八年福建鄉試錄
text:
其尤得士九十人并集其文
之純者爲錄以
獻昇當序諸首簡惟閩士之於
文盛矣嘗卽而推之文章者
治化之徵也故元和之世特
號多才用其文與周漢軋嘉
祐治平之期其宗工鉅筆亦
===
並時而起名之相埒至有見
於翁季伯仲間者
國家以人文化成天下百六十
年于茲道久效臻固宜出而
秉大制作以鳴太平者若是
其班班而偏陬下邑之士皆
知占一經自奮以求齒上國
punctuated: 其尤，得士九十人，并集其文之純者爲錄以獻。昇當序諸首簡。惟閩士之於文，盛矣！嘗卽而推之，文章者，治化之徵也。故元和之世，特號多才，用其文與周漢軋。嘉祐、治平之期，其宗工鉅筆亦並時而起，名之相埒，至有見於翁季伯仲間者。國家以人文化成天下，百六十年于茲，道久效臻，固宜出而秉大制作以鳴太平者若是其班班。而偏陬下邑之士，皆知占一經，自奮以求齒上國。
translation_en:
…the most outstanding among them, obtaining ninety successful candidates; their finest writings were also collected into a record for presentation to the throne. I, Sheng, am charged with writing a preface for its opening pages. How flourishing are the literary achievements of Fujian’s scholars! On examining the matter, I have reflected that literary writing is a sign of good government and its transforming influence. Thus the Yuanhe era was especially renowned for its abundance of talent, and its writings rivaled those of the Zhou and Han. During the Jiayou and Zhiping eras, great literary masters likewise arose together, their reputations matching one another—even among fathers and sons and elder and younger brothers.

Our dynasty has transformed all under Heaven through cultural refinement for one hundred and sixty years now. Its Way has long prevailed, and its effects have reached fruition. It is surely fitting that so many distinguished men should emerge to undertake grand literary compositions and give voice to an age of peace. Even scholars from remote corners and humble towns all know to devote themselves to a single Classic and exert themselves to seek a place among the ranks at the imperial center…

title: 正德八年福建鄉試錄
text:
其勢則然矣閩文獻大藩也
有不日趨於盛哉且文章變
化要亦山川者爲之昔司馬
子長踪跡半天下其後始大
肆於篇章柳子厚得西山之
勝至自謂與萬化冥合閩東
南際大海渺漫數千里不可
===
涯涘延建上下奔流激湍使
人錯愕不能自已至若武夷
之環勝壺公之峭碧旣蜿蜒
委伏若拱若揖而石鼓峨嵋
諸峯亦復嶙峋高聳上插霄
漢士生其間必將有鍾焉顧
駭聞異觀坐致几席又豈無
punctuated: 其勢則然矣。閩，文獻大藩也，有不日趨於盛哉？且文章變化，要亦山川者爲之。昔司馬子長踪跡半天下，其後始大肆於篇章；柳子厚得西山之勝，至自謂與萬化冥合。閩東南際大海，渺漫數千里，不可涯涘；延建上下，奔流激湍，使人錯愕不能自已。至若武夷之環勝、壺公之峭碧，旣蜿蜒委伏，若拱若揖，而石鼓、峨嵋諸峯，亦復嶙峋高聳，上插霄漢。士生其間，必將有鍾焉。顧駭聞異觀，坐致几席，又豈無
translation_en: …Such, indeed, is the natural course of things. Fujian is a great province rich in literary heritage and learned worthies: how could it fail to flourish increasingly each day? Moreover, the transformations of literary writing owe much to mountains and rivers. In former times, Sima Zichang traveled over half the realm before giving full rein to his powers in writing. Liu Zihou encountered the splendid scenery of the Western Hills and went so far as to say that he had become mysteriously united with the myriad transformations of nature. Fujian borders the great sea to the southeast, its waters stretching for thousands of li, with no discernible limit. Throughout Yanping and Jianning, rushing currents and surging rapids leave people astonished and unable to contain themselves. Then there are the encircling splendors of Mount Wuyi and the steep, verdant heights of Mount Hugong, winding and bending low, as though clasping their hands and bowing in salutation. The peaks of Shigu and Emei likewise rise high and rugged, piercing the heavens above. Scholars born among them must surely receive something of their concentrated potency. With such astonishing sounds and extraordinary sights coming to them as they sit at their desks, could there fail to be those who…

title: 正德八年福建鄉試錄
text:
得之以為胸中浩博瑰詭之
奇而於筆下焉發之者哉況
夫江左貴清綺之詞河朔重
剛正之體文之成乎其習者
皆是也閩故多名賢大儒今
其講道之地遺踪相望學者
登其堂入其室覽遺編而考
===
其故焉則升降揖遜之容若
將見之而性命道德之旨猶
恍然有以自悟閩之學以義
理勝者豈一朝之故哉然則
今日之選固宜隨取隨獲有
足饜主司之求者矣雖然科
目本以取士而不能不假士
punctuated: 得之以為胸中浩博瑰詭之奇，而於筆下焉發之者哉？況夫江左貴清綺之詞，河朔重剛正之體，文之成乎其習者皆是也。閩故多名賢大儒，今其講道之地，遺踪相望。學者登其堂，入其室，覽遺編而考其故焉，則升降揖遜之容，若將見之；而性命道德之旨，猶恍然有以自悟。閩之學以義理勝者，豈一朝之故哉？然則今日之選，固宜隨取隨獲，有足饜主司之求者矣。雖然，科目本以取士，而不能不假士
translation_en: …those who absorb these sights as vast, magnificent, and wondrous conceptions within their minds, and give them expression through their brushes? Moreover, Jiangzuo prizes lucid and ornate language, while Heshuo values a firm and upright style: both exemplify how writing is shaped by local practice. Min has long abounded in renowned worthies and great Confucian scholars. Even now, the surviving traces of the places where they expounded the Way stand within sight of one another. When students ascend their halls, enter their chambers, read their surviving writings, and investigate their legacy, they seem almost to see before them the masters’ bearing as they ascended and descended, bowed and yielded precedence. They may still attain a sudden understanding for themselves of the purport of human nature and destiny, the Way and virtue. Could the preeminence of moral principle in the learning of Min have arisen in a single day? Thus, in the selection made today, surely each attempt to find talent should yield it, providing men fully able to satisfy the examiners’ expectations. Nevertheless, although the examination system was originally established to select scholars, it cannot but depend upon scholars …

title: 正德八年福建鄉試錄
text:
為重一代之科目得數人以
顯必其所謂賢者也一榜之
人物得一人以顯必其所謂
尤賢者也唐科目凡幾舉其
稱為龍虎榜者為最盛而歐
陽詹預焉宋科目凡幾舉其
以狀元甲科起而稱名宰相
===
者亦最盛而梁文靖公克家
預焉此所謂得數人以顯者
也歐與梁皆閩產也紹興十
八年榜此文公朱夫子所嘗
登名焉者榜中之眾不必皆
文公也世有慕於文公今其
錄獨傳而三百三十人者其
punctuated: 為重。一代之科目，得數人以顯，必其所謂賢者也；一榜之人物，得一人以顯，必其所謂尤賢者也。唐科目凡幾舉，其稱為龍虎榜者為最盛，而歐陽詹預焉。宋科目凡幾舉，其以狀元甲科起而稱名宰相者亦最盛，而梁文靖公克家預焉。此所謂得數人以顯者也。歐與梁皆閩產也。紹興十八年榜，此文公朱夫子所嘗登名焉者。榜中之眾，不必皆文公也。世有慕於文公，今其錄獨傳，而三百三十人者，其
translation_en: …for its prestige. When the examination system of an entire dynasty gains distinction through a few men, they must be men regarded as worthy; when the men on a single examination list gain distinction through one man, he must be regarded as exceptionally worthy. How many examinations were held under the Tang? The one known as the “Dragon and Tiger List” was the most illustrious, and Ouyang Zhan was among those listed. How many examinations were held under the Song? Those whose top-place or first-class examination success launched them toward renown as grand councilors were likewise the most illustrious, and Liang Kejia, posthumously titled Wenjing, was among them. This is what is meant by gaining distinction through a few men. Ouyang and Liang were both natives of Fujian. The list for the eighteenth year of Shaoxing [1148] was one on which Master Zhu [Zhu Xi], posthumously titled Wengong, had his name entered. The many men on that list need not all have been the equals of Wengong. Because people admire Wengong, its examination record alone survives today, and as for those three hundred and thirty men, their…

title: 正德八年福建鄉試錄
text:
姓名皆籍是以自見此所謂
得一人以顯者也文公亦閩
產也夫閩諸先正之係於科
目其重於天下如此况一鄉
乎其重於後世又如此况當
時乎諸士子固皆閩之俊也
其亦有篤前脩之仰昂焉自
===
奮以爲是科之光者乎夫自
諸先正求之其切深者文也
最隆焉者慈孝也靖深者器
局也盡心謀國者忠也洋洋
乎布滿天下者著述也泝伊
洛以接洙泗者道與德也爲
彼爲此具可師法而其所以
punctuated:
姓名皆籍是以自見，此所謂得一人以顯者也。文公亦閩產也。夫閩諸先正之係於科目，其重於天下如此，况一鄉乎？其重於後世又如此，况當時乎？諸士子固皆閩之俊也，其亦有篤前脩之仰、昂焉自奮以爲是科之光者乎？

夫自諸先正求之，其切深者文也，最隆焉者慈孝也，靖深者器局也，盡心謀國者忠也，洋洋乎布滿天下者著述也，泝伊洛以接洙泗者道與德也。爲彼爲此，具可師法，而其所以
translation_en:
…their names all depend upon this record to become known. This is what is meant by gaining distinction through a single person. Master Wengong [Zhu Xi] was also a native of Fujian. Such is the importance, throughout the realm, of Fujian’s earlier worthies in connection with the examinations—how much greater within their own province! Such, too, is their importance to later generations—how much greater in their own time! These candidates are certainly all outstanding men of Fujian. Might there also be among them those who deepen their reverence for earlier worthies and, with spirits raised [?], rouse themselves to bring glory to this examination?

If we look to those earlier worthies, what is earnest and profound is their literary expression; what is most exalted is their parental kindness and filial devotion; what is composed and deep is their character and capacity; what makes them devote themselves wholeheartedly to planning for the state is their loyalty; what spreads abundantly throughout the realm is their scholarly writing; and what traces the Yi and Luo traditions upstream to connect with those of the Zhu and Si is their Way and virtue. In all these pursuits, they may be taken as teachers and models; and the reason they…

title: 正德八年福建鄉試錄
text:
爲重者固不外是是在諸士
子勉之而已矣
湖廣荆州府荆門州儒學學
正魏尋謹序
punctuated:
爲重者，固不外是。是在諸士子勉之而已矣。
湖廣荆州府荆門州儒學學正魏尋謹序。
translation_en:
…what makes them worthy of esteem indeed lies in nothing beyond these qualities. It remains only for you examination candidates to strive to cultivate them.
Preface respectfully composed by Wei Xun, Instructor at the Confucian School of Jingmen Subprefecture, Jingzhou Prefecture, Huguang.

title: 正德八年福建鄉試錄
text:
正德八年福建鄉試
監臨官
巡按福建監察御史李如圭〔國寶湖廣澧州人己未進士〕
提調官
福建等處承宣布政使司左布政使陳珂〔希白浙江杭州前衞人庚戌進士〕
福建等處承宣布政使司右叅政孫燧〔德成浙江餘姚縣人癸丑進士〕
監試官
福建等處提刑按察司按察使劉遜〔時讓江西安福縣人戊戌進士〕
福建等處提刑按察司僉事胡鐸〔時振浙江餘姚縣人乙丑進士〕
===
考試官
湖廣荆州府荆門州儒學學正魏昂〔廷瞻廣西桂林中衞人庚午貢士〕
直隸淮安府邳州宿遷縣儒學教諭沈璋〔文瑞浙江錢塘縣人辛酉貢士〕
同考試官
直隸真定府定州儒學學正陳則〔德卿廣東番禺縣人辛酉貢士〕
直隸常州府江陰縣儒學教諭羅榦〔定本江西永豐縣人辛酉貢士〕
湖廣辰州府沅州黔陽縣儒學教諭尹孔常〔良臣江西安福縣人丁卯貢士〕
直隸常州府武進縣儒學教諭方一德〔克純廣東東莞縣人丁卯貢士〕
直隸鎮江府丹陽縣儒學訓導劉文詔〔廷綸江西安福縣人庚午貢士〕
punctuated:
正德八年福建鄉試。

監臨官：
巡按福建監察御史李如圭〔國寶，湖廣澧州人，己未進士〕。

提調官：
福建等處承宣布政使司左布政使陳珂〔希白，浙江杭州前衞人，庚戌進士〕。
福建等處承宣布政使司右叅政孫燧〔德成，浙江餘姚縣人，癸丑進士〕。

監試官：
福建等處提刑按察司按察使劉遜〔時讓，江西安福縣人，戊戌進士〕。
福建等處提刑按察司僉事胡鐸〔時振，浙江餘姚縣人，乙丑進士〕。

title: 正德八年福建鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
赫兮咺兮者威儀也
多聞擇其善者而從之多見而識之
仁之實事親是也義之實從兄是也智
之實知斯二者弗去是也禮之實節
文斯二者是也樂之實樂斯二者樂
則生矣生則惡可已也惡可已則不
知足之蹈之手之舞之
===
易
貞者事之幹也
君子之光有孚吉
仁者見之謂之仁知者見之謂之知
夫易聖人之所以極深而研幾也唯深
也故能通天下之志唯幾也故能成
天下之務唯神也故不疾而速不行
而至子曰易有聖人之道四焉者此
之謂也
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

赫兮咺兮者，威儀也。

多聞，擇其善者而從之；多見而識之。

仁之實，事親是也；義之實，從兄是也；智之實，知斯二者弗去是也；禮之實，節文斯二者是也；樂之實，樂斯二者。樂則生矣，生則惡可已也？惡可已，則不知足之蹈之、手之舞之。

易

貞者，事之幹也。

君子之光，有孚，吉。

仁者見之謂之仁，知者見之謂之知。

夫易，聖人之所以極深而研幾也。唯深也，故能通天下之志；唯幾也，故能成天下之務；唯神也，故不疾而速，不行而至。子曰：「易有聖人之道四焉」者，此之謂也。
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

“Splendid and illustrious” refers to awe-inspiring dignity and deportment.

Hear much, select what is good, and follow it; see much and retain it in memory.

The substance of benevolence is serving one’s parents; the substance of righteousness is following one’s elder brothers. The substance of wisdom is understanding these two things and never departing from them. The substance of ritual propriety is regulating and embellishing these two things. The substance of music is taking joy in these two things. When there is joy, it grows; once it grows, how can it be stopped? When it cannot be stopped, one’s feet unwittingly begin to stamp and one’s hands to dance.

Book of Changes (Yi)

Constancy is the mainstay of affairs.

The noble man’s radiance: there is sincerity; good fortune.

The benevolent see it and call it benevolence; the wise see it and call it wisdom.

The Changes is the means by which the sages fathom the depths and investigate the incipient signs of change. Because it is profound, it can comprehend the aspirations of all under Heaven; because it attends to incipient signs, it can bring the affairs of all under Heaven to completion; because it is numinous, it is swift without haste and arrives without traveling. When the Master said, “The Changes contains four aspects of the Way of the sages,” this is what he meant.

于大別南入于江
凡厥庶民有猷有爲有守汝則念之不
協于極不罹于咎皇則受之而康而
色曰予攸好德汝則錫之福時人斯

民

瓊華乎而俟我於庭乎而充耳以青
乎而尚之以瓊瑩乎而俟我於堂乎
而充耳以黃乎而尚之以瓊英乎而

書

東流爲漢，又東爲滄浪之水，過三澨，至于大別，南入于江。
凡厥庶民，有猷、有爲、有守，汝則念之；不協于極，不罹于咎，皇則受之。而康而色，曰：「予攸好德。」汝則錫之福。時人斯其惟皇之極。
三后協心，同底于道。道洽政治，澤潤生民。

詩
俟我於著乎而，充耳以素乎而，尚之以瓊華乎而！俟我於庭乎而，充耳以青乎而，尚之以瓊瑩乎而！俟我於堂乎而，充耳以黃乎而，尚之以瓊英乎而！
民之質矣，日用飲食。
實方實苞，實種實褎，實發實秀，實堅實好，實穎實栗。
translation_en:
Book of Documents

The music master is to receive words of counsel and proclaim them at the proper time.

Flowing east, it becomes the Han; farther east, it becomes the waters of Canglang. Passing Sanshi, it reaches Dabie, then flows south into the Jiang.

Among all the common people, those who have plans, accomplishments, or principles they uphold—you should keep them in mind. Those who do not conform to the supreme standard, yet have incurred no guilt, the sovereign should receive. Make your countenance gracious and say, “What I prize is virtue.” You should then bestow blessings upon them. These people will thus turn to the sovereign’s supreme standard.

The three sovereigns united their hearts and together attained the Way. The Way spread everywhere and government was well ordered; their beneficence nourished the people.

Book of Odes

He awaits me by the entrance screen! His ear pendants are strung with white silk, adorned above with splendid jade! He awaits me in the courtyard! His ear pendants are strung with blue silk, adorned above with lustrous jade! He awaits me in the hall! His ear pendants are strung with yellow silk, adorned above with lovely jade!

Such is the people’s basic nature: daily they eat and drink.

The grain fills out and swells, grows plump and tall, puts forth and flowers, becomes firm and fine, its ears hanging heavy, its kernels full.

title: 正德八年福建鄉試錄
text:
策五道
問帝王之治本乎道帝王之道載於經
近世之議經者有曰天人之極致學
者讀經必究乎此而後可帝王之求
治其亦然耶我
太祖高皇帝因論讀書而曰君道以事天愛
民爲重其本在敬身於乎大哉
王言乎爲治之要盡於是矣試與諸士子論
之不知
===
聖祖之所謂事與愛與敬者果統而言之耶
其亦有所指耶考之於經若曆象璣
衡之類皆觀天文而察時變者也事
天之道盡於是乎若肆赦不廢之屬
皆悲人窮而欲並生者也愛民之道
盡於是乎或曰事天如事親愛民如
子其然乎否也身之所關何者爲大
敬之所將何者爲宜如是而或有所
不得焉又將如之何帝王之處此其
punctuated:
策五道

問：帝王之治本乎道，帝王之道載於經。近世之議經者有曰：「天人之極致。」學者讀經，必究乎此而後可。帝王之求治，其亦然耶？我太祖高皇帝因論讀書而曰：「君道以事天愛民爲重，其本在敬身。」於乎，大哉，王言乎！爲治之要盡於是矣。試與諸士子論之。不知聖祖之所謂事與愛與敬者，果統而言之耶？其亦有所指耶？考之於經，若曆象璣衡之類，皆觀天文而察時變者也，事天之道盡於是乎？若肆赦不廢之屬，皆悲人窮而欲並生者也，愛民之道盡於是乎？或曰：「事天如事親，愛民如子。」其然乎？否也？身之所關，何者爲大？敬之所將，何者爲宜？如是而或有所不得焉，又將如之何？帝王之處此，其
translation_en:
Five policy questions

Question: The government of emperors and kings is rooted in the Way, and their Way is recorded in the Classics. Among recent commentators on the Classics, some have spoken of “the ultimate principles of Heaven and humanity.” Only after thoroughly investigating these may scholars be said to have read the Classics adequately. Is this also true of emperors and kings seeking good government? Our Emperor Taizu Gao, while discussing the reading of books, said: “The way of the ruler gives greatest weight to serving Heaven and loving the people; its foundation lies in reverence for one’s own person.” Ah, how great are these royal words! The essentials of government are fully contained in them. Let us discuss this with you candidates. We ask: when the sagely founder spoke of service, love, and reverence, was he speaking in general terms, or did he also have particular things in mind? Examining the Classics, we find such matters as calendrical observation and astronomical instruments, all concerned with observing celestial patterns and discerning changes in the seasons. Does this exhaust the way of serving Heaven? Such matters as granting pardons and not casting people aside [?] all express compassion for people in distress and a desire that all should live. Does this exhaust the way of loving the people? Some say: “Serve Heaven as you serve your parents, and love the people as your children.” Is this so, or is it not? Among the matters involving one’s own person, which are most important? In applying reverence, what is appropriate? If, despite proceeding thus, something remains unattained, what further course should be taken? As emperors and kings deal with these matters, might they …

title: 正德八年福建鄉試錄
text:
亦有道歟我
聖祖於天人之際深矣匪徒言之而又見之
躬行之實而又發以
聖見之眞藏之金匱者不可得而仰窺矣其
見于
宣宗章皇帝御製五倫書甚爲詳備而當時
儒臣之序
大明日曆則又一言以蔽之可考見已諸
士子必有得於莊誦之餘者其敬陳
===
之
問寇賊姦宄之患自古有之觀虞廷之
命臯陶雖聖世有不能免者顧吾所
以制之何如耳乃者各處地方寇賊
竊發至廑
宸慮命將出師以次削平嘗拜觀
勅諭有曰累年以來各處地方盜賊生發多
因水旱不時差科繁重及各該官司不能
撫恤大哉
punctuated:
亦有道歟？我聖祖於天人之際深矣，匪徒言之，而又見之躬行之實，而又發以聖見之眞。藏之金匱者，不可得而仰窺矣。其見于宣宗章皇帝御製《五倫書》，甚爲詳備；而當時儒臣之序《大明日曆》，則又一言以蔽之，可考見已。諸士子必有得於莊誦之餘者，其敬陳之。
問：寇賊姦宄之患，自古有之。觀虞廷之命臯陶，雖聖世有不能免者，顧吾所以制之何如耳。乃者，各處地方寇賊竊發，至廑宸慮，命將出師，以次削平。嘗拜觀勅諭，有曰：「累年以來，各處地方盜賊生發，多因水旱不時、差科繁重，及各該官司不能撫恤。」大哉，
translation_en:
…also have a way of dealing with this? Our sacred progenitor understood profoundly the relationship between Heaven and humankind. He did not merely speak of it, but embodied it in his own conduct and further elucidated it through the truth of his sagely insights. What is preserved in the golden coffer we cannot reverently inspect. What appears in the Book of the Five Human Relationships (Wulun shu), imperially composed by Emperor Xuanzong, posthumously styled Zhang, is exceptionally detailed and comprehensive. Yet the Confucian officials of that time, in their preface to the Daily Records of the Great Ming (Da Ming rili), summed it up in a single statement, which may be consulted. You candidates must have gained some understanding through your solemn recitation and subsequent reflection. Respectfully set it forth.
Question: The scourge of bandits and evildoers has existed since antiquity. Considering the charge given to Gao Yao at the court of Shun, we see that even a sagely age could not escape it; the issue is simply how we bring it under control. Recently, bandits rose up in various localities, causing His Majesty concern. He appointed generals and dispatched troops, suppressing them one after another. I have reverently read an imperial edict that states: “For years now, outbreaks of banditry in various localities have largely arisen from untimely floods and droughts, onerous labor services and tax levies, and the failure of the responsible authorities to provide care and relief.” How great…

title: 正德八年福建鄉試錄
text:
王言其得捄敝之源致治之本乎天下之事
固難槩論姑以閩中事與諸士子商
之夫水旱天之災也將欲捄之其道
何存差科民所供也將欲省之其要
何在考之昔仕於閩有知福清而闢
陂洫四十里者有令連江而築石堤
三百丈者有知福州而首開五塘者
有知漳州而開渠十四者可謂能備
水旱矣淳熙中有奏除無名之賦七
===
百萬者嘉定中有蠲逋負十數萬者
祥符中有奏止額外增稅者紹興中
有奏蠲一切苛政者可謂能省差科
矣此皆官司所當取法可歷指其人
以實之乎然水旱有備差科不擾固
弭盜之本源也但其間如汀漳二郡
介乎閩廣之地民性獷悍習於為盜
負固山海撲而復起茲欲使之悉安
耒耜之業而歸維新之化如之何則
punctuated: 王言！其得捄敝之源、致治之本乎？天下之事，固難槩論，姑以閩中事與諸士子商之。夫水旱，天之災也，將欲捄之，其道何存？差科，民所供也，將欲省之，其要何在？考之昔仕於閩，有知福清而闢陂洫四十里者，有令連江而築石堤三百丈者，有知福州而首開五塘者，有知漳州而開渠十四者，可謂能備水旱矣。淳熙中，有奏除無名之賦七百萬者；嘉定中，有蠲逋負十數萬者；祥符中，有奏止額外增稅者；紹興中，有奏蠲一切苛政者，可謂能省差科矣。此皆官司所當取法，可歷指其人以實之乎？然水旱有備，差科不擾，固弭盜之本源也。但其間，如汀、漳二郡，介乎閩、廣之地，民性獷悍，習於為盜，負固山海，撲而復起。茲欲使之悉安耒耜之業，而歸維新之化，如之何則
translation_en:
…these royal words! Do they not grasp the source of remedies for abuses and the foundation of good government? The affairs of the realm are indeed difficult to discuss in general terms. Let us therefore discuss matters in Fujian with you examination candidates. Floods and droughts are calamities sent by Heaven: if we wish to relieve them, wherein lies the way? Labor services and levies are supplied by the people: if we wish to reduce them, wherein lies the key?

Examining the records of those who formerly served in Fujian, we find one who, as Magistrate of Fuqing, opened forty li of reservoirs and irrigation ditches; one who, as Magistrate of Lianjiang, built a stone embankment three hundred zhang long; one who, as Prefect of Fuzhou, first opened five ponds; and one who, as Prefect of Zhangzhou, opened fourteen channels. They may be said to have made effective provision against floods and droughts. During the Chunxi era, one official memorialized to abolish unauthorized levies amounting to seven million; during the Jiading era, another remitted arrears amounting to over a hundred thousand; during the Xiangfu era, another memorialized to halt additional taxation beyond the established quota; and during the Shaoxing era, another memorialized to abolish all oppressive measures. They may be said to have effectively reduced labor services and levies. These are all examples that officials ought to follow. Can you identify each of these men to substantiate the accounts?

Now, preparedness against floods and droughts, and freedom from the harassment of labor services and levies, are indeed the foundations for suppressing banditry. Yet within this region, the two prefectures of Tingzhou and Zhangzhou, for example, lie between Fujian and Guangdong. Their people are fierce and unruly by disposition and accustomed to banditry. Relying on the natural defenses of mountains and sea, they rise again after being put down. If we now wish to have them all settle contentedly into the work of tilling the fields and submit to the transforming influence of renewed rule, by what means could…

title: 正德八年福建鄉試錄
text:
可宜詳著于篇將采而行之用副
德意於萬一焉
問學道者以聖人爲標的其工夫次第
先儒悉之矣姑摭一二疑義相與商
之夫脩道以仁求仁在恕仁之說多
端恕之義兩用恕何關於仁耶旣曰
有主則虛又曰有主則實無乃自相
戾耶務博則疑於玩物喪志主靜則
近於無所用心滯近小則局而不舒
===
騖高遠則虛而無實做題入議旣謂
之有識用意作文胡爲而害道協一
本非易事何以曰分殊爲難物理固
非度外何以曰事功爲害性命夫子
罕言也彼謂性非所急者可盡非耶
禮文不相沿襲也彼以禮敎爲先者
非固滯耶顏子稱聖人之敎曰博約
博則爲文學約則爲德行而顏子獨
以德行稱豈其學與後世異耶諸士
punctuated:
可？宜詳著于篇，將采而行之，用副德意於萬一焉。

問：學道者以聖人爲標的，其工夫次第，先儒悉之矣。姑摭一二疑義，相與商之。夫脩道以仁，求仁在恕。仁之說多端，恕之義兩用，恕何關於仁耶？旣曰「有主則虛」，又曰「有主則實」，無乃自相戾耶？務博則疑於玩物喪志，主靜則近於無所用心；滯近小則局而不舒，騖高遠則虛而無實。做題入議，旣謂之有識；用意作文，胡爲而害道？協一本非易事，何以曰分殊爲難？物理固非度外，何以曰事功爲害？性命，夫子罕言也，彼謂性非所急者，可盡非耶？禮文不相沿襲也，彼以禮敎爲先者，非固滯耶？顏子稱聖人之敎曰博約，博則爲文學，約則爲德行，而顏子獨以德行稱，豈其學與後世異耶？諸士
translation_en:
…would be appropriate? Set out your proposals in detail in your essay. We shall adopt and implement them, thereby fulfilling even a ten-thousandth part of the imperial benevolent intent.

Question: Those who study the Way take the sage as their standard. Earlier Confucian scholars have fully explained the successive stages of their efforts. Let us select one or two doubtful points and discuss them together. Cultivating the Way rests on benevolence, and seeking benevolence depends on reciprocity. There are many explanations of benevolence, and the meaning of reciprocity has two applications. How, then, is reciprocity connected with benevolence? It is said both that “with a governing principle, the mind is empty” and that “with a governing principle, the mind is full.” Are these statements not mutually contradictory? Pursuing breadth of learning seems liable to become absorption in things that saps one’s resolve, while emphasizing stillness comes close to leaving the mind unoccupied. Remaining confined to what is near and small constricts one without allowing scope for development; pursuing what is lofty and remote leads to emptiness without substance. Addressing a topic and entering into argument [?] is said to show discernment; why, then, should deliberate effort in literary composition harm the Way? Bringing things into unity is inherently no easy matter; why is it said that discerning their differentiated particulars is difficult? The principles of things are certainly not outside the scope of our concern; why, then, is practical achievement said to be harmful? The Master seldom spoke of human nature and Heaven’s decree. Can those who say that human nature is not an urgent concern be condemned entirely? The forms of ritual have not been transmitted unchanged from one age to the next. Are those who give priority to ritual teaching not rigidly attached to the past? Master Yan described the sage’s teaching in terms of breadth and restraint: breadth pertains to literary learning, restraint to virtuous conduct. Yet Master Yan was renowned specifically for virtuous conduct. Could his learning have differed from that of later generations? You scholars…

title: 正德八年福建鄉試錄
text:
子希顏入聖必講之熟矣願明以告
我
問田有定分賦有定法此仁政之大者
夏商以前姑未暇論若成周徹法旣
已變商七十爲百畝矣及攷遂人與
漢志所載乃有百畝至三百畝者而
又受歸無常可謂有定分耶太宰旣
有九職又有九賦或謂賦爲口率出
錢似又過什一矣可謂有定法耶迨
===
井田法壞論者謂莫善於租庸調莫
不善於兩稅蓋一以丁夫爲本一以
資產爲宗以丁夫爲本則貧富不分
以資產爲宗則真僞難辨而必謂彼
善於此者何故其所以善所以不善
所以不得不變必有說也
國朝稽古致治田有步筭而戶籍定賦有
常額而稅斂薄宜乎民物阜豐矣然
治久弊滋日以彌甚居下恒苦於兼
punctuated:
子希顏入聖，必講之熟矣，願明以告我。
問：田有定分，賦有定法，此仁政之大者。夏商以前，姑未暇論。若成周徹法，旣已變商七十爲百畝矣。及攷遂人與漢志所載，乃有百畝至三百畝者，而又受歸無常，可謂有定分耶？太宰旣有九職，又有九賦，或謂賦爲口率出錢，似又過什一矣，可謂有定法耶？迨井田法壞，論者謂莫善於租庸調，莫不善於兩稅。蓋一以丁夫爲本，一以資產爲宗。以丁夫爲本，則貧富不分；以資產爲宗，則真僞難辨。而必謂彼善於此者，何故？其所以善，所以不善，所以不得不變，必有說也。
國朝稽古致治，田有步筭而戶籍定，賦有常額而稅斂薄，宜乎民物阜豐矣。然治久弊滋，日以彌甚，居下恒苦於兼
translation_en:
…you scholars aspire to emulate Yan Hui and attain sagehood; surely you have studied these matters thoroughly. I ask you to explain them clearly to me.
Question: Land has fixed allotments, and taxation has fixed rules: these are major elements of humane government. Let us for the moment leave aside the Xia and Shang and earlier times. Under the che system of the Zhou, the Shang allotment of seventy mu had already been changed to one hundred mu. Yet, on examining the account of the Director of Rural Administration and the treatise in the History of the Han, we find allotments ranging from one hundred to three hundred mu, with no fixed practice for receiving and returning land. Can this be called a system of fixed allotments? The Grand Steward had both the nine occupations and the nine levies. Some say that these levies were monetary payments assessed per person; this would seem to exceed the tithe. Can this be called a system of fixed taxation rules?
After the well-field system broke down, commentators maintained that no system was better than the grain tax, labor-service commutation, and textile levy (zu-yong-diao), and none worse than the Double Tax system. The former took adult males as its basis, while the latter took assets as its guiding principle. Basing taxation on adult males fails to distinguish rich from poor; basing it on assets makes it difficult to distinguish truthful from false declarations. Why, then, must they insist that the former was better than the latter? There must be an explanation of what made one good and the other bad, and why change became unavoidable.
Our dynasty has consulted antiquity in establishing good government. Land is measured in paces and calculated, and household registration is settled; taxation has regular quotas, and tax exactions are light. The people and their resources ought therefore to flourish in abundance. Yet, as orderly rule has endured, abuses have multiplied, growing worse by the day. Those below constantly suffer from the engrossment of land…

title: 正德八年福建鄉試錄
text:
併供上每困於征求昔之患此者嘗
請行經界而竟拂羣議又有上政本
書而終不見用不知二者可行於今
否也苟難卒行則處之者終無術乎
諸士子其酌古準今以對
問守令親民之職自秦廢封建始置郡
縣而有之由漢而下代或更置殊其
名稱其倚之以成治則一也考之於
史有曰六條有曰八計有曰四事皆
===
所以稽吏治者而行之久近責之專
否亦或不同可歷舉其詳歟三代以
後言治者必曰漢唐宋至言守令之
賢又未嘗不以漢之循吏爲稱首漢
獨何以致此我
朝稽古建官愼擇守令而責成之以六事
又每歲各
命憲臣一員以巡察之又通計其舉否以爲
黜陟惠民之意至矣不知所謂六事
punctuated:
併，供上每困於征求。昔之患此者，嘗請行經界而竟拂羣議，又有上政本書而終不見用。不知二者可行於今否也？苟難卒行，則處之者終無術乎？諸士子其酌古準今以對。
問：守令親民之職，自秦廢封建、始置郡縣而有之。由漢而下，代或更置，殊其名稱，其倚之以成治則一也。考之於史，有曰六條，有曰八計，有曰四事，皆所以稽吏治者，而行之久近、責之專否，亦或不同。可歷舉其詳歟？三代以後，言治者必曰漢、唐、宋。至言守令之賢，又未嘗不以漢之循吏爲稱首。漢獨何以致此？我朝稽古建官，愼擇守令，而責成之以六事。又每歲各命憲臣一員以巡察之，又通計其舉否以爲黜陟，惠民之意至矣。不知所謂六事
translation_en:
…land engrossment, while providing for the authorities is repeatedly made difficult by their exactions. Those who formerly worried about this once requested a survey and demarcation of landholdings, but it ultimately ran counter to the prevailing views. Another submitted a writing on the foundations of government, but it was never adopted. Could these two proposals be implemented today? If they are difficult to implement immediately, must those addressing the problem remain without any means of doing so? You candidates should weigh ancient practice against present circumstances in your replies.
Question: The offices of prefect and county magistrate, which bring officials into close contact with the people, originated when Qin abolished feudal enfeoffment and first established commanderies and counties. From Han onward, successive dynasties sometimes altered these offices and gave them different names, but their reliance on them to achieve good government was the same. Examining the histories, we find references to the Six Articles, the Eight Assessments, and the Four Matters. All were means of evaluating officials’ administration, yet how long they remained in force and whether responsibility was assigned exclusively also differed. Can you enumerate their particulars? When discussing good government after the Three Dynasties, people invariably cite Han, Tang, and Song. When discussing worthy prefects and county magistrates, moreover, they invariably rank Han’s exemplary officials first. How did Han, in particular, achieve this? Our dynasty has consulted antiquity in establishing offices, carefully selected prefects and county magistrates, and held them accountable for results under six matters. Each year it also commissions a censor to conduct inspection tours in each jurisdiction, and comprehensively assesses the officials’ merits and failings as the basis for dismissal or promotion. Its intention to benefit the people is most earnest. As for what are called the six matters, we wonder…

title: 正德八年福建鄉試錄
text:
者與漢唐宋之法亦有同歟我
朝立法之善宜非前代所能及者而近年
以來吏或未能盡稱其職民或未能
盡安其業其故何歟今欲使天下之
守令皆無愧於漢之循吏而田里亦
無不安之民何如而可願悉陳之毋
隱
punctuated: 者，與漢唐宋之法亦有同歟？我朝立法之善，宜非前代所能及者，而近年以來，吏或未能盡稱其職，民或未能盡安其業，其故何歟？今欲使天下之守令皆無愧於漢之循吏，而田里亦無不安之民，何如而可？願悉陳之，毋隱。
translation_en: …whether these also have anything in common with the methods of the Han, Tang, and Song? The excellence of our dynasty’s laws should surely surpass anything previous dynasties could achieve. Yet in recent years, some officials have failed to discharge their duties fully, and some among the people have been unable to pursue their livelihoods in peace. Why is this? If we now wish to ensure that every prefect and magistrate in the realm bears comparison with the conscientious officials of the Han, and that no one in the countryside lives without peace and security, how can this be accomplished? Please set out your views fully, concealing nothing.
