This is what Master Zhu meant by saying, “The finer and more meticulous, the broader and greater.” When one expands the capacity of the mind’s substance, ultimate principle is fully present in what is lofty and remote. Why worry that it will lack substance? This is what Master Cheng meant by saying, “Utterly still and without a trace, yet the myriad phenomena are all arrayed within it.”

Principle is dispersed among the myriad differentiated things, and its most hidden manifestations are ghosts and spirits. If one does not reflect upon what is hidden, one will ultimately gain nothing within oneself; if one does not scrutinize differences, specious resemblances will be able to confound the true. This is why “composing the topic and entering into discussion” involves discernment [?], and why distinguishing differences is difficult.

Literary accomplishment is a minor concern for the gentleman; practical achievement is a secondary outgrowth of the Way and virtue. To confine oneself to literary accomplishment narrows the substance of the mind and separates it from Heaven and Earth. To calculate practical achievements allows the selfish pursuit of external things to prevail, leading to the same destination as Guan Zhong and Shang Yang. This is why worldly writing harms the Way, and why the learning of Yongkang is harmful.

Although human nature was something of which Confucius rarely spoke, the refined and the coarse, the root and the branches, have never involved two different principles. When Yongshu said that human nature was not what the sage taught people first, his intention was that people should first learn through ordinary matters and should not hastily speak of reaching higher understanding. Yet the wording…

title: 正德八年福建鄉試錄
text:
意之間似分性與事爲二物此程子所
以譏其誤也禮雖古今不相襲而正容
謹節所宜先務故子厚以禮爲教其意
欲使學者先有據守則可以變化氣質
而關中躬行之多遂與洛中並此程子
所以稱其善也是則察近小也辨萬殊
也究鬼神也審性命也皆博文之屬也
致高遠也謹禮節也強恕也存心也皆
約禮之屬也而要其所歸則不越乎明
諸心以全其仁而已矣彼文藝事功之
瑣瑣者何足言哉抑愚又有說焉孔門
言仁雖多然如四勿二如之類皆不出
乎敬之一字蓋自程子發明之後世之
三尺之童類能言之然不過勦儒先之
常談布諸語言文字之間而於體驗服
行之功漫不加意至或以擎拳曲跽端
坐拱默爲敬而聖人之旨闇而弗明宜
乎博者失之雜而約者失之陋也愚生
punctuated:
意之間，似分性與事爲二物，此程子所以譏其誤也。禮雖古今不相襲，而正容謹節所宜先務，故子厚以禮爲教，其意欲使學者先有據守，則可以變化氣質，而關中躬行之多遂與洛中並，此程子所以稱其善也。是則察近小也，辨萬殊也，究鬼神也，審性命也，皆博文之屬也；致高遠也，謹禮節也，強恕也，存心也，皆約禮之屬也。而要其所歸，則不越乎明諸心以全其仁而已矣。彼文藝事功之瑣瑣者，何足言哉！

抑愚又有說焉。孔門言仁雖多，然如四勿、二如之類，皆不出乎敬之一字。蓋自程子發明之後，世之三尺之童類能言之，然不過勦儒先之常談，布諸語言文字之間，而於體驗服行之功漫不加意。至或以擎拳曲跽、端坐拱默爲敬，而聖人之旨闇而弗明。宜乎博者失之雜，而約者失之陋也。愚生
translation_en:
…in the purport of his words, he seems to divide human nature and practical affairs into two separate things. This is why Master Cheng criticized his error. Although ritual does not remain unchanged from antiquity to the present, maintaining a proper bearing and carefully observing its forms ought to take priority. Thus Zihou made ritual the basis of his teaching. His intention was that learners should first have something to rely upon and hold fast to, enabling them to transform their temperamental endowment. Consequently, Guanzhong came to rival Luozhong in the number of those who personally put the teachings into practice. This is why Master Cheng praised the excellence of his approach. Thus, examining what is near and small, distinguishing the myriad differences among things, investigating ghosts and spirits, and scrutinizing human nature and destiny all belong to broadening learning through culture. Attaining what is lofty and far-reaching, carefully observing ritual forms, exerting oneself in reciprocity, and preserving the mind all belong to disciplining oneself through ritual. Their ultimate aim amounts to no more than making these principles clear within the mind so as to bring one’s humaneness to fulfillment. How could those petty matters of literary accomplishment and practical achievement merit discussion!

Yet I, in my ignorance, have something further to say. Although the school of Confucius spoke extensively of humaneness, teachings such as the four injunctions beginning “Do not” and the two comparisons beginning “as if” all fall within the single word “reverence.” Since Master Cheng elucidated it, even little children scarcely three feet tall have generally been able to speak of it. Yet people merely borrow the familiar sayings of earlier Confucian scholars and spread them through speech and writing, paying no attention to the work of personally experiencing and putting them into practice. Some even regard holding up clasped hands, kneeling with bent limbs, or sitting upright with folded hands in silence as reverence, leaving the sage’s meaning obscure and unilluminated. Little wonder that those who pursue breadth err through indiscriminate accumulation, while those who pursue restraint err through narrowness. I, this humble scholar, …

title: 正德八年福建鄉試錄
text:
服敬恕之教遵博約之方亦竊有志而
未能者惟執事進而教之幸甚
第四問
葉奇
同考試官教諭方批場中論田賦者率無定
見此策援據該洽鑿鑿可施讀之如探武庫之積鋩錚疊見
而芒寒眩目殆博古而有用者歟
考試官教諭沈批考據精詳敷叙明暢作此策
者鮮見其儷末後發出都里量耗一節尤切時弊盖嘗究心
===
於當世之務者矣
考試官學正魏批田賦一策作者非迂則陋此篇敷
叙顛委明悉筆勢滔滔畧無礙滯參之前場俱優高薦何忝
論治法而欲得其詳當求乎古行治法
而欲宜於俗當酌乎今不求乎古無以
知其原不酌乎今無以通其變田賦者
致治之大法也田以給野人患在於兼
併賦以養君子患在於多取此古今之
通弊而行仁政者所宜先務也請因明
punctuated:
服敬恕之教，遵博約之方，亦竊有志而未能者。惟執事進而教之，幸甚。

第四問
葉奇

同考試官教諭方批：場中論田賦者，率無定見。此策援據該洽，鑿鑿可施。讀之如探武庫之積，鋩錚疊見，而芒寒眩目，殆博古而有用者歟！

考試官教諭沈批：考據精詳，敷叙明暢，作此策者鮮見其儷。末後發出都里量耗一節，尤切時弊，盖嘗究心於當世之務者矣。

考試官學正魏批：田賦一策，作者非迂則陋。此篇敷叙顛委明悉，筆勢滔滔，畧無礙滯。參之前場，俱優，高薦何忝！

論治法而欲得其詳，當求乎古；行治法而欲宜於俗，當酌乎今。不求乎古，無以知其原；不酌乎今，無以通其變。田賦者，致治之大法也。田以給野人，患在於兼併；賦以養君子，患在於多取。此古今之通弊，而行仁政者所宜先務也。請因明
translation_en:
…I embrace the teaching of reverence and reciprocity and follow the method of broad learning and disciplined restraint. These, too, are aspirations I privately cherish but have not yet realized. I would be most fortunate if you would lead me forward and instruct me.

Fourth Question
Ye Qi

Comment by Associate Examiner Fang, Instructor: Most candidates discussing land and taxation in this examination lack settled views. This policy essay draws comprehensively on relevant authorities and offers definite, practicable proposals. Reading it is like exploring the stores of an arsenal: gleaming blades appear one after another [?], their cold brilliance dazzling the eyes. Surely this is learning that combines familiarity with antiquity and practical usefulness!

Comment by Examiner Shen, Instructor: The examination of sources is precise and detailed, and the exposition clear and fluent. Few can match the author of this policy essay. The concluding section on assessing wastage allowances at the du and li levels [?] is especially pertinent to present abuses. He must have devoted serious thought to the affairs of our age.

Comment by Examiner Wei, Instructor: In the policy essay on land and taxation, candidates are either impractical or ill-informed. This piece explains the subject clearly and fully from beginning to end; its prose flows onward without the slightest obstruction. Compared with his work in the preceding examination sessions, all are excellent. How could recommending him for a high place be undeserved?

To discuss methods of government and grasp their details, one must look to antiquity; to implement methods of government suitably for prevailing customs, one must weigh present circumstances. Without looking to antiquity, one cannot understand their origins; without weighing the present, one cannot adapt them to changing circumstances. Land and taxation are fundamental instruments of good government. Land provides for those who work in the fields; the danger lies in its concentration through annexation. Taxes support those who govern; the danger lies in excessive exaction. These are abuses common to past and present, and anyone practicing benevolent government should make addressing them a priority. Allow me, in response to your illuminating…

title: 正德八年福建鄉試錄
text:
問而條陳之古者盛時因民而制田因
田而定賦其予民也常厚而取民也常
薄蓋自禹作司空辨九等之田均什一
之稅而夏商因之及周人徹法雖變商
七十為百畝而其公田以禄君子私田
以給野人則常產之制同私田之入得
其九公田之入得其一則取民之法同
若遂人及漢志所載不同者以其田有
上中下之殊故所受有百畝至三百畝
===
之異民年二十受田六十歸田皆制於
上而不紊也何嘗無定分耶太宰之九
職所以任萬民而使各事其業九賦所
以歛財賄而使各輸其征賦之所歛即
職之所出而或以為口率出錢者妄也
何嘗無定法耶及井田之法既壞限田
之議不行漢晉以降無足言者唐因元
魏北齊之舊為租庸調之法有田則有
租有身則有庸有户則有調租則出粟
punctuated: 問而條陳之。古者盛時，因民而制田，因田而定賦，其予民也常厚，而取民也常薄。蓋自禹作司空，辨九等之田，均什一之稅，而夏商因之。及周人徹法，雖變商七十為百畝，而其公田以禄君子，私田以給野人，則常產之制同；私田之入得其九，公田之入得其一，則取民之法同。若遂人及漢志所載不同者，以其田有上中下之殊，故所受有百畝至三百畝之異。民年二十受田，六十歸田，皆制於上而不紊也，何嘗無定分耶？太宰之九職，所以任萬民而使各事其業；九賦，所以歛財賄而使各輸其征。賦之所歛，即職之所出，而或以為口率出錢者，妄也。何嘗無定法耶？及井田之法既壞，限田之議不行，漢晉以降，無足言者。唐因元魏北齊之舊，為租庸調之法，有田則有租，有身則有庸，有户則有調，租則出粟
translation_en:
…question and set out the particulars in order. In the flourishing ages of antiquity, land allotments were established according to the people, and taxes were fixed according to the land. What was given to the people was always generous, while what was taken from them was always slight. Beginning when Yu served as Minister of Works, fields were distinguished into nine grades and a uniform tithe was imposed; the Xia and Shang followed this practice. When the Zhou instituted the che system, although they changed the Shang allotment of seventy mu to one hundred mu, public fields still provided stipends for gentlemen and private fields supported the cultivators. Thus the system of providing a stable livelihood remained the same. The cultivators received the nine shares yielded by the private fields, while the ruler received the one share yielded by the public fields; thus the method of taking revenue from the people also remained the same. As for the discrepancies between the accounts in the “Director of Outlying Districts” section of the Rites of Zhou and the treatise in the History of the Han, these arose because fields differed in quality—superior, middling, or inferior—so allotments varied from one hundred to three hundred mu. People received land at twenty and returned it at sixty. All this was regulated by those above without disorder. How could there have been no fixed allotments?

The Grand Steward’s nine occupations were the means of assigning work to all the people and ensuring that each pursued an occupation; his nine levies were the means of collecting wealth and goods and ensuring that each paid the required dues. What the levies collected was precisely what the occupations produced. The claim made by some that money was exacted at a per capita rate is unfounded. How could there have been no fixed rules?

Once the well-field system had broken down and proposals to limit landholdings went unimplemented, there was nothing worth discussing from the Han and Jin onward. Following precedents from the Northern Wei and Northern Qi, the Tang established the system of grain tax, labor service or its commutation, and household levy (zu, yong, and diao). Land entailed grain tax, an individual entailed labor service, and a household entailed the household levy. For the grain tax, millet was delivered…

title: 正德八年福建鄉試錄
text:
穀庸調則綾紬絺布隨土所宜户無不
田之人人無不均之税陸贄所謂其取
法也遠其立意也深其斂財也均其成
人也固其裁規也簡其備患也周此其
法之所以善也惜乎官給之田任民自
賣其後兵革既起征斂煩重丁口轉死
田畝互易浮居倍於土着貧富已非其
舊而欲按籍征之誠有難者楊炎不能
斟酌調停疏滯整敝輕變祖宗之舊而
===
行兩税之法户無主客以見居為簿人
無丁中以貧富為差而又效筭緡之末
計折錢穀以定税陸贄所謂總暴賦以
立常規者此其法之所以不善也雖然
授田之法行則夫各有田而貧富不分
固宜以丁夫為本授田之法廢則有田
者寡而貧富懸殊不得不以資產為宗
是又不可執一論也然此皆叔世不經
之制無足深究至宋建炎之間林勳上
punctuated: 穀，庸調則綾紬絺布，隨土所宜。户無不田之人，人無不均之税。陸贄所謂「其取法也遠，其立意也深，其斂財也均，其成人也固，其裁規也簡，其備患也周」，此其法之所以善也。惜乎官給之田，任民自賣，其後兵革既起，征斂煩重，丁口轉死，田畝互易，浮居倍於土着，貧富已非其舊，而欲按籍征之，誠有難者。楊炎不能斟酌調停，疏滯整敝，輕變祖宗之舊，而行兩税之法。户無主客，以見居為簿；人無丁中，以貧富為差。而又效筭緡之末計，折錢穀以定税。陸贄所謂「總暴賦以立常規」者，此其法之所以不善也。雖然，授田之法行，則夫各有田，而貧富不分，固宜以丁夫為本；授田之法廢，則有田者寡，而貧富懸殊，不得不以資產為宗。是又不可執一論也。然此皆叔世不經之制，無足深究。至宋建炎之間，林勳上
translation_en: …grain, while the labor-service commutation and household levy were paid in figured silk, silk cloth, fine ramie, or other cloth, according to what the locality produced. No household had anyone without land to cultivate, and no person bore an inequitable tax. As Lu Zhi said, “Its precedents reach far back; its intentions are profound; its collection of revenue is equitable; its provision for the people is secure; its formulation of rules is simple; and its precautions against misfortune are comprehensive.” These were the merits of the system. Regrettably, people were allowed to sell the land granted them by the government. Later, warfare broke out, levies became burdensome, registered inhabitants wandered and died, and fields changed hands. The transient population grew to twice the settled population, and the distribution of wealth was no longer what it had been. To attempt to collect taxes according to the registers was indeed difficult. Yang Yan failed to weigh and adjust matters, clear obstructions, and remedy abuses. He rashly altered the ancestral system and implemented the Twice-Yearly Tax system. Households were registered according to their current residence, regardless of whether they were established residents or newcomers; individuals were assessed according to wealth, regardless of whether they were classified as fully adult or younger males. Moreover, he imitated the expedient of the tax on strings of cash, converting between cash and grain to determine assessments. This was what Lu Zhi called “combining oppressive levies to establish a permanent rule,” and it explains the defects of this system. Nevertheless, when land allotment was practiced, each adult man had land, and there was no division between rich and poor; it was certainly appropriate to base taxation on adult males. Once land allotment was abolished, few possessed land, and disparities of wealth were enormous; assets necessarily became the basis of taxation. Here, too, one cannot insist on a single principle. Yet these were all irregular institutions of a declining age, unworthy of close investigation. During the Jianyan reign period of the Song, Lin Xun submitted…

title: 正德八年福建鄉試錄
text:
政本書盖亦限田餘意而取民之制似
過於重及淳熙間朱子出判漳州請行
經界之法而沮於羣議竟柅不行洪惟
我
朝稽古致治戶各有籍必審上下之辨而
姦偽莫容田各有則必詳步筭之法而
差等不亂是可謂有定分矣因夫制役
而里甲之制十年更差非若庸調歲征
而有不役之絹也計產定賦而租穀之
===
入隨田多寡非若總計科率而以多者
為額也亦可謂有定法矣然近年以来
治久弊滋冊籍患於混淆而豪猾得以
售其奸征斂苦於無藝而吏胥得以恣
其虐誠有如執事所憂者茲欲講經界
之舊求政本之說以施諸用此在前賢
皆喜談之豈敢謂為不可獨恐弛張變
置之間戾乎人情土俗之宜昔人謂封
建廢而井田不可復者誠亦有見也外
punctuated:
《政本書》，盖亦限田餘意，而取民之制似過於重。及淳熙間，朱子出判漳州，請行經界之法，而沮於羣議，竟柅不行。洪惟我朝稽古致治，戶各有籍，必審上下之辨，而姦偽莫容；田各有則，必詳步筭之法，而差等不亂。是可謂有定分矣。因夫制役，而里甲之制十年更差，非若庸調歲征而有不役之絹也；計產定賦，而租穀之入隨田多寡，非若總計科率而以多者為額也。亦可謂有定法矣。

然近年以来，治久弊滋，冊籍患於混淆，而豪猾得以售其奸；征斂苦於無藝，而吏胥得以恣其虐。誠有如執事所憂者。茲欲講經界之舊，求政本之說，以施諸用，此在前賢皆喜談之，豈敢謂為不可？獨恐弛張變置之間，戾乎人情土俗之宜。昔人謂封建廢而井田不可復者，誠亦有見也。外
translation_en:
…the Book on the Foundations of Government (Zhengben shu). This, too, presumably carried forward the idea of limiting landholdings, but its provisions for levies upon the people seem excessively burdensome. During the Chunxi reign period, Master Zhu took office as prefect of Zhangzhou and requested the implementation of a system for surveying and demarcating fields. Opposition from many quarters obstructed it, however, and in the end it was halted and never implemented. We reverently reflect that our dynasty has drawn upon antiquity to achieve good government. Every household is registered: distinctions between higher and lower grades must be carefully examined, leaving no room for fraud. Every field has its prescribed assessment: the methods of measurement and calculation must be worked out in detail, so that the graded distinctions remain orderly. This may indeed be called a system of fixed apportionment. Labor service is assigned according to the adult males available, and under the lijia household organization, assignments rotate every ten years. This differs from the annual collection of labor-commutation and household taxes, which included silk paid in lieu of service. Taxes are fixed according to property, and grain-tax receipts vary with the amount of land held. This differs from apportioning levies on the basis of aggregate calculations and taking the larger amount as the quota. This, too, may be called a system of fixed rules.

In recent years, however, abuses have multiplied during a long period of settled rule. Registers have become confused, allowing powerful and unscrupulous people to perpetrate fraud; levies have become intolerably unrestrained, allowing clerks to indulge their cruelty. There are indeed problems such as those that concern you. You now wish to examine the old practices of field demarcation and seek out the arguments in the Foundations of Government, in order to put them into practice. These were matters that earlier worthies all delighted in discussing; how could I presume to say that they are inadmissible? My only fear is that, in relaxing or tightening arrangements and changing institutions, we may contravene what accords with people’s sentiments and local customs. Those of former times who said that, once feudal enfeoffment had been abolished, the well-field system could not be restored certainly had insight. Beyond…

title: 正德八年福建鄉試錄
text:
此而求善處之術亦必有說矣竊嘗反
復先王之故深繹後世之弊則亦不獨
患田畝之兼併而猶患鄙里之豐耗豐
者戶多則輕於輸稅耗者戶寡則苦於
取盈謂宜依倣均田稍爲之限而又酌
周人九兩繫民之法定立常制使分籍
貿田者皆不得出其鄉則戶里必均而
可以免財賦偏重之弊申明
舊章使征租督課者皆不得違其式則稅
===
斂不橫而可以紓赤子呻吟之憂庶於
苴漏補罅或一少助也若夫節用愛人
以爲致治之本更俟他日爲
聖天子獻焉
第五問
劉世揚
同考試官訓導方 批 策場正欲觀學者通
濟之才諸作非腐則迂曉得此卷議論切當文采振發而又不僅故
事所拘奇士也敬服敬服
punctuated:
此而求善處之術，亦必有說矣。竊嘗反復先王之故，深繹後世之弊，則亦不獨患田畝之兼併，而猶患鄙里之豐耗。豐者戶多，則輕於輸稅；耗者戶寡，則苦於取盈。謂宜依倣均田，稍爲之限，而又酌周人九兩繫民之法，定立常制，使分籍貿田者皆不得出其鄉，則戶里必均，而可以免財賦偏重之弊。申明舊章，使征租督課者皆不得違其式，則稅斂不橫，而可以紓赤子呻吟之憂。庶於苴漏補罅，或一少助也。若夫節用愛人，以爲致治之本，更俟他日爲聖天子獻焉。

第五問
劉世揚

同考試官訓導方批：策場正欲觀學者通濟之才，諸作非腐則迂。曉得此卷議論切當，文采振發，而又不僅故事所拘，奇士也。敬服，敬服！
translation_en:
…beyond this, there must also be something to propose in seeking an effective way to handle the matter. I have repeatedly considered the precedents of the former kings and carefully examined the abuses of later ages. The concern is not solely the concentration of farmland in a few hands, but also the prosperity and decline of local communities. Prosperous communities have many households, so their tax burden is light; declining communities have few households, so they suffer in making up the full quota. I suggest drawing upon the equal-field system to impose some limits, and also adapting the Zhou people's method of binding the people through nine bonds, thereby establishing lasting regulations. If those who establish separate household registrations or trade land are all prohibited from going outside their own township, households will be evenly distributed among the communities, and the problem of disproportionately heavy fiscal burdens can be avoided. Reaffirm the existing statutes, so that those who collect land taxes and supervise their payment may never depart from the prescribed rules. Tax exactions will then cease to be arbitrary, and the distress that makes the common people groan can be relieved. This might offer some small help in plugging leaks and patching gaps. As for practicing economy and cherishing the people as the foundation of good government, I shall await another day to present these matters to the sagely Son of Heaven.

Fifth Question
Liu Shiyang

Comment by Associate Examiner Fang, Assistant Instructor: The policy examination is intended precisely to reveal candidates' capacity for practical understanding and effective action. The other compositions are either stale or impractical. I find [?] that this script's arguments are apt and sound, its literary expression vigorous and stirring, and its reasoning not confined merely by precedents. Here is an exceptional scholar. My admiration, my admiration!

title: 正德八年福建鄉試錄
text:
同考試官訓導劉批用守令以安民正
朝廷今日所深致意者此策博古知今卓有定見是用錄之
考試官教諭沈批世未甞乏才顧吾所以用之
者何如耳此能發之而鋪叙委曲處又整潔精采蓋有學識者矣
考試官學正魏批此策塲中類多勦攈雷同可
厭此篇有灼見而下筆警抜逈異眾作取子豈特魁秋闈而已哉
人君欲安天下之民旣當有以重其本
尤當有以操其要夫守令民之本也賢
否休戚之相關勢所必致有天下者不
===
可一日而不重焉者也於此又有要焉
不知所以操之則所以責任勸懲者皆
不得其道而爲守令者亦何所激發而
思奮哉知此則可以安天下之民矣昔
者先王建萬國親諸侯未有守令之職
也自秦廢封建分天下爲郡縣而始有
之由漢而唐而宋沿襲不變雖其間更
置名稱不能以皆同而倚之以成治則
一也故漢宣帝甞曰庶民安於田里而
punctuated:
同考試官訓導劉批：用守令以安民，正朝廷今日所深致意者。此策博古知今，卓有定見，是用錄之。

考試官教諭沈批：世未甞乏才，顧吾所以用之者何如耳。此能發之，而鋪叙委曲處，又整潔精采，蓋有學識者矣。

考試官學正魏批：此策塲中，類多勦攈雷同，可厭。此篇有灼見，而下筆警抜，逈異眾作。取子豈特魁秋闈而已哉！

人君欲安天下之民，旣當有以重其本，尤當有以操其要。夫守令，民之本也；賢否休戚之相關，勢所必致。有天下者不可一日而不重焉者也。於此又有要焉，不知所以操之，則所以責任勸懲者皆不得其道，而爲守令者亦何所激發而思奮哉？知此，則可以安天下之民矣。昔者先王建萬國，親諸侯，未有守令之職也。自秦廢封建，分天下爲郡縣，而始有之。由漢而唐而宋，沿襲不變。雖其間更置名稱，不能以皆同，而倚之以成治，則一也。故漢宣帝甞曰：「庶民安於田里而
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner Liu, Assistant Instructor: Employing prefects and magistrates to bring peace to the people is precisely what the court is giving its closest attention to today. This policy essay displays extensive knowledge of antiquity and an understanding of the present, with remarkably firm judgments. For this reason it has been selected for inclusion.

Comment by Examiner Shen, Instructor: The world has never lacked talented men; the question is simply how we employ them. This essay brings out that point. Even where its exposition follows the subject’s subtleties, it remains orderly, polished, and brilliant. Its author is surely a man of learning and discernment.

Comment by Examiner Wei, School Director: In this policy-essay examination, most submissions are derivative compilations [?], tiresomely alike. This essay offers penetrating insights, and its writing is striking and outstanding, far different from the other compositions. In selecting you, could we intend merely that you should head the autumn Provincial Examination, and nothing more?

If a ruler wishes to bring peace to the people of the realm, he must give due weight to their foundation and, still more, grasp the essential means of doing so. Prefects and magistrates are the foundation of the people’s well-being. That the people’s welfare or suffering should be bound up with the worthiness or unworthiness of these officials is an inevitable consequence of their position. The ruler of the realm cannot neglect their importance for even a single day. Yet here too there is an essential point. Without knowing how to grasp it, all his means of assigning responsibility, encouraging, and punishing will miss their proper course. What, then, will inspire those serving as prefects and magistrates to exert themselves? Understanding this makes it possible to bring peace to the people of the realm.

In antiquity, the former kings established the myriad states and maintained close ties with the feudal lords; the offices of prefect and magistrate did not yet exist. They first appeared when Qin abolished the feudal system and divided the realm into commanderies and counties. From Han through Tang to Song, this arrangement was inherited without change. Although the titles were altered from time to time and were not all identical, reliance upon these officials to achieve good government remained the same. title: 正德八年福建鄉試錄
text:
無愁嘆者政平訟理也與我共此者惟
良二千石乎唐太宗曰為朕養民者惟
都督刺史縣令尤為親民不可不擇宋
神宗因選法未善乃曰今以一州生靈
付庸人常痛心疾首三君者何其重守
令若是耶攷之于史漢嘗置部刺史以
察十三部矣其詔書所察六條如強豪
不法違詔侵害失政召變選署弗平子
弟不飭比惡損政是也然其法不及於
===
令而獨於二千石察之蓋一守得而諸
縣無不治耳唐嘗遣黜陟使以察十一
道矣若陸贄所言八計則稽户口之豐
耗墾田之贏縮賦役之薄厚案籍之煩
簡囚繫之盈虛姦盜之有無選舉之衆
寡學校之興廢是也惜其法不述於詔
而獨於庾何等受遣之日說之則亦不
過一時之事耳至宋歐陽脩慨天下多
弊議選朝臣分察諸路其所欲明著之
punctuated: 無愁嘆者，政平訟理也。與我共此者，惟良二千石乎？」唐太宗曰：「為朕養民者，惟都督、刺史，縣令尤為親民，不可不擇。」宋神宗因選法未善，乃曰：「今以一州生靈付庸人，常痛心疾首。」三君者，何其重守令若是耶？攷之于史，漢嘗置部刺史以察十三部矣。其詔書所察六條，如強豪不法、違詔侵害、失政召變、選署弗平、子弟不飭、比惡損政是也。然其法不及於令，而獨於二千石察之，蓋一守得而諸縣無不治耳。唐嘗遣黜陟使以察十一道矣。若陸贄所言八計，則稽户口之豐耗、墾田之贏縮、賦役之薄厚、案籍之煩簡、囚繫之盈虛、姦盜之有無、選舉之衆寡、學校之興廢是也。惜其法不述於詔，而獨於庾何等受遣之日說之，則亦不過一時之事耳。至宋，歐陽脩慨天下多弊，議選朝臣分察諸路，其所欲明著之
translation_en:
…and have no cause for sorrow or lamentation, it is because government is equitable and lawsuits are properly adjudicated. Who shares this responsibility with me but good officials of the two-thousand-bushel rank?” Emperor Taizong of Tang said: “Those who nurture the people for me are the area commanders and prefects. County magistrates are especially close to the people and must be carefully chosen.” Emperor Shenzong of Song, finding the selection procedures inadequate, said: “To entrust the living souls of an entire prefecture to a mediocre man—this constantly causes me anguish and distress.” Why did these three rulers attach such great importance to prefects and county magistrates?
Consulting the histories, we find that the Han established regional inspectors to scrutinize the thirteen regions. The six articles of inquiry set out in the imperial edict concerned such matters as powerful local magnates acting lawlessly; violations of edicts and abuses that harmed the people; failures of government that provoked unrest; inequity in selecting and appointing officials; lack of discipline among sons and younger brothers; and collusion with evildoers to the detriment of government. Yet these regulations did not extend to county magistrates: scrutiny was directed solely at officials of the two-thousand-bushel rank. For if a suitable prefect was secured, none of the counties under him would fail to be well governed.
The Tang dispatched commissioners for demotion and promotion to inspect the eleven circuits. The eight assessments proposed by Lu Zhi examined growth or decline in registered households and population; expansion or contraction of cultivated land; lightness or severity of taxes and labor services; complexity or simplicity of case files and registers; the number of prisoners held; the presence or absence of malefactors and thieves; the number of men selected and recommended for office; and the flourishing or decline of schools. Regrettably, these procedures were not set forth in an edict, but were explained only when Yu He and the others received their commissions. Thus they amounted merely to a measure for that particular occasion.
Under the Song, Ouyang Xiu lamented the many abuses throughout the realm and proposed selecting court officials to inspect the various circuits separately. The matters he wished to have explicitly set forth …

title: 正德八年福建鄉試錄
text:
事不過公廉勤幹四者而已而當時惟
詔諸轉運使兼按察似未足以得其實
焉夫以守令爲重則必不輕以授人嚴
吏治之稽則必有實效以應之者故三
代以後言治者必曰漢唐宋至言守令
之賢獨舉而歸之於漢何耶蓋由宣帝
綜核名實信賞必罰所致耳觀其拜刺
史守相輒親見問退加考察而後用之
責之既專任之復久及治效之著輒勉
===
以璽書增其祿秩故爵一關內侯則天
下之爲守者勸矣封一褒德侯則天下
之爲令者勸矣以是漢世循吏之盛過
於唐宋載諸傳者可見也洪惟我
朝稽古建官愼擇守令而責成之以學校
農桑戶口田野詞訟盜賊之六事又歲
各
命憲臣一員以巡察之又通計其舉否以爲
黜陟焉然八計已具六事之中而公廉
punctuated:
事，不過公廉勤幹四者而已。而當時惟詔諸轉運使兼按察，似未足以得其實焉。夫以守令爲重，則必不輕以授人；嚴吏治之稽，則必有實效以應之者。故三代以後言治者，必曰漢唐宋；至言守令之賢，獨舉而歸之於漢，何耶？蓋由宣帝綜核名實、信賞必罰所致耳。觀其拜刺史守相，輒親見問，退加考察而後用之。責之既專，任之復久，及治效之著，輒勉以璽書，增其祿秩。故爵一關內侯，則天下之爲守者勸矣；封一褒德侯，則天下之爲令者勸矣。以是漢世循吏之盛，過於唐宋，載諸傳者可見也。
洪惟我朝稽古建官，愼擇守令，而責成之以學校、農桑、戶口、田野、詞訟、盜賊之六事。又歲各命憲臣一員以巡察之，又通計其舉否，以爲黜陟焉。然八計已具六事之中，而公廉
translation_en:
…the matters he sought to set out clearly amounted to just four qualities: public-mindedness, integrity, diligence, and competence. Yet at the time, the court merely ordered the various Transport Commissioners to undertake concurrent inspection duties; this seems to have been insufficient to secure substantive results. If prefects and magistrates are regarded as important, appointments to these posts must not be made lightly; if scrutiny of their administration is rigorous, there must be actual achievements to meet it. Thus, when discussing good government after the Three Dynasties, people invariably cite the Han, Tang, and Song. But when discussing worthy prefects and magistrates, why do they single out the Han alone? It was surely because Emperor Xuan comprehensively checked actual performance against professed merit, reliably rewarded achievement, and unfailingly punished wrongdoing. Consider how, when appointing Regional Inspectors, Governors, and Chancellors of princedoms, he always received and questioned them personally, then further investigated them after they withdrew, before employing them. He gave them undivided responsibility and kept them in office for long terms. Once their administrative achievements became evident, he encouraged them with letters bearing the imperial seal and increased their salaries and ranks. Thus, by granting one man the rank of Marquis within the Passes, he encouraged all who served as Governors throughout the realm; by enfeoffing one man as Marquis Who Extols Virtue, he encouraged all who served as Magistrates. Consequently, the abundance of exemplary officials under the Han surpassed that under the Tang and Song, as their recorded biographies show.
We reverently reflect that our dynasty has established offices after examining ancient precedents, carefully selected prefects and magistrates, and held them accountable for results in six matters: schools, agriculture and sericulture, households and population, farmland, litigation, and banditry. Each year it also appoints one censorial official to conduct inspections in each jurisdiction, and comprehensively assesses the officials’ performance as the basis for dismissal or promotion. Now, the eight criteria of assessment are already encompassed within these six matters, while public-mindedness and integrity…

title: 正德八年福建鄉試錄
text:
勤幹四者之要正憲臣今日之所求凡
事皆得按察有非漢法非條不省之遺
也立法之善誠有非漢唐宋可比者百
四十餘年吏稱其職民安其業用此道
耳然法久弊生理極人玩近年以來吏
或有受直怠事之愆民率多流離失業
之患豈無興學校而使文風比齊魯如
文翁者乎勸農桑而使嘉禾無螟犯如
魯恭者乎增戶口而使隣縣民歸如第
===
五訪者乎闢田野而歲增溉田三萬頃
如召信臣者乎簡詞訟而獄八年無重
囚如黃霸者乎息盜賊而化刀劍為牛
犢如龔遂者乎今日固不必借才於異
代也夫守令豈不欲民之安也拘文法
則美意或窒而事無濟數變易則膏澤
莫究而績不彰循虛名而不責實效則
賢否混淆真贗相半雖有賞罰何足以
為勸懲哉愚願
punctuated: 勤幹四者之要，正憲臣今日之所求。凡事皆得按察，有非漢法非條不省之遺也。立法之善，誠有非漢唐宋可比者。百四十餘年，吏稱其職，民安其業，用此道耳。然法久弊生，理極人玩。近年以來，吏或有受直怠事之愆，民率多流離失業之患。豈無興學校而使文風比齊魯，如文翁者乎？勸農桑而使嘉禾無螟犯，如魯恭者乎？增戶口而使隣縣民歸，如第五訪者乎？闢田野而歲增溉田三萬頃，如召信臣者乎？簡詞訟而獄八年無重囚，如黃霸者乎？息盜賊而化刀劍為牛犢，如龔遂者乎？今日固不必借才於異代也。夫守令豈不欲民之安也？拘文法，則美意或窒而事無濟；數變易，則膏澤莫究而績不彰；循虛名而不責實效，則賢否混淆，真贗相半。雖有賞罰，何足以為勸懲哉？愚願
translation_en:
…diligence and competence: the essentials of these four qualities are precisely what the censorial officials seek today. All matters may be investigated, without the shortcoming of Han regulations, under which matters outside the specified articles were not examined. The excellence of this legislation truly surpasses anything comparable under the Han, Tang, or Song. For more than 140 years, officials have fulfilled their duties and the people have pursued their livelihoods in peace, solely through this approach. Yet as laws endure, abuses arise; even when principles are fully developed, people treat them lightly. In recent years, some officials have been guilty of drawing their salaries while neglecting their duties, and many among the people have suffered displacement and loss of livelihood.

Are there none like Wen Weng, who promoted schools and made the literary culture rival that of Qi and Lu? None like Lu Gong, who encouraged farming and sericulture so that fine grain suffered no attack by borers? None like Diwu Fang, who increased the registered population and drew people from neighboring counties to settle under his administration? None like Shao Xinchen, who opened up farmland and increased irrigated land by 30,000 qing annually? None like Huang Ba, who reduced litigation so that for eight years his prison held no prisoners charged with grave offenses? None like Gong Sui, who quelled banditry and turned swords and sabers into cattle and calves? Surely today we need not borrow talent from other ages.

Do prefects and county magistrates not wish the people to live in peace? When constrained by legal formalities, their good intentions may be thwarted and their undertakings accomplish nothing. When they are frequently replaced, their beneficence cannot fully reach the people and their achievements remain obscure. When empty reputations are accepted without demanding actual results, the worthy and unworthy become confused, and the genuine and spurious each account for half. Even if rewards and punishments exist, how can they suffice to encourage good conduct and deter wrongdoing? I humbly wish…

title: 正德八年福建鄉試錄
text:
朝廷之上特重是選責之專而使得行其
所志任之久而使必究其所施然後按
文以稽其功循名以責其實異者予以
重爵而不靳罪者繩以明法而弗貸則
天下之爲守令者將日夜激勵務安其
民必使田里無愁嘆之聲以副
朝廷勤恤之意吾見循吏輩出而漢諸君
子有不足多者矣執事毋以爲書生之
迂談而進之幸甚
punctuated: 朝廷之上特重是選，責之專而使得行其所志，任之久而使必究其所施，然後按文以稽其功，循名以責其實。異者予以重爵而不靳，罪者繩以明法而弗貸，則天下之爲守令者將日夜激勵，務安其民，必使田里無愁嘆之聲，以副朝廷勤恤之意。吾見循吏輩出，而漢諸君子有不足多者矣。執事毋以爲書生之迂談而進之，幸甚。
translation_en: …that the imperial court give particular weight to selecting these officials, entrust them with undivided responsibility so that they can carry out their intentions, and retain them in office long enough to ensure that their measures take full effect. Only then should it examine their records to assess their achievements and require actual performance to match their professed accomplishments. Those of exceptional merit should receive high rank without stint; the culpable should be held to clearly established laws without pardon. Then all who serve as prefects and magistrates throughout the realm will spur themselves on day and night, striving to bring peace to their people. They will ensure that no cries of sorrow or sighs of distress arise from the villages and fields, thus fulfilling the court’s intent to care diligently for the people. I foresee exemplary local officials emerging in succession, such that even those gentlemen of the Han will scarcely seem worthy of especial praise. If you, sir, would refrain from dismissing this as a bookish scholar’s impractical talk and submit it to the court, I would be most grateful.

title: 正德八年福建鄉試錄
text:
福建鄉試錄後序
正德八年秋八月福建鄉試
事既竣錄既成學正昪既序
諸首簡矣璋忝承乏可無一
言以申告之夫
國家之設科舉所以網羅賢才
而用之然知人之難在昔為
===
然故必因文以知言因言以
知人耳言之平正通達則施
於政而為有用之文三代以
前六經之文尚矣秦漢而下
高者涉於荒遠卑者安於粗
陋靡麗險譎悉文之病也迨
宋濂洛關閩諸賢輩出講明
punctuated:
福建鄉試錄後序

正德八年秋八月，福建鄉試事既竣，錄既成，學正昪既序諸首簡矣。璋忝承乏，可無一言以申告之？夫國家之設科舉，所以網羅賢才而用之。然知人之難，在昔為然，故必因文以知言，因言以知人耳。言之平正通達，則施於政而為有用之文。三代以前，六經之文尚矣。秦漢而下，高者涉於荒遠，卑者安於粗陋，靡麗險譎，悉文之病也。迨宋，濂洛關閩諸賢輩出，講明
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Fujian Provincial Examination

In autumn, in the eighth month of the eighth year of Zhengde (1513), the Fujian Provincial Examination had concluded, its record had been compiled, and Bian 昪, the Instructor, had already supplied a preface on its opening pages. Having unworthily served to fill a vacancy, could I, Zhang 璋, offer no words to reiterate its admonitions? The state established the civil-service examinations to gather worthy and talented men and employ them. Yet discerning men’s character was difficult even in antiquity. Thus one must use their writing to understand their words, and their words to understand the men themselves. If their words are balanced, upright, clear, and coherent, their writing can be applied to government and serve a useful purpose. The writings of the Six Classics from the Three Dynasties and earlier were indeed exalted. From the Qin and Han onward, the loftier writings strayed into the fanciful and remote, while the lower rested content with coarseness and crudity. Ornate extravagance and strained ingenuity are all defects in writing. With the Song, the worthies of Lian, Luo, Guan, and Min arose in succession and elucidated…

title: 正德八年福建鄉試錄
text:
理道使六經之文煥然大明
天下後世用之於身而身脩
用之於家而家齊用之於國
與天下則治且平其菽粟布
帛民生不可一日而缺焉者
夫六經爾諸士子所素服也
今日之進用固以文爲階矣
===
其知文之所重乎脫或變其
初服而鼓怪誕不經之說以
聳人之觀聽豈直文之無裨
於用耶殆爲曲學之病漢聲
律之病唐新說之病宋其害
有不可勝言者矣一若菽粟
布帛人或厭之而喜珍異之
punctuated: 理道，使六經之文煥然大明，天下後世用之於身而身脩，用之於家而家齊，用之於國與天下則治且平。其菽粟布帛，民生不可一日而缺焉者。夫六經，爾諸士子所素服也。今日之進用，固以文爲階矣，其知文之所重乎？脫或變其初服，而鼓怪誕不經之說，以聳人之觀聽，豈直文之無裨於用耶？殆爲曲學之病漢、聲律之病唐、新說之病宋，其害有不可勝言者矣。一若菽粟布帛，人或厭之，而喜珍異之
translation_en: …the principles of the Way, making the writings of the Six Classics shine forth with renewed clarity. Throughout the world and in later generations, those who apply them to themselves cultivate their persons; those who apply them to their families bring their families into order; and those who apply them to the state and all under Heaven bring good government and peace. They are like grain and cloth, indispensable to the people's livelihood even for a single day. The Six Classics are what you candidates have long adhered to. Your advancement into service today assuredly takes literary composition as its stepping-stone, but do you understand what matters most in writing? If you should abandon your original commitments and promote bizarre, unfounded doctrines to startle people's eyes and ears, would this merely mean that your writing had no practical benefit? It would be like the distorted learning that afflicted the Han, the preoccupation with prosody that afflicted the Tang, and the novel doctrines that afflicted the Song: the harm would be beyond telling. It is just as when people grow weary of grain and cloth and delight instead in rare and exotic…

title: 正德八年福建鄉試錄
text:
服食雖足以快一時之口體
而害亦隨之嘗聞之李諤有
云文筆日繁其政日亂彼豈
無所徵耶是知文必達於用
則言之發於文者非虛文而
成於事業矣豈輪轅飾而弗
庸也耶昔者伊尹起莘野而
===
形三嘆於應聘傅說舉版築
而敷三命於對揚卒成格天
綏民之績是皆有得於文者
諸士子能允蹈伊傅之說使
堯舜之道大行於世則於
國家求賢之意與吾儕取之之
責庶無負哉
punctuated: 服食，雖足以快一時之口體，而害亦隨之。嘗聞之，李諤有云：「文筆日繁，其政日亂。」彼豈無所徵耶？是知文必達於用，則言之發於文者，非虛文而成於事業矣。豈輪轅飾而弗庸也耶？昔者伊尹起莘野而形三嘆於應聘，傅說舉版築而敷三命於對揚，卒成格天綏民之績，是皆有得於文者。諸士子能允蹈伊傅之說，使堯舜之道大行於世，則於國家求賢之意與吾儕取之之責，庶無負哉！
translation_en:
…clothing and food: although they may briefly gratify the palate and body, harm follows in their wake. I have heard that Li E said: “As literary compositions grow daily more elaborate, government grows daily more disordered.” Surely his words had some basis? From this we know that writing must serve practical purposes. Then words expressed in writing will not be empty ornament but will find fulfillment in deeds and achievements. How could this be like wheels and carriage shafts that are decorated but never used?

Formerly, Yi Yin rose from the fields of Shen and gave expression to three sighs when answering the invitation to serve; Fu Yue was raised from the work of building rammed-earth walls and elaborated upon three royal charges in his reverent responses. Ultimately, they accomplished deeds that moved Heaven and brought peace to the people. Both understood something essential about writing. If you examination candidates can faithfully follow the teachings of Yi Yin and Fu Yue, causing the Way of Yao and Shun to prevail throughout the world, then perhaps neither the state's purpose in seeking worthy men nor our responsibility in selecting them will have been betrayed!

title: 正德八年福建鄉試錄
text:
直隸淮安府邳州宿遷縣儒
學教諭沈璋謹序
punctuated: 直隸淮安府邳州宿遷縣儒學教諭沈璋謹序。
translation_en: Preface respectfully composed by Shen Zhang, Instructor of the Confucian School of Suqian County, Pizhou, Huai'an Prefecture, Zhili.

title: 正德八年福建鄉試錄
text:
福建鄉試錄序
我
太祖高皇帝定鼎之三年卽
詔天下開科取士著其事爲令良
法美意傳之
列聖以迄於
皇上皆世守而遵行之是歲癸酉
===
復維其期福建藩司舉行如
例先是白于巡按監察御史
李如圭走幣帛于四方聘昪
等以司考校而御史李如圭
寔柄其事而臨焉乃特悉意
綜理謂作興宜隆固有縟其
儀文者矣謂防範宜密固有
punctuated:
福建鄉試錄序

我太祖高皇帝定鼎之三年，卽詔天下開科取士，著其事爲令。良法美意，傳之列聖，以迄於皇上，皆世守而遵行之。是歲癸酉，復維其期，福建藩司舉行如例。先是，白于巡按監察御史李如圭，走幣帛于四方，聘昪等以司考校。而御史李如圭寔柄其事而臨焉，乃特悉意綜理。謂作興宜隆，固有縟其儀文者矣；謂防範宜密，固有
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Fujian Provincial Examination

In the third year after establishing his dynasty, our Emperor Taizu Gao issued an edict ordering examinations throughout the realm to select men for office, and established this procedure as a standing regulation. This excellent institution and its admirable intent were transmitted through the successive sage emperors down to His Majesty, each generation preserving and observing them. This year, the guiyou year [1513], the appointed time came round again, and the Fujian Provincial Administration Commission conducted the examination according to precedent. Beforehand, it reported to Regional Inspector Li Rugui and dispatched gifts of silk in all directions to invite Bian and others to oversee the examination and evaluation. Censor Li Rugui himself took charge of the undertaking and supervised it, devoting his full attention to its overall management. Holding that the encouragement of learning should be accorded high honor, he duly made its ceremonies elaborate; holding that safeguards should be stringent, he duly …

title: 正德八年福建鄉試錄
text:
嚴其科條者矣謂百執事必
皆其人固有選擇而充者矣
于時寇起鄰壤提督三省軍
務右副都御史俞諫巡撫汀
漳諸郡右副都御史周南咸
承
上命會兵於饒武功旣集文事適
===
舉鎮守福建太監崔安奉
命而來提督市舶太監尚春督理
糧餉南京户部主事胡德皆
有事茲土亦莫不崇獎斯文
以勵士氣旣八月入鎖院士
之就試者凡若干人皆提學
副使姚鏌所取以應選者也
punctuated: 嚴其科條者矣。謂百執事必皆其人，固有選擇而充者矣。于時，寇起鄰壤，提督三省軍務右副都御史俞諫、巡撫汀漳諸郡右副都御史周南，咸承上命，會兵於饒。武功旣集，文事適舉。鎮守福建太監崔安奉命而來，提督市舶太監尚春、督理糧餉南京户部主事胡德，皆有事茲土，亦莫不崇獎斯文，以勵士氣。旣八月，入鎖院，士之就試者凡若干人，皆提學副使姚鏌所取以應選者也。
translation_en: …there were accordingly measures to make the examination regulations stringent. He held that all those performing duties must be suitable for their posts; accordingly, men were selected to fill them. At that time, bandits rose in neighboring territory. Yu Jian, Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and Supreme Commander of Military Affairs in Three Provinces, and Zhou Nan, Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and Grand Coordinator of Tingzhou, Zhangzhou, and the other prefectures, both received imperial orders and assembled their troops at Rao. Just as military success was achieved, the literary undertaking was duly set in motion. Cui An, the Grand Eunuch stationed in Fujian, came under imperial orders. Shang Chun, the Grand Eunuch supervising maritime trade, and Hu De, a Secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue overseeing military provisions and pay, also had duties in this territory. All honored and encouraged literary learning to inspire the scholars. When the eighth month arrived, we entered the examination compound and were sequestered. The scholars presenting themselves for examination numbered so many in all [number unspecified]; all had been selected by Yao Mo, the Education Intendant serving as Vice Commissioner, to participate in the selection.

title: 正德八年福建鄉試錄
text:
御史李如圭復謂去取之法
宜公宜愼乃偕昪等焚香誓
戒而始事事凡三試之考試
爲昪與敎諭沈璋同考試爲
學正陳則敎諭羅榦尹孔常
方一德訓導劉文詔方準劉
芳王尚忠提調則左布政使
===
陳珂右參政孫燧監試則按
察使劉遜僉事胡鐸贊襄防
範於外則右布政使鄒文盛
左參政王子言左參議彭夔
副使湯沐僉事蔡天祐查約
胡璉而署都指揮僉事楊勳
崔灝亦相與協力焉事竣拔
punctuated: 御史李如圭復謂去取之法宜公宜愼，乃偕昪等焚香誓戒而始事。事凡三試之考試，爲昪與敎諭沈璋；同考試爲學正陳則、敎諭羅榦、尹孔常、方一德、訓導劉文詔、方準、劉芳、王尚忠。提調則左布政使陳珂、右參政孫燧；監試則按察使劉遜、僉事胡鐸。贊襄防範於外，則右布政使鄒文盛、左參政王子言、左參議彭夔、副使湯沐、僉事蔡天祐、查約、胡璉，而署都指揮僉事楊勳、崔灝亦相與協力焉。事竣，拔
translation_en:
Censor Li Rugui further declared that the procedures for rejecting and accepting candidates must be impartial and circumspect. Together with Bian and the others, he therefore burned incense, took an oath, and issued admonitions before beginning the work. The Examiners for the three examination sessions were Bian and Instructor Shen Zhang. The Associate Examiners were Instructor Chen Ze; Instructors Luo Gan, Yin Kongchang, and Fang Yide; and Assistant Instructors Liu Wenzhao, Fang Zhun, Liu Fang, and Wang Shangzhong. The Proctors were Left Provincial Administration Commissioner Chen Ke and Right Provincial Administration Vice Commissioner Sun Sui. The examination monitors were Surveillance Commissioner Liu Xun and Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Hu Duo.

Those assisting with arrangements and safeguards outside the examination compound were Right Provincial Administration Commissioner Zou Wensheng, Left Provincial Administration Vice Commissioner Wang Ziyan, Left Provincial Administration Assistant Commissioner Peng Kui, Surveillance Vice Commissioner Tang Mu, and Assistant Surveillance Commissioners Cai Tianyou, Zha Yue, and Hu Lian. Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioners Yang Xun and Cui Hao likewise joined in supporting their efforts. When the work was finished, they selected…

title: 正德八年福建鄉試錄
text:
其尤得士九十人并集其文
之純者爲錄以
獻尋當序諸首簡惟閩士之於
文盛矣嘗卽而推之文章者
治化之徵也故元和之世特
號多才用其文與周漢軏嘉
祐治平之期其宗工鉅筆亦
===
並時而起名之相埒至有見
於翁季伯仲間者
國家以人文化成天下百六十
年于玆道久效臻固宜出而
秉大制作以鳴太平者若是
其班班而偏陬下邑之士皆
知占一經自奮以求齒上國
punctuated:
其尤，得士九十人，并集其文之純者爲錄，以獻。尋當序諸首簡。惟閩士之於文，盛矣！嘗卽而推之，文章者，治化之徵也。故元和之世，特號多才，用其文與周漢軏。嘉祐、治平之期，其宗工鉅筆亦並時而起，名之相埒，至有見於翁季伯仲間者。
國家以人文化成天下，百六十年于玆，道久效臻，固宜出而秉大制作，以鳴太平者，若是其班班。而偏陬下邑之士，皆知占一經，自奮以求齒上國。
translation_en:
…the most outstanding among them, obtaining ninety successful candidates; their most accomplished compositions were also gathered into a record for presentation to the throne. I was then to provide a preface on its opening leaves. The scholars of Fujian have indeed flourished in literary composition! Reflecting upon this, I have concluded that literary writing is a sign of the transforming influence of good government. Thus the Yuanhe era was particularly renowned for its abundance of talent, its writings ranking alongside those of the Zhou and Han [?]. During the Jiayou and Zhiping eras, its great masters and powerful writers likewise arose together. Some whose reputations matched one another were even found among fathers and younger generations [?], or among elder and younger brothers.
For 160 years now, our dynasty has transformed all under Heaven through cultural refinement. As its Way has endured and its effects have matured, it is surely fitting that those who come forth to undertake great literary compositions, giving voice to an age of peace, should be so conspicuously numerous. Even scholars from remote corners and humble towns know to devote themselves to a single Classic and exert themselves, seeking a place among the ranks in the imperial realm…

title: 正德八年福建鄉試錄
text:
其勢則然矣閩文獻大藩也
有不日趨於盛哉且文章變
化要亦山川者爲之昔司馬
子長踪跡半天下其後始大
肆於篇章柳子厚得西山之
勝至自謂與萬化冥合閩東
南際大海渺漫數千里不可
===
涯涘延建上下奔流激湍使
人錯愕不能自已至若武夷
之環勝壺公之峭碧旣蜿蜒
委伏若拱若揖而石鼓峨嵋
諸峯亦復嶙峋高聳上挿霄
漢士生其間必將有鍾焉顧
駭聞異觀坐致几席又豈無
punctuated: 其勢則然矣。閩，文獻大藩也，有不日趨於盛哉？且文章變化，要亦山川者爲之。昔司馬子長踪跡半天下，其後始大肆於篇章；柳子厚得西山之勝，至自謂與萬化冥合。閩東南際大海，渺漫數千里，不可涯涘。延建上下，奔流激湍，使人錯愕不能自已。至若武夷之環勝、壺公之峭碧，旣蜿蜒委伏，若拱若揖，而石鼓、峨嵋諸峯，亦復嶙峋高聳，上挿霄漢。士生其間，必將有鍾焉。顧駭聞異觀，坐致几席，又豈無
translation_en: …Such, indeed, is the natural tendency. Fujian is a great province rich in literary culture and worthy men: could it fail to flourish increasingly day by day? Moreover, the transformations of literary writing are, in essence, also brought about by mountains and rivers. In former times, Sima Zichang traveled over half the realm; only afterward did his writing attain its full expansive power. Liu Zihou encountered the splendid scenery of Xishan and went so far as to say that he had become mystically united with the myriad transformations of nature. Along its southeastern edge, Fujian borders the great sea, stretching boundlessly for thousands of li, its limits beyond sight. Through the upper and lower reaches of Yanping and Jianning, rushing currents and surging rapids leave people astonished and unable to contain themselves. As for the encircling splendors of Wuyi and the precipitous green heights of Hugong, they wind and dip as though clasping their hands in salute or bowing; the peaks of Shigu and Emei likewise rise rugged and lofty, thrusting into the heavens. Scholars born among them must surely receive something of their concentrated potency. Indeed, marvels to hear and extraordinary sights come to them as they sit at their desks and mats: how could there be none who…

title: 正德八年福建鄉試錄
text:
得之以為胸中浩博瓌詭之
奇而於筆下焉發之者哉况
夫江左貴清綺之詞河朔重
剛正之體文之成乎其習者
皆是也閩故多名賢大儒今
其講道之地遺踪相望學者
登其堂入其室覽遺編而考
===
其故焉則升降揖遜之容若
將見之而性命道德之旨猶
恍然有以自悟閩之學以義
理勝者豈一朝之故哉然則
今日之選固宜隨取隨獲有
足饜主司之求者矣雖然科
目本以取士而不能不假士
punctuated: 得之以為胸中浩博瓌詭之奇，而於筆下焉發之者哉？况夫江左貴清綺之詞，河朔重剛正之體，文之成乎其習者皆是也。閩故多名賢大儒，今其講道之地，遺踪相望。學者登其堂，入其室，覽遺編而考其故焉，則升降揖遜之容若將見之，而性命道德之旨猶恍然有以自悟。閩之學以義理勝者，豈一朝之故哉？然則今日之選，固宜隨取隨獲，有足饜主司之求者矣。雖然，科目本以取士，而不能不假士
translation_en: …those who absorb these sights, making them a source of vast and wondrous marvels within their hearts, and give them expression through their brushes? Moreover, Jiangzuo prizes lucid and ornate diction, while Heshuo esteems a forceful and upright style: both exemplify how writing is shaped by local habits. Fujian has long had many renowned worthies and great Confucian scholars. The surviving traces of the places where they taught the Way are still found within sight of one another. When students ascend their halls, enter their chambers, read their surviving writings, and examine their traditions, they seem almost to see their bearing as they ascended and descended, bowed and deferred; and they may still, in a moment of illumination, attain their own understanding of the purport of human nature, Heaven’s mandate, the Way, and virtue. Could Fujian’s learning have come to excel in moral principle in a single day? Thus, in today’s selection, worthy candidates should surely be found at every turn, sufficient to satisfy what the presiding examiners seek. Nevertheless, although the examination system was originally intended to select scholars, it cannot but depend upon scholars…

title: 正德八年福建鄉試錄
text:
爲重一代之科目得數人以
顯必其所謂賢者也一榜之
人物得一人以顯必其所謂
尤賢者也唐科目凡幾舉其
稱爲龍虎榜者爲最盛而歐
陽詹預焉宋科目凡幾舉其
以狀元甲科起而稱名宰相
===
者亦最盛而梁文靖公克家
預焉此所謂得數人以顯者
也歐與梁皆閩產也紹興十
八年榜此文公朱夫子所嘗
登名焉者榜中之眾不必皆
文公也世有慕於文公今其
錄獨傳而三百三十人者其
punctuated: 爲重。一代之科目，得數人以顯，必其所謂賢者也；一榜之人物，得一人以顯，必其所謂尤賢者也。唐科目凡幾？舉其稱爲龍虎榜者爲最盛，而歐陽詹預焉。宋科目凡幾？舉其以狀元甲科起而稱名宰相者亦最盛，而梁文靖公克家預焉。此所謂得數人以顯者也。歐與梁皆閩產也。紹興十八年榜，此文公朱夫子所嘗登名焉者。榜中之眾，不必皆文公也。世有慕於文公，今其錄獨傳，而三百三十人者，其
translation_en:
…for their prestige. When the examinations of an entire dynasty gain distinction through a few men, these must be men regarded as worthy. When the men on a single examination list gain distinction through one man, he must be regarded as exceptionally worthy. How many examinations were held under the Tang? The one whose list was called the “Dragon and Tiger List” is cited as the most illustrious, and Ouyang Zhan was among those on it. How many examinations were held under the Song? Those whose graduates rose from first place or the highest ranks to become renowned chief councillors are likewise cited as the most illustrious, and Liang Kejia, posthumously titled Wenjing, was among them. This is what is meant by gaining distinction through a few men. Both Ouyang and Liang were natives of Fujian.

The examination list of the eighteenth year of Shaoxing was one on which Master Zhu Xi, posthumously titled Wengong, had his name inscribed. The many men on that list were not necessarily all the equal of Master Zhu. Because people have admired him, its examination record alone has been transmitted to the present; and as for those 330 men, their …

title: 正德八年福建鄉試錄
text:
姓名皆藉是以自見此所謂
得一人以顯者也文公亦閩
產也夫閩諸先正之係於科
目其重於天下如此况一鄉
乎其重於後世又如此况當
時乎諸士子固皆閩之俊也
其亦有篤前脩之仰昂焉自
===
奮以為是科之光者乎夫自
諸先正求之其切深者文也
最隆焉者慈孝也靖深者器
局也盡心謀國者忠也洋洋
乎布滿天下者著述也泝伊
洛以接洙泗者道與德也為
彼為此具可師法而其所以
punctuated:
姓名皆藉是以自見，此所謂得一人以顯者也。文公亦閩產也。夫閩諸先正之係於科目，其重於天下如此，况一鄉乎？其重於後世又如此，况當時乎？諸士子固皆閩之俊也，其亦有篤前脩之仰，昂焉自奮，以為是科之光者乎？

夫自諸先正求之，其切深者文也，最隆焉者慈孝也，靖深者器局也，盡心謀國者忠也，洋洋乎布滿天下者著述也，泝伊洛以接洙泗者道與德也。為彼為此，具可師法，而其所以
translation_en:
…their names all gain visibility through this. This is what is meant by becoming illustrious through a single man. Lord Wen, too, was a native of Fujian. The association of Fujian’s earlier worthies with the examinations carries such weight throughout the realm—how much more within a single province! It carries such weight for later generations—how much more in their own time! These candidates are assuredly all outstanding men of Fujian. Might there be among them some who, deeply revering their worthy predecessors, rouse themselves with lofty resolve to bring distinction to this examination?

If we seek examples among these earlier worthies, what is incisive and profound is their writing; what is most exalted is their parental kindness and filial devotion; what is tranquil and deep is their capacity and breadth of character. Their wholehearted planning for the state is loyalty; what spreads far and wide throughout the realm is their scholarly writing; what traces the Yi and Luo traditions upstream to connect with those of the Zhu and Si is their Way and virtue. Whether in this respect or that, all may be taken as models to emulate; and the grounds upon which they…

title: 正德八年福建鄉試錄
text:
爲重者固不外是是在諸士
子勉之而已矣
湖廣荆州府荆門州儒學學
正魏尋謹序
punctuated:
爲重者，固不外是，是在諸士子勉之而已矣。
湖廣荆州府荆門州儒學學正魏尋謹序。
translation_en:
…what makes them worthy of esteem surely lies in nothing beyond these qualities. It remains only for the examination candidates to strive to emulate them.
This preface was respectfully composed by Wei Xun, Instructor in the Confucian School of Jingmen Department, Jingzhou Prefecture, Huguang.

title: 正德八年福建鄉試錄
text:
正德八年福建鄉試
監臨官
巡按福建監察御史李如圭〔國寶湖廣澧州人己未進士〕
提調官
福建等處承宣布政使司左布政使陳珂〔希白浙江杭州前衞人庚戌進士〕
福建等處承宣布政使司右參政孫燧〔德成浙江餘姚縣人癸丑進士〕
監試官
福建等處提刑按察司按察使劉遜〔時讓江西安福縣人戊戌進士〕
福建等處提刑按察司僉事胡鐸〔時振浙江餘姚縣人乙丑進士〕
===
考試官

title: 正德八年福建鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
赫兮喧兮者威儀也
多聞擇其善者而從之多見而識之
仁之實事親是也義之實從兄是也智
之實知斯二者弗去是也禮之實節
文斯二者是也樂之實樂斯二者樂
則生矣生則惡可已也惡可已則不
知足之蹈之手之舞之
===
易
貞者事之幹也
君子之光有孚吉
仁者見之謂之仁知者見之謂之知
夫易聖人之所以極深而研幾也惟深
也故能通天下之志唯幾也故能成
天下之務唯神也故不疾而速不行
而至子曰易有聖人之道四焉者此
之謂也
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

赫兮喧兮者，威儀也。

多聞，擇其善者而從之；多見而識之。

仁之實，事親是也；義之實，從兄是也；智之實，知斯二者弗去是也；禮之實，節文斯二者是也；樂之實，樂斯二者。樂則生矣，生則惡可已也？惡可已，則不知足之蹈之、手之舞之。

易

貞者，事之幹也。

君子之光，有孚，吉。

仁者見之謂之仁，知者見之謂之知。

夫易，聖人之所以極深而研幾也。惟深也，故能通天下之志；唯幾也，故能成天下之務；唯神也，故不疾而速，不行而至。子曰：「易有聖人之道四焉」者，此之謂也。
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

“Resplendent and illustrious” refers to dignified bearing.

Listen widely, select what is good, and follow it; observe widely and retain what you see.

The substance of benevolence is serving one’s parents; the substance of righteousness is obeying one’s elder brothers. The substance of wisdom is understanding these two duties and never departing from them. The substance of ritual propriety is regulating and refining these two duties. The substance of music is delighting in these two duties. With delight, they flourish; once they flourish, how can they be stopped? When they cannot be stopped, one’s feet begin to stamp and one’s hands to dance without one’s knowing it.

Book of Changes

Constancy is the mainstay of affairs.

The noble man’s radiance: sincerity brings good fortune.

The benevolent see it and call it benevolence; the wise see it and call it wisdom.

The Changes is the means by which the sages plumb the depths and investigate the incipient signs of change. Through its depth, it can comprehend the aspirations of all under Heaven; through its incipient signs, it can accomplish the affairs of all under Heaven; through its numinous power, it is swift without haste and arrives without travelling. This is what the Master meant when he said, “The Changes contains four aspects of the way of the sages.”

title: 正德八年福建鄉試錄
text:
書
工以納言時而颺之
東流為漢又東為滄浪之水過三澨至
于大別南入于江
凡厥庶民有猷有為有守汝則念之不
協于極不罹于咎皇則受之而康而
色曰予攸好德汝則錫之福時人斯
其惟皇之極
三后協心同底于道道洽政治澤潤生
===
民
詩
俟我於著乎而充耳以素乎而尚之以
瓊華乎而俟我於庭乎而充耳以青
乎而尚之以瓊瑩乎而俟我於堂乎
而充耳以黃乎而尚之以瓊英乎而
民之質矣日用飲食
實方實苞實種實褎實發實秀實堅實
好實穎實栗
punctuated:
書

工以納言，時而颺之。

東流為漢，又東為滄浪之水，過三澨，至于大別，南入于江。

凡厥庶民，有猷、有為、有守，汝則念之；不協于極，不罹于咎，皇則受之。而康而色，曰：「予攸好德。」汝則錫之福，時人斯其惟皇之極。

三后協心，同底于道；道洽政治，澤潤生民。

詩

俟我於著乎而，充耳以素乎而，尚之以瓊華乎而！俟我於庭乎而，充耳以青乎而，尚之以瓊瑩乎而！俟我於堂乎而，充耳以黃乎而，尚之以瓊英乎而！

民之質矣，日用飲食。

實方實苞，實種實褎，實發實秀，實堅實好，實穎實栗。
translation_en:
Book of Documents

Let the officials submit their words; proclaim those that are right.

Flowing east, it becomes the Han; farther east, it becomes the waters of the Canglang. Passing the Sanshi, it reaches Dabie and flows south into the Yangzi.

Among the common people, those who have plans, accomplishments, or principles they uphold—you should keep them in mind. Those who do not conform to the supreme standard but have incurred no blame—the sovereign should accept them. Compose your countenance toward them. When they say, “What I love is virtue,” confer blessings upon them. These people will then adhere to the sovereign’s supreme standard.

The three sovereigns united their hearts and together attained the Way. The Way prevailed, government was well ordered, and their beneficence nourished the people.

Book of Odes

He awaits me by the entrance screen, with ear pendants of white silk, adorned with beautiful jade! He awaits me in the courtyard, with ear pendants of blue silk, adorned with lustrous jade! He awaits me in the hall, with ear pendants of yellow silk, adorned with splendid jade!

The people’s basic needs are their daily food and drink.

The grain sprouted and grew thickly; its stems swelled and grew tall. It sent forth shoots and ears; its kernels grew firm and fine, its ears full and its grain plump.

title: 正德八年福建鄉試錄
text:
策五道
問帝王之治本乎道帝王之道載於經
近世之議經者有曰天人之極致學
者讀經必究乎此而後可帝王之求
治其亦然耶我
太祖高皇帝因論讀書而曰君道以事天愛
民爲重其本在敬身於乎大哉
王言乎爲治之要盡於是矣試與諸士子論
之不知
===
聖祖之所謂事與愛與敬者果統而言之耶
其亦有所指耶考之於經若曆象璣
衡之類皆觀天文而察時變者也事
天之道盡於是乎若肆赦不廢之屬
皆悲人窮而欲並生者也愛民之道
盡於是乎或曰事天如事親愛民如
子其然乎否也身之所關何者爲大
敬之所將何者爲宜如是而或有所
不得焉又將如之何帝王之處此其
punctuated:
策五道

問：帝王之治本乎道，帝王之道載於經。近世之議經者有曰：「天人之極致。」學者讀經，必究乎此而後可。帝王之求治，其亦然耶？我太祖高皇帝因論讀書而曰：「君道以事天愛民爲重，其本在敬身。」於乎，大哉，王言乎！爲治之要盡於是矣。試與諸士子論之。不知聖祖之所謂事與愛與敬者，果統而言之耶？其亦有所指耶？考之於經，若曆象璣衡之類，皆觀天文而察時變者也。事天之道盡於是乎？若肆赦不廢之屬，皆悲人窮而欲並生者也。愛民之道盡於是乎？或曰：「事天如事親，愛民如子。」其然乎否也？身之所關，何者爲大？敬之所將，何者爲宜？如是而或有所得不得焉，又將如之何？帝王之處此，其
translation_en:
Five Policy Questions

Question: The government of emperors and kings is rooted in the Way, and their Way is recorded in the Classics. Among recent commentators on the Classics, some have spoken of “the ultimate principles of Heaven and humanity.” Only after thoroughly investigating these may scholars be said to have read the Classics adequately. Is it likewise for emperors and kings seeking good government? Our Emperor Taizu Gao, while discussing reading, said: “The ruler’s Way places foremost serving Heaven and loving the people; its foundation lies in maintaining reverence in one’s own conduct.” Ah, how great are these royal words! They encompass all the essentials of government. Let us discuss them with you examination candidates.

When our sagely founder spoke of serving, loving, and reverence, was he speaking comprehensively, or did he also have particular things in mind? Examining the Classics, we find such matters as calendrical observations and astronomical instruments, all means of observing celestial patterns and discerning seasonal changes. Is the Way of serving Heaven exhausted by these? Such matters as granting pardons and not abandoning [those in distress] all express compassion for people in hardship and the desire that all should live. Is the Way of loving the people exhausted by these? Some say: “Serve Heaven as you serve your parents, and love the people as your children.” Is this so or not? Among the matters that concern one’s own person, which are the most important? To what should reverence properly be applied? If, proceeding thus, one should still fail to attain something, what should one then do? When emperors and kings address these matters, might they …

title: 正德八年福建鄉試錄
text:
亦有道歟我
聖祖於天人之際深矣匪徒言之而又見之
躬行之實而又發以
聖見之眞藏之金匱者不可得而仰窺矣其
見于
宣宗章皇帝御製五倫書甚爲詳備而當時
儒臣之序
大明日曆則又一言以蔽之可考見已諸
士子必有得於莊誦之餘者其敬陳
===
之
問寇賊姦宄之患自古有之觀虞廷之
命臯陶雖聖世有不能免者顧吾所
以制之何如耳乃者各處地方寇賊
竊發至廑
宸慮命將出師以次削平嘗拜觀
勅諭有曰累年以來各處地方盜賊生發多
因水旱不時差科繁重及各該官司不能
撫恤大哉
punctuated:
亦有道歟？我聖祖於天人之際深矣，匪徒言之，而又見之躬行之實，而又發以聖見之眞。藏之金匱者，不可得而仰窺矣。其見于宣宗章皇帝御製《五倫書》，甚爲詳備；而當時儒臣之序《大明日曆》，則又一言以蔽之，可考見已。諸士子必有得於莊誦之餘者，其敬陳之。
問：寇賊姦宄之患，自古有之。觀虞廷之命臯陶，雖聖世有不能免者，顧吾所以制之何如耳。乃者各處地方寇賊竊發，至廑宸慮，命將出師，以次削平。嘗拜觀勅諭，有曰：「累年以來，各處地方盜賊生發，多因水旱不時、差科繁重，及各該官司不能撫恤。」大哉，
translation_en:
…is there also a way to do so? Our august founding emperor possessed a profound understanding of the relationship between Heaven and humankind. He not only spoke of it but also manifested it in his own conduct and expounded it through his genuine sagely insights. What is stored in the golden coffer we cannot reverently examine. What appears in Emperor Xuanzong Zhang’s imperially composed Book of the Five Human Relationships (Wulun shu) is exceedingly detailed and comprehensive. The preface written by the Confucian officials of that time to the Daily Calendar of the Great Ming (Da Ming rili), moreover, sums it up in a single statement, which may be consulted. You candidates must have gained some understanding from your solemn reading. Respectfully set it forth.
Question: The scourge of bandits and evildoers has existed since antiquity. Consider the appointment of Gao Yao at the court of Shun: even an age of sages could not escape it entirely. The issue is simply how we bring it under control. Recently, bandits have risen in various localities, causing concern to His Majesty, who ordered commanders to lead troops out and suppress them in succession. I have reverently read an imperial admonition that states: “For years now, outbreaks of banditry in various localities have mostly resulted from untimely floods and droughts, onerous service obligations and levies, and the failure of the responsible authorities to provide care and relief.” How great …

title: 正德八年福建鄉試錄
text:
王言其得捄敝之源致治之本乎天下之事
固難槩論姑以閩中事與諸士子商
之夫水旱天之災也將欲捄之其道
何存差科民所供也將欲省之其要
何在考之昔仕於閩有知福清而闢
陂洫四十里者有令連江而築石堤
三百丈者有知福州而首開五塘者
有知漳州而開渠十四者可謂能備
水旱矣淳熈中有奏除無名之賦七
===
百萬者嘉定中有蠲逋負十數萬者
祥符中有奏止額外增稅者紹興中
有奏蠲一切苛政者可謂能省差科
矣此皆官司所當取法可歷指其人
以實之乎然水旱有備差科不擾固
弭盜之本源也但其間如汀漳二郡
介乎閩廣之地民性獷悍習於為盜
負固山海撲而復起兹欲使之悉安
耒耜之業而歸維新之化如之何則
punctuated: 王言！其得捄敝之源、致治之本乎？天下之事，固難槩論，姑以閩中事與諸士子商之。夫水旱，天之災也，將欲捄之，其道何存？差科，民所供也，將欲省之，其要何在？考之昔仕於閩，有知福清而闢陂洫四十里者，有令連江而築石堤三百丈者，有知福州而首開五塘者，有知漳州而開渠十四者，可謂能備水旱矣。淳熈中，有奏除無名之賦七百萬者；嘉定中，有蠲逋負十數萬者；祥符中，有奏止額外增稅者；紹興中，有奏蠲一切苛政者，可謂能省差科矣。此皆官司所當取法，可歷指其人以實之乎？然水旱有備，差科不擾，固弭盜之本源也。但其間，如汀、漳二郡，介乎閩、廣之地，民性獷悍，習於為盜，負固山海，撲而復起。兹欲使之悉安耒耜之業，而歸維新之化，如之何則
translation_en:
…the sovereign’s words! Do they not grasp the source of remedies for abuses and the foundation of good government? The affairs of the realm are certainly difficult to discuss in sweeping terms; let us therefore discuss matters in Fujian with you candidates. Floods and droughts are calamities sent by Heaven. By what means can relief be provided? Labor services and tax levies are obligations borne by the people. What is essential to reducing them?

Examining those who formerly held office in Fujian, we find a magistrate of Fuqing who constructed embankments and irrigation channels extending forty li; a magistrate of Lianjiang who built a stone embankment three hundred zhang long; a prefect of Fuzhou who first established five reservoirs; and a prefect of Zhangzhou who opened fourteen channels. These men may be said to have made effective provision against floods and droughts. During the Chunxi era, someone memorialized requesting the abolition of unauthorized levies totaling seven million; during the Jiading era, someone remitted arrears amounting to more than a hundred thousand; during the Xiangfu era, someone memorialized requesting a halt to tax increases beyond the prescribed quota; and during the Shaoxing era, someone memorialized requesting the abolition of all oppressive measures. These men may be said to have effectively reduced labor services and tax levies. All are examples that officials ought to follow. Can you identify each of these men in turn to substantiate these accounts?

Preparedness against floods and droughts, together with freedom from burdensome labor services and tax levies, is indeed the foundation for suppressing banditry. Yet among these places, the two prefectures of Tingzhou and Zhangzhou lie along the border between Fujian and Guangdong. Their people are fierce and unruly by disposition and accustomed to banditry. Relying on the natural defenses of mountains and sea, they rise again after being crushed. If we now wish to bring them all to settle contentedly into agricultural livelihoods and submit to the transforming influence of renewed governance, how might this be…

title: 正德八年福建鄉試錄
text:
可宜詳著于篇將采而行之用副
德意於萬一焉
問學道者以聖人爲標的其工夫次第
先儒悉之矣姑摭一二疑義相與商
之夫脩道以仁求仁在恕仁之說多
端恕之義兩用恕何關於仁耶旣曰
有主則虛又曰有主則實無乃自相
戾耶務博則疑於玩物喪志主靜則
近於無所用心滯近小則局而不舒
===
騖高遠則虛而無實做題入議旣謂
之有識用意作文胡爲而害道協一
本非易事何以曰分殊爲難物理固
非度外何以曰事功爲害性命夫子
罕言也彼謂性非所急者可盡非耶
禮文不相沿襲也彼以禮教爲先者
非固滯耶顏子稱聖人之教曰博約
博則爲文學約則爲德行而顏子獨
以德行稱豈其學與後世異耶諸士
punctuated:
可？宜詳著于篇，將采而行之，用副德意於萬一焉。
問：學道者以聖人爲標的，其工夫次第，先儒悉之矣。姑摭一二疑義，相與商之。夫脩道以仁，求仁在恕。仁之說多端，恕之義兩用，恕何關於仁耶？旣曰有主則虛，又曰有主則實，無乃自相戾耶？務博則疑於玩物喪志，主靜則近於無所用心，滯近小則局而不舒，騖高遠則虛而無實。做題入議，旣謂之有識，用意作文，胡爲而害道？協一本非易事，何以曰分殊爲難？物理固非度外，何以曰事功爲害？性命，夫子罕言也，彼謂性非所急者，可盡非耶？禮文不相沿襲也，彼以禮教爲先者，非固滯耶？顏子稱聖人之教曰博約，博則爲文學，約則爲德行，而顏子獨以德行稱，豈其學與後世異耶？諸士
translation_en:
…would be appropriate? Set this out in detail in your essay. We shall adopt and implement your proposals, thereby fulfilling even a ten-thousandth part of the imperial benevolent intention.
Question: Those who study the Way take the sage as their standard. Earlier Confucian scholars have fully explained the successive stages of this work. Let us select one or two doubtful points for discussion together. Cultivating the Way depends on humaneness, and seeking humaneness rests on reciprocity. Explanations of humaneness are manifold, while the meaning of reciprocity has two applications. How does reciprocity relate to humaneness? It is said both that having a ruling principle makes the mind empty and that having a ruling principle makes it full. Are these statements not contradictory? Pursuing breadth of learning invites the suspicion of dissipating one's resolve through preoccupation with things; giving primacy to stillness comes close to leaving the mind unoccupied. Remaining confined to what is near and small restricts one and prevents expansion; pursuing what is lofty and remote leads to emptiness without substance. If framing a topic and entering into discussion [?] is said to show discernment, why should deliberately composing an essay harm the Way? Bringing things into accord with their single source is no easy matter: why, then, is differentiation said to be difficult? The principles of things certainly do not lie outside our concern: why, then, are practical achievements said to be harmful? The Master seldom spoke of human nature and destiny. Can those who say that human nature is not an urgent concern be condemned entirely? The forms of ritual are not simply inherited unchanged: are those who give priority to ritual teaching not rigidly attached to them? Master Yan described the sage's teaching in terms of broadening and restraining. Broadening pertains to literary learning, and restraining to virtuous conduct. Yet Master Yan was celebrated specifically for virtuous conduct. Was his learning different from that of later generations? You scholars…

title: 正德八年福建鄉試錄
text:
子希顏入聖必講之熟矣願明以告
我
問田有定分賦有定法此仁政之大者
夏商以前姑未暇論若成周徹法旣
已變商七十爲百畝矣及攷遂人與
漢志所載乃有百畝至三百畝者而
又受歸無常可謂有定分耶太宰旣
有九職又有九賦或謂賦爲口率出
錢似又過什一矣可謂有定法耶迨
===
井田法壞論者謂莫善於租庸調莫
不善於兩稅蓋一以丁夫爲本一以
資產爲宗以丁夫爲本則貧富不分
以資產爲宗則真僞難辨而必謂彼
善於此者何故其所以善所以不善
所以不得不變必有說也
國朝稽古致治田有步算而戶籍定賦有
常額而稅斂薄宜乎民物阜豐矣然
治久弊滋日以彌甚居下恒苦於兼
punctuated:
子希顏入聖，必講之熟矣，願明以告我。

問：田有定分，賦有定法，此仁政之大者。夏商以前，姑未暇論。若成周徹法，旣已變商七十爲百畝矣，及攷遂人與漢志所載，乃有百畝至三百畝者，而又受歸無常，可謂有定分耶？太宰旣有九職，又有九賦，或謂賦爲口率出錢，似又過什一矣，可謂有定法耶？迨井田法壞，論者謂莫善於租庸調，莫不善於兩稅。蓋一以丁夫爲本，一以資產爲宗。以丁夫爲本，則貧富不分；以資產爲宗，則真僞難辨。而必謂彼善於此者，何故？其所以善、所以不善、所以不得不變，必有說也。國朝稽古致治，田有步算而戶籍定，賦有常額而稅斂薄，宜乎民物阜豐矣。然治久弊滋，日以彌甚，居下恒苦於兼
translation_en:
…you candidates aspire to emulate Yan Hui and attain sagehood, and must have studied these matters thoroughly. I ask you to explain them clearly to me.

Question: Land has fixed allotments, and taxation has established rules: these are major elements of benevolent government. Let us leave aside for now the Xia, the Shang, and earlier times. Under the che system of the Zhou, the Shang allotment of seventy mu had already been changed to one hundred mu. Yet when we examine the section on the Director of the Outlying Districts and the treatise in the History of the Han, we find allotments ranging from one hundred to three hundred mu, with no constant rule governing their receipt and return. Can this be called a system of fixed allotments? The Grand Steward had the nine occupations as well as the nine levies. Some say that these levies were monetary payments assessed per person; this would seem to exceed the tithe. Can this be called an established system of taxation?

After the well-field system broke down, commentators held that no system was better than the grain tax, labor service or its commutation, and household levy (zu-yong-diao), and none worse than the Twice-Yearly Tax. The former took adult males as its basis, while the latter took assets as its foundation. Taking adult males as the basis fails to distinguish rich from poor; taking assets as the foundation makes it difficult to distinguish true declarations from false ones. Why, then, insist that the former was better than the latter? There must be an explanation of what made one good and the other bad, and why change became unavoidable.

Our dynasty has consulted antiquity in establishing good government. Land is measured and calculated, and household registers are settled; taxes have regular quotas, and collections are light. The people should therefore be prosperous and goods abundant. Yet, as government continues over time, abuses proliferate and grow worse by the day. Those below constantly suffer from encroachment…

title: 正德八年福建鄉試錄
text:
併供上每困於征求昔之患此者嘗
請行經界而竟拂羣議又有上政本
書而終不見用不知二者可行於今
否也苟難卒行則處之者終無術乎
諸士子其酌古準今以對
問守令親民之職自秦廢封建始置郡
縣而有之由漢而下代或更置殊其
名稱其倚之以成治則一也考之於
史有曰六條有曰八計有曰四事皆
===
所以稽吏治者而行之久近責之專
否亦或不同可歷舉其詳歟三代以
後言治者必曰漢唐宋至言守令之
賢又未嘗不以漢之循吏爲稱首漢
獨何以致此我
朝稽古建官愼擇守令而責成之以六事
又每歲各
命憲臣一員以巡察之又通計其舉否以爲
黜陟惠民之意至矣不知所謂六事
punctuated:
併，供上每困於征求。昔之患此者，嘗請行經界，而竟拂羣議；又有上《政本書》而終不見用。不知二者可行於今否也？苟難卒行，則處之者終無術乎？諸士子其酌古準今以對。
問：守令，親民之職，自秦廢封建，始置郡縣而有之。由漢而下，代或更置，殊其名稱，其倚之以成治則一也。考之於史，有曰六條，有曰八計，有曰四事，皆所以稽吏治者，而行之久近、責之專否，亦或不同。可歷舉其詳歟？三代以後，言治者必曰漢、唐、宋；至言守令之賢，又未嘗不以漢之循吏爲稱首。漢獨何以致此？我朝稽古建官，愼擇守令，而責成之以六事。又每歲各命憲臣一員以巡察之，又通計其舉否以爲黜陟，惠民之意至矣。不知所謂六事
translation_en:
…land engrossment, while providing for those above is continually made difficult by fiscal demands. Those who formerly worried about this once requested a survey and demarcation of landholdings, but their proposal ultimately ran counter to prevailing opinion. There was also someone who submitted the Book on the Foundations of Government (Zhengben shu), but it was never put to use. Could these two proposals be implemented today? If they are difficult to implement immediately, must those dealing with the problem remain without any means of addressing it? You candidates should weigh ancient precedents against present circumstances in your replies.
Question: Prefects and county magistrates hold offices that deal directly with the people. These offices originated when the Qin abolished feudal enfeoffment and first established commanderies and counties. From the Han onward, successive dynasties sometimes altered these offices and gave them different names, but their reliance on them to achieve good government remained the same. Examining the histories, we find references to the Six Articles, the Eight Criteria, and the Four Matters, all means of assessing officials’ administration. Yet how long they were in force and whether responsibility was assigned exclusively also differed. Can you enumerate their particulars? When discussing good government after the Three Dynasties, one invariably names the Han, Tang, and Song; when discussing worthy prefects and county magistrates, one invariably gives first place to the Han’s exemplary officials. How did the Han, in particular, achieve this? Our dynasty has consulted antiquity in establishing offices, carefully selected prefects and county magistrates, and held them accountable for results in six matters. Each year it also commissions one censor for each jurisdiction to conduct inspections, and assesses the officials’ overall performance as the basis for dismissal or promotion. Its intention to benefit the people is most thorough indeed. As for these so-called six matters…

title: 正德八年福建鄉試錄
text:
者與漢唐宋之法亦有同歟我
朝立法之善宜非前代所能及者而近年
以來吏或未能盡稱其職民或未能
盡安其業其故何歟今欲使天下之
守令皆無愧於漢之循吏而田里亦
無不安之民何如而可願悉陳之毋
隱
punctuated: 者，與漢唐宋之法亦有同歟？我朝立法之善，宜非前代所能及者，而近年以來，吏或未能盡稱其職，民或未能盡安其業，其故何歟？今欲使天下之守令皆無愧於漢之循吏，而田里亦無不安之民，何如而可？願悉陳之，毋隱。
translation_en: …do these also have anything in common with the regulations of the Han, Tang, and Song dynasties? The excellence of our dynasty’s laws should surpass anything earlier dynasties could achieve. Yet in recent years, some officials have failed to fulfill all the duties of their offices, and some people have been unable to pursue their livelihoods in peace. Why is this? If we now wish to ensure that all prefects and county magistrates throughout the realm measure up to the exemplary officials of the Han, and that no one in the countryside lacks peace and security, how can this be achieved? Please set forth your views fully, concealing nothing.
