text:
第壹場
四書
赫兮喧兮者威儀也
張岳
同考試官訓導王批盛德之容未易模寫
此作味嘆淫泆如親炙君子之有斐者可嘉
同考試官學正陳批說得可畏可象意思明白
考試官教諭沈批講赫喧處不窘不複允宜錄出
考試官學正魏批得傳者釋詩意
===
大學引詩言君子外之著者乃其容之盛也
蓋容者德之符也君子德既盛矣則容之著
於外者有不極其盛哉大學傳之三章引衛
風淇澳之詩而釋之以明明德者止於至善
及此蓋謂君子於至善也求之既有其方得
之豈無其驗彼詩言君子之有斐不能以自
秘也日見夫華采之呈露不容以自遏也日
見夫光輝之發越布濩流行於一身之內而
足以炳示乎斯民何其赫耶洋溢充滿於四
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

赫兮喧兮者，威儀也。

張岳

同考試官訓導王批：盛德之容，未易模寫。此作味嘆淫泆，如親炙君子之有斐者，可嘉。

同考試官學正陳批：說得可畏可象意思明白。

考試官教諭沈批：講赫喧處，不窘不複，允宜錄出。

考試官學正魏批：得傳者釋詩意。

《大學》引《詩》，言君子外之著者，乃其容之盛也。蓋容者，德之符也。君子德既盛矣，則容之著於外者，有不極其盛哉？《大學》傳之三章，引《衛風》《淇澳》之詩而釋之，以明明德者止於至善。及此，蓋謂君子於至善也，求之既有其方，得之豈無其驗？彼《詩》言君子之有斐，不能以自秘也，日見夫華采之呈露；不容以自遏也，日見夫光輝之發越。布濩流行於一身之內，而足以炳示乎斯民，何其赫耶！洋溢充滿於四
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

“‘Resplendent and glorious’ refers to his awe-inspiring bearing and exemplary deportment.”

Zhang Yue

Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Assistant Instructor: The outward bearing of abundant virtue is not easily depicted. This composition savors and praises it with overflowing feeling [?], as though its author had personally received the influence of the refined gentleman. Commendable.

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: It clearly explains the sense of inspiring awe and providing a model for others.

Comment by Examiner Shen, Instructor: Its discussion of “resplendent and glorious” is neither constrained nor repetitive. It certainly deserves to be selected for inclusion.

Comment by Examiner Wei, Instructor: It captures the intent with which the author of the commentary explains the poem.

The Great Learning quotes the Book of Odes to say that what is outwardly manifest in the gentleman is the fullness of his bearing. For bearing is the outward sign of virtue. Once the gentleman’s virtue is abundant, how could his outwardly manifest bearing fail to attain its utmost fullness? The third chapter of the commentary to the Great Learning quotes and explains the poem “The Bend of the Qi” from the “Airs of Wei,” to show that those who illuminate their luminous virtue rest in the highest good. At this point, its meaning is surely this: since the gentleman has a method for seeking the highest good, could his attainment of it lack confirming signs? The poem speaks of the gentleman’s refinement: he cannot keep it concealed, and daily one sees his splendid colors revealed; he cannot restrain it, and daily one sees his radiance shining forth. Spreading and circulating throughout his person, it suffices to shine visibly before the people. How resplendent he is! Overflowing and filling his four…

title: 正德八年福建鄉試錄
text:
體之間而足以昭著於下國何其喧耶詩之
言如此果何謂耶蓋言夫威以示畏也而君
子盛德之著則有所謂威焉巍而整者其衣
冠也端而肅者其瞻視也儼然於正位之居
而君人之軌範以立真有若神明之陟降可
敬而不可狎見焉者有不自阻而懾乎儀以
示象也而君子盛德之著則有所謂儀焉輯
柔以和者其容止也委蛇以適者其進退也
秩然於日用之著而君子之容節已具真有
===
若日星之煥耀可仰而亦可度慕焉者有不
覩之爲快乎是則詩之所謂赫喧而有徵於
威儀如此則君子止至善之驗著矣謂非學
問自脩中來耶抑因是而論之人受天地之
中以生所謂命也足以有動作威儀之則以
定命也威儀之係於人也亦大矣故衛武公
一國之君也當耄耋之年猶作詩以自警而
於威儀之敬慎者尤拳拳焉其所慮者遠矣
况夫有天下者又當何如耶從事於大學而
punctuated:
體之間，而足以昭著於下國，何其喧耶！詩之言如此，果何謂耶？蓋言夫威以示畏也，而君子盛德之著，則有所謂威焉。巍而整者，其衣冠也；端而肅者，其瞻視也。儼然於正位之居，而君人之軌範以立，真有若神明之陟降，可敬而不可狎。見焉者，有不自阻而懾乎？儀以示象也，而君子盛德之著，則有所謂儀焉。輯柔以和者，其容止也；委蛇以適者，其進退也。秩然於日用之著，而君子之容節已具，真有若日星之煥耀，可仰而亦可度。慕焉者，有不覩之爲快乎？是則詩之所謂赫喧，而有徵於威儀如此，則君子止至善之驗著矣。謂非學問自脩中來耶？

抑因是而論之，人受天地之中以生，所謂命也；足以有動作威儀之則，以定命也。威儀之係於人也亦大矣。故衛武公，一國之君也，當耄耋之年，猶作詩以自警，而於威儀之敬慎者尤拳拳焉，其所慮者遠矣。况夫有天下者，又當何如耶？從事於大學，而
translation_en:
…throughout his limbs, sufficiently manifest to shine forth among the realms below—how resplendent it is! What, precisely, do these words of the poem mean? Majesty inspires awe, and in the manifestation of the gentleman’s abundant virtue there is what we call majesty. Lofty and orderly are his robes and cap; composed and solemn is his gaze. Dignified in occupying his proper position, he establishes a model for the ruler of men. Truly, he resembles divine spirits ascending and descending: worthy of reverence, but admitting no undue familiarity. Could anyone who sees him fail to check himself and feel awe? Deportment presents a model, and in the manifestation of the gentleman’s abundant virtue there is what we call deportment. Gentle and harmonious is his bearing; easy and unforced are his movements, whether advancing or withdrawing. Order is manifest in his daily conduct, and the gentleman’s regulated bearing is fully realized. Truly, he resembles the radiance of sun and stars: one may look up to him and also take him as a measure. Could anyone who admires him fail to delight in beholding him? Thus the brilliance and resplendence spoken of in the poem find confirmation in majesty and deportment in this way, making evident the proof that the gentleman rests in the highest good. Could one say that this does not come from learning, inquiry, and self-cultivation?

To pursue the matter further: people receive the balanced principle of Heaven and Earth at birth; this is what is called their allotted endowment. It enables them to possess standards for movement, majesty, and deportment, by which to secure that endowment. Majesty and deportment therefore have a great bearing upon human life. Thus Duke Wu of Wei, the ruler of a single state, still composed a poem to admonish himself when already in his eighties or nineties. He was particularly earnest about reverence and care in majesty and deportment: his concerns reached far into the future. How much more, then, must be required of one who possesses all under Heaven? By devoting himself to the Great Learning and…

title: 正德八年福建鄉試錄
text:
所以致其力者如武公焉則亦庶乎其可也
多聞擇其善者而從之多見而識之
劉世揚
同考試官訓導方批此題似易而難非嘗
從事於博約之學者不能言之至此
同考試官訓導劉批講閒見從識處明當可嘉
考試官教諭沈批理明詞暢
考試官學正魏批發明聖人論知之事始盡
博所聞而取之精博所見而記之備聖人自
===
言然也蓋聞見者知之資也夫旣博矣而又
取之精記之備焉知之道其庶幾矣乎聖人
謙已誨人之意如此蓋謂不知而作我固無
是矣然豈可諉之不知而已耶彼天下之理
無窮而寓於聞者衆矣不有所聞固無以發
吾之聰然聞矣而或局於寡陋亦豈足以盡
其知哉吾則廣其所聽自師友之論難以極
於載籍之浩繁蓋有囊括而不遺者是則所
謂多聞矣然擇之不精寧無泛濫之失乎又
punctuated:
所以致其力者如武公焉，則亦庶乎其可也。

多聞，擇其善者而從之；多見而識之。
劉世揚

同考試官訓導方批：此題似易而難，非嘗從事於博約之學者，不能言之至此。
同考試官訓導劉批：講閒見從識處，明當可嘉。
考試官教諭沈批：理明詞暢。
考試官學正魏批：發明聖人論知之事始盡。

博所聞而取之精，博所見而記之備，聖人自言然也。蓋聞見者，知之資也。夫旣博矣，而又取之精、記之備焉，知之道其庶幾矣乎！聖人謙已誨人之意如此。蓋謂不知而作，我固無是矣，然豈可諉之不知而已耶？彼天下之理無窮，而寓於聞者衆矣。不有所聞，固無以發吾之聰；然聞矣，而或局於寡陋，亦豈足以盡其知哉？吾則廣其所聽，自師友之論難，以極於載籍之浩繁，蓋有囊括而不遺者，是則所謂多聞矣。然擇之不精，寧無泛濫之失乎？又
translation_en:
…if one applies oneself as did Duke Wu, then one may come close to accomplishing it.

“Hear much, select what is good and follow it; see much and remember it.”
Liu Shiyang 劉世揚

Associate Examiner Fang, Assistant Instructor, comments: “This topic seems easy but is difficult. Anyone who has not engaged in learning that combines breadth with restraint could not have expressed it so fully.”
Associate Examiner Liu, Assistant Instructor, comments: “The exposition [?] brings out the points concerning following and remembering; it is clear, apt, and commendable.”
Examiner Shen, Instructor, comments: “The principles are clear and the language flows smoothly.”
Examiner Wei, School Instructor, comments: “Only here is the sage’s discussion of knowing fully elucidated.”

To hear broadly yet select with discrimination, and to see broadly yet remember comprehensively—this is what the sage said of himself. Hearing and seeing are the resources of knowledge. Once these are broad, if one also selects with discrimination and remembers comprehensively, surely one approaches the way of knowing! Such was the sage’s intention in speaking humbly of himself to instruct others. He meant: “Acting without knowing—I certainly do not do this. Yet how could one simply plead ignorance and leave it at that?” The principles of all under Heaven are inexhaustible, and many are embodied in what one hears. Without hearing anything, I would certainly have no means of developing my discernment. Yet even after hearing, if I remained confined by scant and shallow learning, how could I fully realize my knowledge? I therefore broaden what I hear, ranging from discussions and debates with teachers and friends to the vast abundance of written records, encompassing all and omitting nothing. This is what is meant by hearing much. Yet if selection is insufficiently discriminating, how could one avoid the fault of indiscriminate diffusion? Moreover …

title: 正德八年福建鄉試錄
text:
必擬議詳審求夫至當歸一之論其善在彼
也而吾即之以為據守焉雚度精切究夫可
久不易之道其善在此也而吾取之以為持
循焉善者從之則惡者在所畧矣天下之理
無盡而寓於見者衆矣不有所見固無以啓
吾之明然見矣而或狃於淺近亦豈足以致
其知哉吾則廣其所覽自日用之應酬以極
於宇宙之變化蓋有網羅而無外者是則所
謂多見矣然識之不備寧無疎略之失乎又
===
必合善與惡皆歛而藏之於廣大悉備之中
以俟參考於他日焉兼惡與善皆默而識之
於寬裕有容之地以俟決擇於將來焉善惡
皆記則惡者亦可鑒矣是則擇善於多聞之
中能識於多見之後則理雖不能盡知而亦
可次於知矣尚何妄作之有哉雖然夫子嘗
以多學而識發子貢之問矣今觀此言乃若
敎人以務博者何歟蓋一以貫之道之體也
學之者必先於博而後可以語約博固所以
punctuated: 必擬議詳審，求夫至當歸一之論。其善在彼也，而吾即之以為據守焉；雚度精切，究夫可久不易之道。其善在此也，而吾取之以為持循焉。善者從之，則惡者在所畧矣。天下之理無盡，而寓於見者衆矣。不有所見，固無以啓吾之明；然見矣，而或狃於淺近，亦豈足以致其知哉？吾則廣其所覽，自日用之應酬，以極於宇宙之變化，蓋有網羅而無外者，是則所謂多見矣。然識之不備，寧無疎略之失乎？又必合善與惡，皆歛而藏之於廣大悉備之中，以俟參考於他日焉；兼惡與善，皆默而識之於寬裕有容之地，以俟決擇於將來焉。善惡皆記，則惡者亦可鑒矣。是則擇善於多聞之中，能識於多見之後，則理雖不能盡知，而亦可次於知矣，尚何妄作之有哉？雖然，夫子嘗以多學而識發子貢之問矣。今觀此言，乃若敎人以務博者，何歟？蓋一以貫之，道之體也。學之者必先於博，而後可以語約，博固所以
translation_en:
…must deliberate carefully and examine thoroughly, seeking an account that is perfectly fitting and converges upon a single conclusion. Wherever goodness lies in those things, I approach it and make it a basis to hold fast to; I scrutinize and assess precisely [?], investigating the Way that can endure without change. Wherever goodness lies in these things, I adopt it as a rule to uphold and follow. When one follows what is good, what is bad may be passed over.

The principles of the world are inexhaustible, and many are embodied in what one sees. Without seeing anything, I would certainly have no means to awaken my understanding. Yet if, having seen, I remain confined by habit to what is superficial and close at hand, how could that suffice to bring my knowledge to its fullest extent? I therefore broaden what I observe, from the interactions of daily life to the transformations of the universe, encompassing everything and leaving nothing outside. This is what is meant by seeing much. Yet if one does not retain it comprehensively, how could one avoid the fault of careless omission? One must also gather together both good and bad, storing them within a capacious and comprehensive mind, to await comparison and examination another day; embracing bad together with good, one must silently commit both to memory within a generous and accommodating mind, to await judgment and selection in the future. When good and bad are both recorded, even the bad can serve as a warning.

Thus, if one selects what is good from the many things heard and can retain the many things seen, then, though one cannot know all principles exhaustively, one can attain the rank next to knowledge. What scope would remain for acting rashly? Nevertheless, the Master once prompted Zigong to ask a question by speaking of learning much and retaining it. Now, looking at these words, he seems to teach people to pursue breadth. Why is this? It is because threading all things together with a single principle is the essential substance of the Way. Those who study it must first attain breadth before they can be spoken to about its essentials. Breadth is indeed the means by which…

title: 正德八年福建鄉試錄
text:
為約之地耳欲學之博舍聞見之廣其何以
哉然曰擇曰識則亦非徒務博者矣聖人教
人下學上達其序固如此云
仁之實事親是也義之實從兄是也智
之實知斯二者弗去是也禮之實節
文斯二者是也樂之實樂斯二者樂
則生矣生則惡可已也惡可已則不
知足之蹈之手之舞之
廖雲龍
===
同考試官訓導劉批說出事親從兄之
大典所以體於身者親切有味蓋讀孟而有得者
同考試官教諭羅批讀其文亦若至手舞足蹈之為可喜
考試官教諭沈批義理文字實自胸中流出
考試官學正魏批辭整意完
大賢既言道之實而不越乎孝弟必推道之
實而皆體乎孝弟蓋孝弟乃良心之真切者
也仁義之實固不越此矣而智禮樂之實豈
非所以體之也哉昔孟子之意謂夫天下之
punctuated:
為約之地耳。欲學之博，舍聞見之廣，其何以哉？然曰擇、曰識，則亦非徒務博者矣。聖人教人下學上達，其序固如此云。

仁之實，事親是也；義之實，從兄是也；智之實，知斯二者弗去是也；禮之實，節文斯二者是也；樂之實，樂斯二者，樂則生矣；生則惡可已也？惡可已，則不知足之蹈之、手之舞之。

廖雲龍

同考試官訓導劉批：說出事親從兄之大典，所以體於身者，親切有味，蓋讀孟而有得者。

同考試官教諭羅批：讀其文，亦若至手舞足蹈之，為可喜。

考試官教諭沈批：義理文字，實自胸中流出。

考試官學正魏批：辭整意完。

大賢既言道之實而不越乎孝弟，必推道之實而皆體乎孝弟。蓋孝弟乃良心之真切者也，仁義之實固不越此矣，而智禮樂之實豈非所以體之也哉？昔孟子之意，謂夫天下之
translation_en:
…serves as the foundation for a concise grasp, nothing more. If one wishes to make one’s learning broad, how can one do so without breadth in what one hears and sees? Yet the words “select” and “remember” show that this is not merely a pursuit of breadth. In teaching people to learn through everyday matters and attain higher understanding, the sage’s sequence is indeed like this.

“The substance of benevolence is serving one’s parents; the substance of righteousness is following one’s elder brothers. The substance of wisdom is knowing these two things and not departing from them. The substance of ritual propriety is regulating and embellishing these two things. The substance of music is taking joy in these two things. With joy they flourish; once they flourish, how can they be stopped? When they cannot be stopped, one’s feet begin to stamp and one’s hands to dance without one’s knowing it.”

Liao Yunlong 廖雲龍

Comment by Associate Examiner Liu, Assistant Instructor: He explains the great norms of serving one’s parents and following one’s elder brothers. His account of how to embody them personally is intimate and rich in meaning. He is evidently someone who has gained understanding from reading the Mencius.

Comment by Associate Examiner Luo, Instructor: Reading his essay, one likewise seems brought to the point of dancing with one’s hands and stamping one’s feet. How delightful!

Comment by Examiner Shen, Instructor: The moral principles and the writing truly flow from his own heart.

Comment by Examiner Wei, Instructor: The language is orderly and the meaning complete.

Having stated that the substance of the Way does not extend beyond filial devotion and respect for elder brothers, the great worthy must further expound the substance of the Way, showing how it is embodied entirely in filial devotion and fraternal respect. For these are the most genuine and immediate expressions of the innate moral heart. The substance of benevolence and righteousness certainly does not extend beyond them; and are not the substance of wisdom, ritual propriety, and music likewise the means of embodying them? Mencius’s meaning was that, of all under Heaven’s …

title: 正德八年福建鄉試錄
text:
道不同而孝弟之務爲急是故仁道也凡愛
焉者皆夫仁之用矣然仁主於愛而天性之
恩則其所最切者仁之實不在於事親乎義
亦道也凡敬焉者皆夫義之用矣然義主於
敬而因心之友則其所最先者義之實不在
於從兄乎仁義之實不越乎孝弟如此自是
而智而禮而樂亦皆道也顧孰非所以體此
者哉故智固無乎不知也智之實則惟究極
乎斯二者真見夫親之當事也真見夫兄之
===
當從也爲之確焉以守終吾之身而有弗去
焉者此矣禮固無乎不節也而禮之實則惟
節文乎斯二者親不徒以事也兄不徒以從
也爲之秩然以辨致吾之委曲而復有燦焉
者此矣樂亦無乎不樂也而其所謂實者亦
惟樂斯二者和順於愛敬之間而無所矯拂
從容於事從之際而無所勉強樂則有根乎
其中而孝弟之意自油然以生矣生則有動
於其機而孝弟之意自藹然不可已矣不可
punctuated: 道不同，而孝弟之務爲急。是故仁，道也，凡愛焉者，皆夫仁之用矣。然仁主於愛，而天性之恩則其所最切者，仁之實不在於事親乎？義亦道也，凡敬焉者，皆夫義之用矣。然義主於敬，而因心之友則其所最先者，義之實不在於從兄乎？仁義之實不越乎孝弟如此，自是而智而禮而樂，亦皆道也，顧孰非所以體此者哉？故智固無乎不知也，智之實則惟究極乎斯二者，真見夫親之當事也，真見夫兄之當從也，爲之確焉以守，終吾之身而有弗去焉者，此矣。禮固無乎不節也，而禮之實則惟節文乎斯二者，親不徒以事也，兄不徒以從也，爲之秩然以辨，致吾之委曲而復有燦焉者，此矣。樂亦無乎不樂也，而其所謂實者亦惟樂斯二者，和順於愛敬之間而無所矯拂，從容於事從之際而無所勉強。樂則有根乎其中，而孝弟之意自油然以生矣；生則有動於其機，而孝弟之意自藹然不可已矣。不可
translation_en:
…the ways differ, yet the practice of filial devotion and fraternal deference is most urgent. Thus benevolence is a way, and every act of love is an expression of benevolence. Yet benevolence centers on love, and affection arising from our natural endowment is its most intimate concern. Does not the substance of benevolence lie in serving one’s parents? Righteousness, too, is a way, and every act of respect is an expression of righteousness. Yet righteousness centers on respect, and brotherly affection arising from the heart comes foremost. Does not the substance of righteousness lie in following one’s elder brothers? In this manner, the substance of benevolence and righteousness does not extend beyond filial devotion and fraternal deference. Wisdom, ritual propriety, and music are likewise ways: which of them does not serve to embody these two duties?

Wisdom certainly leaves nothing unknown, yet its substance lies solely in thoroughly comprehending these two duties: truly seeing that one’s parents ought to be served and that one’s elder brothers ought to be followed. Holding firmly to them and never departing from them throughout one’s life—this is its substance. Ritual propriety certainly leaves nothing unregulated, yet its substance lies solely in regulating and giving fitting form to these two duties. Parents are not merely to be served, nor elder brothers merely to be followed. Making orderly distinctions in these duties, attending fully to their finer details, and thereby giving them manifest beauty—this is its substance. Music, too, leaves nothing without joy, yet what is called its substance lies solely in delighting in these two duties. In love and respect there is harmony and accord, without distortion or resistance; in serving parents and following elder brothers there is ease, without forced effort. With joy taking root within, the impulse toward filial devotion and fraternal deference naturally wells forth. As it arises, its inner spring is stirred, and this impulse naturally flourishes so abundantly that it cannot cease. Unable to…

title: 正德八年福建鄉試錄
text:
已而又盛焉則形於足蹈手舞之餘而皆自
得於至樂流通之會寧知其所以蹈且舞哉
蓋至是而孝弟之理已具而吾之妙契於孝
弟者亦至矣然非知之明而守之固又何以
節之密而樂之深哉雖然論道有全體入道
有次序全體固不可偏廢入道而失其序焉
亦未有能會其全者故有子以孝弟爲爲仁
之本而又以本立道生爲言孟子此章之論
意或出此然則學者誠能從事於所謂事親
===
從兄焉固亦將有得其實而兼舉其華者矣
易
君子之光有孚吉
劉世揚
同考試官訓導方批題本平易不難於
作但多不見君子濟世之心此作得之是宜錄出
同考試官訓導劉批此題作者多以光孚
於孚纏冗不潔體貼本義以成文惟此篇爲最
考試官教諭沈批發明君德功效自源
punctuated:
已而又盛焉，則形於足蹈手舞之餘，而皆自得於至樂流通之會，寧知其所以蹈且舞哉？蓋至是而孝弟之理已具，而吾之妙契於孝弟者亦至矣。然非知之明而守之固，又何以節之密而樂之深哉？雖然，論道有全體，入道有次序。全體固不可偏廢，入道而失其序焉，亦未有能會其全者。故有子以孝弟爲爲仁之本，而又以本立道生爲言。孟子此章之論，意或出此。然則學者誠能從事於所謂事親從兄焉，固亦將有得其實而兼舉其華者矣。
易
君子之光，有孚，吉。
劉世揚
同考試官訓導方批：「題本平易，不難於作，但多不見君子濟世之心。此作得之，是宜錄出。」
同考試官訓導劉批：「此題作者多以光孚於孚，纏冗不潔。體貼本義以成文，惟此篇爲最。」
考試官教諭沈批：「發明君德功效，自源
translation_en:
…and, growing still more abundant, it finds expression in the dancing of the feet and waving of the hands. All comes spontaneously at the point where supreme joy flows freely: how could one know what makes one dance and wave one’s hands? At this point, the principles of filial devotion and fraternal deference are fully realized, and my subtle accord with them has also reached its utmost. Yet without understanding them clearly and holding firmly to them, how could one regulate them so precisely through ritual and take such profound joy in them? Nevertheless, discussing the Way involves its entirety, while entering the Way involves a sequence. Certainly no part of that entirety may be neglected; yet no one who loses the proper sequence in entering the Way has ever been able to comprehend it as a whole. Thus Youzi regarded filial devotion and fraternal deference as the root of practicing benevolence, and also said that when the root is established, the Way grows. The purport of Mencius’s discussion in this chapter may derive from this. If students can truly devote themselves to what is called serving their parents and deferring to their elder brothers, they will surely grasp its substance while also bringing forth its flourishing expression.
Book of Changes
“The gentleman’s radiance: there is sincerity; auspicious.”
Liu Shiyang
Associate Examiner Fang, Assistant Instructor, comments: “The topic is straightforward and easy, and not difficult to write on. Yet most answers fail to reveal the gentleman’s desire to bring succor to the world. This answer captures it and therefore deserves to be recorded.”
Associate Examiner Liu, Assistant Instructor, comments: “Most who write on this topic take radiance as inspiring trust in sincerity [?], becoming tangled and verbose, without clarity. For composing an essay through close appreciation of the original meaning, this piece alone is the best.”
Examiner Shen, Instructor, comments: “It elucidates the efficacy of the ruler’s virtue, beginning from its source…

title: 正德八年福建鄉試錄
text:
祖委曲不苟作者
考試官學正魏批文得精微之旨
具君人之大德成濟世之大功爻易之旨焫
也蓋濟世者必有德而後可也六五之德光
而有孚其成功之大也宜哉周公繫未濟六
五之辭及此蓋謂君子不患於時之難濟而
患於德之未全何則六五君子以柔順而爲
文明之主又虛中以應九二之賢固能貞吉
且无悔矣然文明之德非徒蘊積而已也其
===
形於外者自有英華發越之美焉志不舍命
而章之含者溢而爲綱紀法度之施明不可
晦而膏之屯者達而爲經綸匡濟之業蔚然
炳然日新而不已其爲光也何盛邪虛中之
德非徒勉強而已也其在於我者則有誠意
懇切之美焉自信之真而設施舉措有非聲
音笑貌之所爲以益爲志而翕受敷宣莫非
精神心術之所運攣如交如至實而不妄其
爲孚也何盛邪君子妙乎是德於已則濟世
punctuated:
祖，委曲不苟，作者。
考試官學正魏批：文得精微之旨。
具君人之大德，成濟世之大功，爻易之旨焫也。蓋濟世者必有德而後可也。六五之德，光而有孚，其成功之大也宜哉！周公繫未濟六五之辭及此，蓋謂君子不患於時之難濟，而患於德之未全。何則？六五君子以柔順而爲文明之主，又虛中以應九二之賢，固能貞吉且无悔矣。然文明之德，非徒蘊積而已也。其形於外者，自有英華發越之美焉。志不舍命，而章之含者溢而爲綱紀法度之施；明不可晦，而膏之屯者達而爲經綸匡濟之業。蔚然炳然，日新而不已，其爲光也何盛邪！虛中之德，非徒勉強而已也。其在於我者，則有誠意懇切之美焉。自信之真，而設施舉措有非聲音笑貌之所爲；以益爲志，而翕受敷宣莫非精神心術之所運。攣如交如，至實而不妄，其爲孚也何盛邪！君子妙乎是德於已，則濟世
translation_en:
… its source [?], with thoroughness and care: the work of an accomplished writer.

Examiner Wei, School Instructor, comments: “The composition captures the subtle and profound purport.”

To possess the great virtue of a ruler of men and accomplish the great work of bringing deliverance to the world—such is the purport of this line in the Changes [?]. For one must possess virtue before one can bring deliverance to the world. The virtue of the six in the fifth place is radiant and sincere: how fitting that its accomplishment should be great! When the Duke of Zhou appended these words to the six in the fifth place of Before Completion, he meant that the gentleman worries not that the times make deliverance difficult, but that his virtue is not yet complete. Why is this? The gentleman represented by the six in the fifth place is yielding and compliant, yet serves as the lord of cultivated brilliance. Moreover, with an open heart he responds to the worthy man represented by the nine in the second place. He can assuredly remain steadfast and attain good fortune, without regret.

Yet the virtue of cultivated brilliance does not merely accumulate within. When it takes outward form, it naturally displays the beauty of splendid efflorescence. His resolve does not forsake his mandate; the distinction held within overflows into the implementation of guiding principles, laws, and standards. His brightness cannot be obscured; his stored bounty flows forth into the work of ordering affairs, setting things right, and bringing deliverance. Flourishing and resplendent, it renews itself daily without cease. How abundant is its radiance!

The virtue of an open heart, moreover, is not merely a matter of exerting oneself. Within oneself, it possesses the beauty of earnest and heartfelt sincerity. From the genuineness of his inward assurance, his measures and actions achieve what voice, laughter, and outward manner cannot accomplish. With the aim of benefiting others, his receptive gathering and expansive dissemination alike proceed from the workings of his spirit and heart. Bound together and joined in mutual fellowship, utterly real and without falsehood—how abundant is his sincerity!

When the gentleman realizes this virtue consummately within himself, then the means of bringing deliverance to the world …

title: 正德八年福建鄉試錄
text:
之具自我而全矣吾知其光之所及既有以
燭乎羣動而孚之所感又有以發乎衆志向
雖汔濟未出乎中矣今知其極而變焉觀人
文之宜圖嚮明之治百姓可以昭明也天下
可以化成也所謂光被四表者有之吉之大
來也而豈倖得乎昔雖欲濟不續其終矣今
知其怠而勉焉因孚號之厲敦化邦之道四
方以之風動也萬邦以之作孚也所謂惠我
以德者有之吉之洊至也而豈徒然乎夫德
===
者功之本功者德之推德盛而功自見矣周
公以是繫爻其意精矣乎抑又考之六五以
陰居陽亦非正者今復於正而光與孚且極
其盛焉是亦何修而致此哉蓋其文明知乎
正理而又虛心下求得正人以為之輔其所
以交修之者至矣故匪徒正之可復德亦因
以益著學問之功其大有如此觀太甲成王
初亦不能無過而卒至於圖惟厥終克念作
聖是固其自知之明而交修之功亦有不可
punctuated: 之具自我而全矣。吾知其光之所及，既有以燭乎羣動，而孚之所感，又有以發乎衆志。向雖汔濟，未出乎中矣；今知其極而變焉，觀人文之宜，圖嚮明之治，百姓可以昭明也，天下可以化成也。所謂光被四表者有之，吉之大來也，而豈倖得乎？昔雖欲濟，不續其終矣；今知其怠而勉焉，因孚號之厲，敦化邦之道，四方以之風動也，萬邦以之作孚也。所謂惠我以德者有之，吉之洊至也，而豈徒然乎？夫德者，功之本；功者，德之推。德盛而功自見矣。周公以是繫爻，其意精矣乎！抑又考之，六五以陰居陽，亦非正者。今復於正，而光與孚且極其盛焉，是亦何修而致此哉？蓋其文明，知乎正理，而又虛心下求，得正人以為之輔，其所以交修之者至矣。故匪徒正之可復，德亦因以益著。學問之功，其大有如此！觀太甲、成王，初亦不能無過，而卒至於圖惟厥終、克念作聖，是固其自知之明，而交修之功亦有不可
translation_en:
…the means of bringing order to the world are thus made complete within oneself. I know that wherever his radiance reaches, it can illuminate the manifold movements of things, while the influence of his sincerity can awaken the aspirations of the multitude. Previously, although almost across the stream, he had not yet emerged from its midst. Now, recognizing the limit of his situation, he changes: he considers the fitting patterns of human culture and plans a government turned toward the light. The common people can thereby be enlightened, and all under Heaven transformed and perfected. What is called “radiance extending to the four quarters” is realized here. Great good fortune comes—how could it be obtained by mere luck? Previously, although wishing to cross, he did not carry the undertaking through to its end. Now, recognizing his indolence, he exerts himself. He heeds the danger signaled by a sincere cry and earnestly pursues the Way of transforming the states. The four quarters respond as if moved by the wind, and the myriad states are stirred to trust. What is called “benefiting me with virtue” is realized here. Good fortune arrives repeatedly—how could this happen without cause? Virtue is the root of achievement; achievement is the extension of virtue. When virtue flourishes, achievement naturally becomes manifest. How subtle was the intent of the Duke of Zhou in appending these words to the line!

Yet consider further: the Six in the Fifth Place, a yin line occupying a yang position, is itself not correctly placed. Now it returns to correctness, and its radiance and sincerity attain their fullest flourishing. Through what cultivation has this been achieved? Its civilized clarity enables it to understand correct principles; moreover, it humbly seeks assistance from those below and obtains upright people as helpers. The mutual cultivation thus undertaken is most thorough. Hence not only can correctness be restored, but virtue also becomes increasingly manifest through it. Such is the greatness of what learning accomplishes! Consider Tai Jia and King Cheng: neither was free of faults at the beginning, yet in the end they attained the states described as “taking thought for the outcome” and “being mindful and becoming a sage.” This certainly reflects the clarity of their self-knowledge, but the contribution of mutual cultivation also cannot be…

title: 正德八年福建鄉試錄
text:
誣者讀是文者合而觀之可也
夫易聖人之所以極深而研幾也唯深
也故能通天下之志唯幾也故能成
天下之務唯神也故不疾而速不行
而至子曰易有聖人之道四焉者此
之謂也
丘道隆
同考試官訓導方批夫易以下正見易
具聖道末二句但指以示人耳此作發揮真切獨冠本房
===
同考試官訓導劉批題有理絡作者多
支屬而意不相承此篇理明辭順首尾照應蓋深於
易學者
考試官教諭沈批聖人作易之用發揮殆盡
考試官學正魏批文雅義精
易作於聖人而極其用之妙此易所以具乎
聖道也蓋易之作固有以妙其用也聖人之
道夫豈外於是哉宜大傳言之以示人也且
易之用雖妙於天下而易之作實原於聖人
punctuated:
誣者。讀是文者，合而觀之可也。

夫《易》，聖人之所以極深而研幾也。唯深也，故能通天下之志；唯幾也，故能成天下之務；唯神也，故不疾而速，不行而至。子曰：「《易》有聖人之道四焉」者，此之謂也。

丘道隆

同考試官訓導方批：「夫易」以下，正見《易》具聖道，末二句但指以示人耳。此作發揮真切，獨冠本房。

同考試官訓導劉批：題有理絡，作者多支屬而意不相承。此篇理明辭順，首尾照應，蓋深於《易》學者。

考試官教諭沈批：聖人作《易》之用，發揮殆盡。

考試官學正魏批：文雅義精。

《易》作於聖人，而極其用之妙，此《易》所以具乎聖道也。蓋《易》之作，固有以妙其用也。聖人之道，夫豈外於是哉？宜《大傳》言之以示人也。且《易》之用雖妙於天下，而《易》之作實原於聖人。
translation_en:
…cannot be denied. Those who read this essay may consider these points together.

“The Changes is the means by which the sages plumb the depths and investigate the incipient. Only through depth can they comprehend the intentions of all under Heaven; only through understanding the incipient can they accomplish the affairs of all under Heaven; only through spiritual efficacy can they be swift without haste and arrive without traveling. The Master said, ‘The Changes contains four ways of the sages’: this is what he meant.”

Qiu Daolong

Comment by Associate Examiner Fang, Assistant Instructor: The passage beginning ‘The Changes’ directly shows that the Changes embodies the Way of the sages; the final two clauses merely point this out to the reader. This essay’s exposition is true and incisive, and it stands alone as the best in this examining section.

Comment by Associate Examiner Liu, Assistant Instructor: The topic has a coherent thread of principle. Most writers branch into loosely connected points [?], without continuity of meaning. In this essay, the principles are clear and the language flows smoothly; its beginning and end correspond. Its author is evidently deeply versed in the study of the Changes.

Comment by Examiner Shen, Instructor: The purposes for which the sages composed the Changes are expounded almost exhaustively.

Comment by Examiner Wei, School Instructor: Elegant in expression and precise in meaning.

The Changes was composed by the sages and brings the subtlety of its application to the utmost: this is why the Changes embodies the Way of the sages. Indeed, the composition of the Changes provided the means for its subtle application. How could the Way of the sages lie outside this? It is fitting that the Great Commentary should explain this to instruct people. Moreover, although the application of the Changes works subtly throughout all under Heaven, its composition truly originated with the sages.

title: 正德八年福建鄉試錄
text:
是故理之深者隱而未見也其何以極之聖
人繫辭定占而極乎至精則其深者以顯焉
理之幾者動而尚微也其何以研之聖人通
變立象而極乎至變則其幾者以著焉夫易
為聖人之極深辭占所在即深矣凡有問焉
而尚辭尚占則疑者以决天下之志有不通
者乎易為聖人之研幾象變所在即幾矣凡
有求焉而尚變尚象則怠者以勉天下之務
有不成者乎然是深也幾也發微而不可見
===
充周而不可窮又妙於神焉是以通志成務
不待於疾而自速果誰之使耶開物定業不
待於行而自至抑誰之為耶於此可見易有
聖人之道四焉者正以辭占極深而志通於
無為變象研幾而務成於無外辭占也變象
也皆變化之道神之所為也聖道之具於易
者非此之謂與吁易道之妙於用如此聖人
作易之功所以為至也哉抑又論之易之道
固聖人之道聖人之道實天地之道也蓋天
punctuated: 是故，理之深者，隱而未見也，其何以極之？聖人繫辭定占而極乎至精，則其深者以顯焉。理之幾者，動而尚微也，其何以研之？聖人通變立象而極乎至變，則其幾者以著焉。夫易為聖人之極深，辭占所在即深矣。凡有問焉，而尚辭尚占，則疑者以决，天下之志有不通者乎？易為聖人之研幾，象變所在即幾矣。凡有求焉，而尚變尚象，則怠者以勉，天下之務有不成者乎？然是深也、幾也，發微而不可見，充周而不可窮，又妙於神焉。是以通志成務，不待於疾而自速，果誰之使耶？開物定業，不待於行而自至，抑誰之為耶？於此可見，易有聖人之道四焉者，正以辭占極深而志通於無為，變象研幾而務成於無外。辭占也，變象也，皆變化之道，神之所為也。聖道之具於易者，非此之謂與？吁！易道之妙於用如此，聖人作易之功所以為至也哉！抑又論之，易之道固聖人之道，聖人之道實天地之道也。蓋天
translation_en: Thus, what is profound in principle lies hidden and has not yet appeared. How can its depths be fully plumbed? The sages appended statements and established divinations, reaching the utmost refinement; thereby what is profound becomes manifest. The incipient workings of principle have begun to stir but remain subtle. How can they be investigated? The sages comprehended change and established images, reaching the utmost transformation; thereby these incipient workings become evident. The Book of Changes is the means by which the sages plumb the depths: wherever its statements and divinations are found, there are these depths. Whenever someone has a question and esteems its statements and divinations, doubts are resolved. Could any intentions under Heaven then remain uncomprehended? The Book of Changes is the means by which the sages investigate incipient workings: wherever its images and changes are found, there are these workings. Whenever someone seeks something and esteems its changes and images, the indolent are spurred to exertion. Could any affairs under Heaven then remain unaccomplished? Yet these depths and incipient workings disclose subtleties while remaining invisible, pervade everything while remaining inexhaustible, and possess the further marvel of numinous efficacy. Thus, in comprehending intentions and accomplishing affairs, they are swift of themselves without needing haste: who indeed makes this happen? In opening things to understanding and settling undertakings, they arrive of themselves without needing to travel: whose doing is this? Here we can see why the Book of Changes contains four aspects of the sages’ Way: its statements and divinations plumb the depths, so that intentions are comprehended without deliberate action; its changes and images investigate incipient workings, so that affairs are accomplished with nothing left outside their scope. Statements and divinations, changes and images—all are the way of transformation, the workings of numinous efficacy. Is this not what it means for the sages’ Way to be fully embodied in the Book of Changes? Ah! Such is the marvelous functioning of the Way of Changes. This is why the sages’ achievement in making the Book of Changes is supreme! To discuss it further: the Way of Changes is indeed the sages’ Way, and the sages’ Way is truly the Way of Heaven and Earth. For Heaven…

title: 正德八年福建鄉試錄
text:
地之道顯設於日用事爲之間乃自然之易
也天地有是道而不能以告乎人於是有聖
人者出其憂世之意深而易始作觀之辭占
變象四者之用至精至變而極於至神易有
以冒乎聖人之道矣於乎聖人不能以其心
易覺天下而託諸易豈其所以得已哉吾夫
子於是章既詳言易之用而覆說其意者所
以明聖人作易之功如是也學易君子宜致
思焉
===
書
工以納言時而颺之
林達
同考試官訓導劉批聖人以樂觀人此言
可見作者於時颺處多欠發明此作命意造語儼若
親承虞廷之謦欬者矣是宜錄之
同考試官教諭羅批此題作者多體認
欠明類用浮詞語意精到惟此篇爲最
考試官教諭沈批明快莊重無如此作
punctuated:
地之道，顯設於日用事爲之間，乃自然之易也。天地有是道，而不能以告乎人，於是有聖人者出，其憂世之意深，而易始作。觀之辭占變象四者之用，至精至變，而極於至神，易有以冒乎聖人之道矣。於乎！聖人不能以其心易覺天下，而託諸易，豈其所以得已哉？吾夫子於是章既詳言易之用，而覆說其意者，所以明聖人作易之功如是也。學易君子宜致思焉。

書
工以納言，時而颺之。
林達

同考試官訓導劉批：「聖人以樂觀人，此言可見。作者於時颺處，多欠發明。此作命意造語，儼若親承虞廷之謦欬者矣，是宜錄之。」

同考試官教諭羅批：「此題作者多體認欠明，類用浮詞。語意精到，惟此篇爲最。」

考試官教諭沈批：「明快莊重，無如此作。」
translation_en:
…the Way of Earth, manifest in everyday affairs and activities, is the Changes of nature itself. Heaven and Earth possess this Way but cannot communicate it to humanity. Thus sages arose, deeply concerned for the world, and the Book of Changes was first composed. Consider the functions of its four elements—statements, divinations, transformations, and images: supremely subtle and adaptable, they culminate in the utmost spiritual efficacy. The Changes thus encompasses the Way of the sages. Alas! The sages could not awaken all under Heaven through the Changes within their own minds [?], and so entrusted it to the Book of Changes. How could they have refrained from doing so? In this chapter, our Master not only explains the functions of the Changes in detail but also reiterates their significance, thereby illuminating the sages’ achievement in composing it. Gentlemen who study the Changes should give this careful thought.

Book of Documents
“The music masters are to receive the words and sing them forth at the appropriate times.”
By Lin Da.

Comment by Associate Examiner Liu, Assistant Instructor: “That the sages observed people through music is evident in this statement. Those writing on this topic generally fail to elucidate ‘at the appropriate times, sing them forth.’ This essay’s conception and phrasing make its author seem almost to have personally heard the voice of the sage at the court of Yu [Shun]. It therefore deserves to be recorded.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Luo, Instructor: “Most writers on this topic lack a clear understanding and generally resort to empty phrases. For precision of language and depth of meaning, this essay is the best.”

Comment by Examiner Shen, Instructor: “For clarity, force, dignity, and gravity, no essay equals this one.”

title: 正德八年福建鄉試錄
text:
考試官學正魏批得旨
聖君命官欲以人所達之詞而察於所作之
樂焉蓋觀人莫要於樂也樂官以人所達之
詞而察於樂則其改過與否豈能揜哉昔舜
命禹之意若曰庶頑讒說之徒固示之以教
矣然侯明撻識之外又豈無所驗乎彼典樂
之官以教冑子爲職者也於是則有以委任
之而考言之是託焉典樂之工以育人材爲
務者也於是則有以責成之而察言之是寄
===
焉蓋人心之動因言以宣庶頑於受教之餘
必有言以上納也人心之蘊因言以達讒說
於改過之初必有言以上陳也則采其所納
播諸律呂而敷布於摶拊之間錄其所陳被
諸聲音而諷咏於合止之下時時颺之即其
樂而察其心日日宣之因其音而考其志如
其言之合於道而見於樂也果能和其聲而
無所乖則其向忠直之化也明矣如其言之
背於理而見於樂也不能和其聲而有所乖
punctuated:
考試官學正魏批：得旨。

聖君命官，欲以人所達之詞而察於所作之樂焉。蓋觀人莫要於樂也。樂官以人所達之詞而察於樂，則其改過與否，豈能揜哉？昔舜命禹之意若曰：庶頑讒說之徒，固示之以教矣。然侯明撻識之外，又豈無所驗乎？彼典樂之官，以教冑子爲職者也，於是則有以委任之，而考言之是託焉；典樂之工，以育人材爲務者也，於是則有以責成之，而察言之是寄焉。蓋人心之動，因言以宣，庶頑於受教之餘，必有言以上納也；人心之蘊，因言以達，讒說於改過之初，必有言以上陳也。則采其所納，播諸律呂，而敷布於摶拊之間；錄其所陳，被諸聲音，而諷咏於合止之下。時時颺之，即其樂而察其心；日日宣之，因其音而考其志。如其言之合於道而見於樂也，果能和其聲而無所乖，則其向忠直之化也明矣；如其言之背於理而見於樂也，不能和其聲而有所乖，
translation_en:
Examiner Wei, an Instructor, comments: “Grasps the purport.”

The sage ruler appoints officials intending to examine the words people express through the music made from them. For nothing is more essential to observing people than music. If the music officials examine people’s expressed words through music, how could it remain concealed whether they have corrected their faults?

The intention behind Shun’s charge to Yu in antiquity was as though he said: The various obstinate people and those who utter slanders have certainly been shown the teachings. Yet beyond making matters clear through archery and impressing them upon people through flogging, could there be no further means of verification? The official in charge of music has the duty of teaching the sons of the nobility. Thus he is given an appointment and entrusted with examining their words. The musicians responsible for music make nurturing talent their task. Thus they are charged with achieving results and entrusted with scrutinizing their words.

For the stirrings of the human heart are expressed through words: after receiving instruction, the various obstinate people will surely have words to submit to their superiors. What lies within the human heart is conveyed through words: when those who utter slanders first correct their faults, they will surely have words to present to their superiors. Accordingly, collect what they submit, set it to the pitch standards, and give it expression amid the beating of drums; record what they present, clothe it in musical sounds, and chant it in time with the music’s beginnings and endings. Repeatedly give their words musical expression, examining their hearts through the music; proclaim them day after day, investigating their intentions through its sounds. If their words accord with the Way and are expressed in music, and they can indeed harmonize their sounds without discord, then it is clear that they are turning toward transformation into loyal and upright people. If their words run counter to principle and are expressed in music, and they cannot harmonize their sounds but produce discord, …

title: 正德八年福建鄉試錄
text:
則其稔頑讒之習也必矣夫如是則在人善
惡之實已悉而我勸懲之典由之行焉夫豈
有不當者哉抑有虞之世九德咸事百僚師
師何頑讒之足慮耶而舜深致意於此嘗命
龍以典之矣至是又總命於禹先之以三者
之教終之以颺言之法必欲其改過而承之
庸之焉聖人生物之仁至矣厥後羣后德讓
庶尹允諧而卒無頑讒之可見者其有感於
帝之仁也夫
===
三后協心同底于道道洽政治澤潤生
民
廖雲龍
同考試官訓導劉批題本冠冕似易而難
場中作者牽綴重複令人厭觀此作詞暢理明必邃
於璧經者
同考試官教諭羅批深得康王望畢公
成終之意
考試官教諭沈批詞不費而理自足佳作也
punctuated:
則其稔頑讒之習也必矣。夫如是，則在人善惡之實已悉，而我勸懲之典由之行焉，夫豈有不當者哉？抑有虞之世，九德咸事，百僚師師，何頑讒之足慮耶？而舜深致意於此，嘗命龍以典之矣。至是，又總命於禹，先之以三者之教，終之以颺言之法，必欲其改過而承之、庸之焉。聖人生物之仁至矣！厥後羣后德讓，庶尹允諧，而卒無頑讒之可見者，其有感於帝之仁也夫！

三后協心，同底于道；道洽政治，澤潤生民。

廖雲龍

同考試官訓導劉批：「題本冠冕，似易而難。場中作者牽綴重複，令人厭觀。此作詞暢理明，必邃於璧經者。」

同考試官教諭羅批：「深得康王望畢公成終之意。」

考試官教諭沈批：「詞不費而理自足，佳作也。」
translation_en:
…then it is certain that their habits of obstinacy and slander have become ingrained. In this way, the true goodness or wickedness of others is fully known, and our rules for encouragement and punishment are applied accordingly. How could there be anything inappropriate in this? Yet in the age of Youyu, all nine virtues were put into service, and the hundred officials learned from one another. What cause was there to worry about obstinacy and slander? Nevertheless, Shun gave this matter profound attention and had already commanded Long to take charge of it. At this point he also issued comprehensive instructions to Yu, beginning with the three forms of teaching and ending with the method of proclaiming their words. He was determined that they should mend their faults, so that he might then receive and employ them. The sage’s benevolence in nurturing living beings was indeed supreme! Thereafter, the assembled lords yielded to one another in virtue, and the many administrators were truly harmonious, until no obstinacy or slander could be seen. Surely they had been moved by the emperor’s benevolence!

“The three lords united their hearts and together attained the Way; the Way permeated government, and its beneficence enriched the lives of the people.”

Liao Yunlong

Comment by Associate Examiner Liu, Assistant Instructor: “The topic is inherently grand: it seems easy but is difficult. Writers in the examination hall string things together and repeat themselves, making their work tiresome to read. This composition is fluent in expression and clear in reasoning. Its author must be deeply versed in the ‘Wall Classic’ [?].”

Comment by Associate Examiner Luo, Instructor: “It thoroughly grasps King Kang’s intention in expecting the Duke of Bi to bring the undertaking to completion.”

Comment by Examiner Shen, Instructor: “The wording is economical, yet the reasoning is fully sufficient. An excellent composition.”

title: 正德八年福建鄉試錄
text:
考試官學正魏批旨趣悠深
羣臣相契以圖治故能致民於至治甚矣殷
民之難化也非羣臣契其心以圖治何以使
之蒙至治之休哉昔康王命畢公保釐東郊
至此以成終之責期之蓋謂天下之事每成
於同而化殷之事尤戒夫異彼周公愼厥始
矣君陳和厥中矣而成終之責又惟公是賴
三后繼作雖非一時而前倡後和同一化殷
以爲心初不以時而有異焉三后迭出雖非
===
一人而彼作此述同一化民以爲念初不以
人而有間焉由是推此心以爲治寬嚴固異
施矣而轉移感動于以薰蒸乎民者道未始
不同也達此心以爲治剛柔固異尚也而鼓
舞作興于以甄陶乎民者道未嘗不合也心
協道同如此由是至道之所孚積累於三紀
之餘渾淪磅礴而有以浹民之肌膚善政之
所布更張於三后之手森嚴整肅而有以昭
人之耳目舉東郊之民皆沐浴於膏澤之中
punctuated:
考試官學正魏批：「旨趣悠深。」

羣臣相契以圖治，故能致民於至治。甚矣，殷民之難化也！非羣臣契其心以圖治，何以使之蒙至治之休哉？昔康王命畢公保釐東郊，至此以成終之責期之，蓋謂天下之事每成於同，而化殷之事尤戒夫異。彼周公愼厥始矣，君陳和厥中矣，而成終之責又惟公是賴。三后繼作，雖非一時，而前倡後和，同一化殷以爲心，初不以時而有異焉；三后迭出，雖非一人，而彼作此述，同一化民以爲念，初不以人而有間焉。由是推此心以爲治，寬嚴固異施矣，而轉移感動，于以薰蒸乎民者，道未始不同也；達此心以爲治，剛柔固異尚也，而鼓舞作興，于以甄陶乎民者，道未嘗不合也。心協道同如此，由是至道之所孚，積累於三紀之餘，渾淪磅礴，而有以浹民之肌膚；善政之所布，更張於三后之手，森嚴整肅，而有以昭人之耳目。舉東郊之民，皆沐浴於膏澤之中
translation_en:
Examiner Wei, Instructor, comments: “The purport is profound and far-reaching.”

The ministers accorded with one another in seeking good government, and thus were able to bring the people to a state of consummate order. How difficult it was to transform the people of Yin! Unless the ministers united their purposes in seeking good government, how could they have enabled the people to enjoy the blessings of consummate order? Formerly, King Kang commanded the Duke of Bi to safeguard and govern the eastern suburbs. At this point he charged him with the responsibility of bringing the work to completion. His meaning was that affairs throughout the realm generally succeed through unity, and that in transforming the people of Yin, discord was especially to be guarded against. The Duke of Zhou had been circumspect at the beginning; Jun Chen had brought harmony in the middle; and the responsibility for completing the work now rested upon the duke alone. These three lords undertook the work in succession. Though they did not serve at the same time, the earlier one initiated and the later ones responded, sharing a single resolve to transform Yin: differences of time never altered that resolve. Though the three lords who appeared in succession were different men, one carried forward what another had begun, sharing a single concern to transform the people: differences of person never caused any division.

Thus, in extending this purpose to government, they might indeed apply leniency and severity differently; yet the Way by which they wrought change and stirred hearts, gradually permeating the people with their influence, was never different. In giving expression to this purpose through government, they might indeed favor firmness or gentleness differently; yet the Way by which they encouraged and roused the people, molding and shaping them, was never out of accord. Such was the concord of their purposes and the unity of their Way. Consequently, the influence inspired by the consummate Way accumulated over more than three twelve-year cycles, becoming all-embracing and vast, and penetrating the very flesh and skin of the people. The beneficent government they instituted was adjusted and renewed at the hands of the three lords, becoming imposing, orderly, and disciplined, and making its effects manifest to the people's ears and eyes. All the people of the eastern suburbs bathed in its nourishing blessings …

title: 正德八年福建鄉試錄
text:
大化昭融無復昔日之以蕩陵德也不猶江
河之灌漑乎合下都之衆皆游泳於化育之
內至仁洋溢無復向日之怙侈滅義也不猶
雨露之沾濡乎是則政本於道道本於心三
后心同則道同道同則自有以達於政而極
于洽成終之責至是盡矣公也可不念之哉
嗟夫蕞爾殷民周公師保之君陳簡進之至
畢公之時已升大猷矣何足以介吾慮者而
康王倦倦以邦之安危惟玆殷士爲言至於
===
望畢公以成終必極於澤潤生民四夷咸賴
而後已焉其不安於小成也如是八百年有
道之長孰謂不基於斯乎
詩
民之質矣日用飲食
張岳
同考試官訓導王批形容有周臣子以天
下之福荅君之意藹然如見其邃於經學者高薦何忝
同考試官學正陳批近時有以日用飲食
punctuated:
大化昭融，無復昔日之以蕩陵德也，不猶江河之灌漑乎？合下都之衆，皆游泳於化育之內，至仁洋溢，無復向日之怙侈滅義也，不猶雨露之沾濡乎？是則政本於道，道本於心。三后心同則道同，道同則自有以達於政，而極于洽，成終之責至是盡矣。公也可不念之哉！
嗟夫！蕞爾殷民，周公師保之，君陳簡進之，至畢公之時，已升大猷矣。何足以介吾慮者？而康王倦倦以邦之安危惟玆殷士爲言，至於望畢公以成終，必極於澤潤生民，四夷咸賴而後已焉。其不安於小成也如是，八百年有道之長，孰謂不基於斯乎？
詩
民之質矣，日用飲食。
張岳
同考試官訓導王批：形容有周臣子以天下之福荅君之意，藹然如見其邃於經學者，高薦何忝？
同考試官學正陳批：近時有以日用飲食
translation_en:
…The great transforming influence shines forth harmoniously; no longer do they undermine virtue through dissipation as in former days. Is this not like irrigation by the great rivers? All the people of the lower capital are immersed in this nurturing transformation. Supreme benevolence overflows; no longer do they rely on extravagance and destroy righteousness as before. Is this not like being moistened by rain and dew? Thus government is rooted in the Way, and the Way is rooted in the heart. When the hearts of the three lords are alike, their Way is alike; when their Way is alike, it naturally finds expression in government and brings harmony to its fullest extent. The responsibility for bringing the undertaking to completion is thereby fully discharged. Can you, my lord, fail to give thought to this?
Alas! This small body of Yin people was instructed and protected by the Duke of Zhou, and selected and advanced by Jun Chen. By the time of the Duke of Bi, they had already advanced to the great Way. What about them could warrant our concern? Yet King Kang earnestly [?] spoke of the security or peril of the state as depending upon these very Yin gentlemen. In looking to the Duke of Bi to bring the undertaking to completion, he would accept nothing less than beneficence nourishing the people and all the peoples of the four quarters benefiting from it. Such was his refusal to rest content with a minor achievement. Who could say that the foundation of eight hundred years of enduring rule in accordance with the Way did not lie here?
Book of Odes
“The people are simple in nature, daily taking food and drink.”
Zhang Yue
Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Assistant Instructor: This portrays the intent of a Zhou minister to repay his ruler with blessings for all under Heaven. Its warmth seems to bring that intent before our eyes. For one so deeply versed in classical learning, what cause would there be for shame in recommending him highly?
Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: Recently there have been those who take “daily taking food and drink”…

title: 正德八年福建鄉試錄
text:
對說殊戾本旨此作見理明白而詞亦足以發之錄之
以破穿鑿者之疑
考試官敎諭沈批能悉詩人忠愛之情
考試官學正魏批詩正而葩此作得之
民淳而安其常詩人願神之福君然也蓋日
用飲食民之所以安其常而淳者在是矣君
福之盛何以加于此哉昔天保詩人託神意
以答其君如此謂夫吾君統天下以為治則
亦兼天下以為福然則神之貽福於吾君者
===
不於吾民有徵乎將見夫民之習於僞也自
是以返其真民之趨於巧也自是而歸於朴
國邑都鄙之間而有渾龐沕穆之風里巷閻
閻之內而興篤實醇厚之化皥皥焉與世相
忘而思慮之不作其在於我周者亦猶夫邃
古之初矣蠢蠢焉與物為友而好惡之不形
其在於今日者亦猶夫顓蒙之時矣民質如
此復何為哉蓋其生長於斯世固亦有所游
息以安日用之常俯仰於兩間固亦有所從
punctuated:
對說，殊戾本旨。此作見理明白，而詞亦足以發之，錄之以破穿鑿者之疑。
考試官敎諭沈批：能悉詩人忠愛之情。
考試官學正魏批：詩正而葩，此作得之。
民淳而安其常，詩人願神之福君然也。蓋日用飲食，民之所以安其常而淳者在是矣。君福之盛，何以加于此哉？昔天保詩人託神意以答其君，如此謂夫吾君統天下以為治，則亦兼天下以為福。然則神之貽福於吾君者，不於吾民有徵乎？將見夫民之習於僞也，自是以返其真；民之趨於巧也，自是而歸於朴。國邑都鄙之間，而有渾龐沕穆之風；里巷閻閻之內，而興篤實醇厚之化。皥皥焉與世相忘，而思慮之不作，其在於我周者，亦猶夫邃古之初矣。蠢蠢焉與物為友，而好惡之不形，其在於今日者，亦猶夫顓蒙之時矣。民質如此，復何為哉？蓋其生長於斯世，固亦有所游息，以安日用之常；俯仰於兩間，固亦有所從
translation_en:
…to explain them in opposition to one another greatly violates the original meaning. This composition grasps the principle clearly, and its language is adequate to express it. It is included here to dispel the doubts of those who force strained interpretations upon the text.
Examiner Shen, Instructor, comments: “It fully conveys the poet’s feelings of loyalty and love.”
Examiner Wei, School Instructor, comments: “Poetry is upright yet richly adorned; this composition captures that quality.”
The people are simple and content with their accustomed lives: this is how the poet wishes the spirits to bless his ruler. For it is in everyday eating and drinking that the people find contentment in their accustomed lives and remain simple. How could the abundance of the ruler’s blessings surpass this? Long ago, the poet of ‘Heaven Protects’ (Tianbao) conveyed the spirits’ intentions to respond to his ruler in this way. His meaning was that our ruler brings all under Heaven together under his governance, and so likewise embraces all under Heaven in his blessings. Would not the blessings that the spirits bestow upon our ruler therefore find their manifestation among our people?
We shall see those among the people who have become accustomed to falseness henceforth return to genuineness, and those inclined toward cunning henceforth return to simplicity. Throughout the capital, towns, great settlements, and countryside, there will be an atmosphere of unspoiled fullness and profound harmony; within the lanes and among the dwellings [?], a transformation toward sincerity, solidity, purity, and generosity will arise. In carefree contentment, they and the world will forget one another, and calculating thoughts will not arise. Life in our Zhou will resemble the very beginnings of remote antiquity. Unselfconsciously active, they will be companions to all things, without likes or dislikes taking shape. Life today will resemble the age of primal innocence. With the people so simple, what further need is there to do anything? Growing up in this world, they naturally have scope to wander and rest, finding contentment in the regular course of daily life; living between Heaven and Earth, they naturally also have scope to be at ease…

title: 正德八年福建鄉試錄
text:
容以爲日用之樂亦惟曰渴以飲也夏之水
冬之湯而飲惟其時苟適焉則止用是以終
吾之生而已固未甞出此而他有慕焉飢而
食也朝之饔夕之飧而食惟其時苟飽焉則
棄用是以遂吾之欲而已亦未甞外此而他
有事焉飲而不知其所以飲者果誰之爲也
食而不知其所以食者抑誰之賜也此其質
何如哉是知風俗者天下之大事化成者王
者之盛節以是爲福臣子荅君之意至矣雖
===
然君者納民於軌物者也曾謂民之質否而
果係於神哉洪範有言斂時五福用敷錫厥
庶民其所以斂而敷之者固自乎君而神無
預矣君以是敷之而民皆化於質以厚其福
焉是即所謂錫汝保極也天保詩人盛稱君
福而德之一字獨於此章發之有旨哉後之
舍民事而徼淫祀以祝釐者可以鑒矣
載戢干戈載櫜弓矢我求懿德肆于時
夏
punctuated:
容以爲日用之樂，亦惟曰：渴以飲也，夏之水、冬之湯，而飲惟其時，苟適焉則止，用是以終吾之生而已，固未甞出此而他有慕焉。飢而食也，朝之饔、夕之飧，而食惟其時，苟飽焉則棄，用是以遂吾之欲而已，亦未甞外此而他有事焉。飲而不知其所以飲者，果誰之爲也？食而不知其所以食者，抑誰之賜也？此其質何如哉！是知風俗者，天下之大事；化成者，王者之盛節。以是爲福，臣子荅君之意至矣。雖然，君者，納民於軌物者也。曾謂民之質否而果係於神哉？《洪範》有言：「斂時五福，用敷錫厥庶民。」其所以斂而敷之者，固自乎君，而神無預矣。君以是敷之，而民皆化於質，以厚其福焉，是即所謂「錫汝保極」也。《天保》詩人盛稱君福，而德之一字獨於此章發之，有旨哉！後之舍民事而徼淫祀以祝釐者，可以鑒矣。

載戢干戈，載櫜弓矢。我求懿德，肆于時夏。
translation_en:
…at ease, finding pleasure in their daily lives. They say only: when thirsty, we drink—water in summer, hot water in winter, each at its proper season. Once refreshed, we stop. With this we simply sustain ourselves to the end of our lives; we have never coveted anything beyond it. When hungry, we eat—the morning meal and the evening meal, each at its proper time. Once full, we set the food aside. With this we simply satisfy our wants; we have never concerned ourselves with anything beyond it. They drink without knowing whose doing has made their drinking possible; they eat without knowing whose bounty has provided their food. How great is their simplicity! Thus we know that customs are a great concern of the realm, and bringing moral transformation to completion is a sovereign’s splendid achievement. To regard this as a blessing expresses to the utmost the intent of a subject responding to his ruler.

Nevertheless, it is the ruler who brings the people within proper norms. Could one really suppose that whether the people are simple or not depends upon the spirits? The Great Plan says: “Gather these five blessings, and distribute them widely among the common people.” The gathering and distribution depend upon the ruler himself; the spirits have no part in them. When the ruler distributes blessings in this way, the people are all transformed toward simplicity, thereby increasing their blessings. This is precisely what is meant by “They grant you the preservation of the ultimate standard.” The poet of Heaven Protects lavishly praises the ruler’s blessings, yet brings out the word “virtue” only in this stanza. How significant this is! Those of later ages who neglect the people’s affairs and seek blessings through improper sacrifices may take warning from this.

“Then we put away shields and spears; then we sheathed bows and arrows. We seek admirable virtue, to spread it throughout these lands of Xia.”

title: 正德八年福建鄉試錄
text:
馬明衡
同考試官訓導王批模寫有周偃武脩文
太平氣象殆無餘蘊如躬逢其盛者錄之以為後學之式
同考試官學正陳批講求懿德處體認
精切而通篇詞氣舂容其有得於詩者矣
考試官教諭沈批明暢宜錄
考試官學正魏批得周王巡守之意
休天下之兵弘天下之化周王巡守然也甚
矣武功既成文德所當敷也周王有見於此
===
其得巡守之道哉此巡守而朝會祭告之樂
歌也想周王當朝會之日正式序之餘以為
武以戡亂而亦不可黷文以致治而在所當
脩是故若干若戈向固用之以伐暴也暴焉
既伐可玩之而常事乎今則聚之府庫之中
示天下有休息之意熈熈乎治平之境也若
弓若矢昔固資之以定亂也亂焉既定可樂
之而輕試乎今則韜之櫜服之内俾四海無
征伐之擾皞皞乎泰和之域也夫武事既偃
punctuated:
馬明衡

同考試官訓導王批：模寫有周偃武脩文、太平氣象，殆無餘蘊，如躬逢其盛者，錄之以為後學之式。
同考試官學正陳批：講求懿德處，體認精切，而通篇詞氣舂容，其有得於詩者矣。
考試官教諭沈批：明暢，宜錄。
考試官學正魏批：得周王巡守之意。

休天下之兵，弘天下之化，周王巡守然也。甚矣，武功既成，文德所當敷也！周王有見於此，其得巡守之道哉！此巡守而朝會祭告之樂歌也。想周王當朝會之日，正式序之餘，以為武以戡亂，而亦不可黷；文以致治，而在所當脩。是故若干若戈，向固用之以伐暴也；暴焉既伐，可玩之而常事乎？今則聚之府庫之中，示天下有休息之意，熈熈乎治平之境也。若弓若矢，昔固資之以定亂也；亂焉既定，可樂之而輕試乎？今則韜之櫜服之内，俾四海無征伐之擾，皞皞乎泰和之域也。夫武事既偃，
translation_en:
Ma Mingheng

Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Assistant Instructor: His portrayal of the Zhou dynasty laying aside arms and cultivating civil virtue, and of the atmosphere of peace, leaves scarcely anything unexpressed. It is as though he personally witnessed that flourishing age. This is recorded as a model for later students.
Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, School Instructor: In his discussion of seeking admirable virtue, his understanding is precise and penetrating. Throughout, his language and cadence are measured and expansive. He has indeed gained an understanding of the Odes.
Comment by Examiner Shen, Instructor: Clear and fluent; it deserves inclusion.
Comment by Examiner Wei, School Instructor: He grasps the purpose of the Zhou king’s tours of inspection.

To give respite to the arms of all under Heaven and extend moral transformation throughout the realm: such was the Zhou king’s purpose in touring his dominions. How imperative it is, once military achievements are complete, to spread civil virtue! The Zhou king understood this. Surely he grasped the proper way to conduct tours of inspection! This is a ceremonial song for court assemblies and sacrificial announcements during such tours. We may imagine that, on the day of an assembly, after setting the ceremonial order aright [?], the Zhou king reflected that military force serves to quell disorder but must not be used wantonly, while civil virtue brings good government and must therefore be cultivated.

Thus shields and dagger-axes had indeed formerly been used to punish the violent. But once the violent had been punished, could these weapons be treated as playthings and their use made a regular occupation? Now they were gathered into the storehouses and arsenals, showing all under Heaven the intention to grant repose: a joyful realm of order and peace. Bows and arrows had indeed formerly been relied upon to settle disorder. But once disorder had been settled, could one delight in them and lightly put them to use? Now they were stowed in their cases and quivers, sparing all within the Four Seas the disturbances of military campaigns: a bright and contented realm of supreme harmony. Now that military affairs had been laid to rest, …

title: 正德八年福建鄉試錄
text:
文德當敷彼殷辛肆惡懿德之昏也甚矣我
則益求至理之攸歸而德之昏者以復明商
紂不善義德之喪也乆矣我則益求當然之
所在而德之喪者以復振故凡見於天理之
當爲靡不在於宣布之餘篤近舉遠之教洋
溢乎中國也今日之行豈誇示武功者哉故
凡本乎人心之固有罔不在於敷陳之下移
風易俗之化旁達乎華夏也今日之會豈徒
恃兵戎者哉是則休兵於戡亂之後弘化於
===
致治之先周王所以保天命者有如是夫大
抵文武之用各以其時也好戰則不可與從
事于安忘戰則不可與從事于危故周王當
布昭聖武之餘而拳拳於懿德之求及其後
也又不忘乎洛水之講此所以文武並用克
盡君道而延八百年有道之長者豈偶然之
故哉有天下者尚其鑒諸
春秋
取汶陽田〔成公二年〕公如晉 公至自晉
punctuated:
文德當敷。彼殷辛肆惡，懿德之昏也甚矣！我則益求至理之攸歸，而德之昏者以復明。商紂不善，義德之喪也乆矣！我則益求當然之所在，而德之喪者以復振。故凡見於天理之當爲，靡不在於宣布之餘，篤近舉遠之教洋溢乎中國也。今日之行，豈誇示武功者哉？故凡本乎人心之固有，罔不在於敷陳之下，移風易俗之化旁達乎華夏也。今日之會，豈徒恃兵戎者哉？是則休兵於戡亂之後，弘化於致治之先，周王所以保天命者有如是夫！大抵文武之用，各以其時也。好戰則不可與從事于安，忘戰則不可與從事于危。故周王當布昭聖武之餘，而拳拳於懿德之求；及其後也，又不忘乎洛水之講。此所以文武並用，克盡君道，而延八百年有道之長者，豈偶然之故哉？有天下者尚其鑒諸！

春秋
取汶陽田〔成公二年〕。公如晉，公至自晉。
translation_en:
…civil virtue should be spread abroad. Xin of Yin gave free rein to evil: how deeply splendid virtue had been obscured! We therefore strive all the more to discover where the highest principle leads, so that obscured virtue may shine again. Zhou of Shang acted wickedly: how long righteous virtue had been lost! We therefore strive all the more to discover what ought rightly to be done, so that lost virtue may be restored. Thus everything that Heaven’s principle requires us to do is proclaimed, and the teaching of treating those nearby generously and drawing in those far away overflows throughout the central realm. Could today’s undertaking merely be a display of military achievement? Thus everything inherent in the human heart is set forth, and the transforming influence that changes prevailing practices and customs spreads throughout Huaxia. Could today’s assembly rely on armed force alone? To give the troops rest after suppressing disorder and to extend moral transformation as the first step toward good government—such was the means by which the king of Zhou preserved Heaven’s Mandate!

In general, civil and military measures each have their proper time. Those who delight in war cannot be entrusted with the affairs of peace; those who forget war cannot be entrusted with the affairs of danger. Thus, after displaying his sagely martial prowess, the king of Zhou devoted himself earnestly to seeking splendid virtue; later, he also did not neglect military exercises by the Luo River. In this way he employed both civil and military measures, fully discharged the duties of a ruler, and prolonged a reign of good government for eight hundred years. Could this have happened by chance? May those who possess All under Heaven take heed of this example!

Spring and Autumn Annals
“Acquired the fields of Wenyang.” 〔Second year of Duke Cheng〕 “The duke went to Jin.” “The duke returned from Jin.”

title: 正德八年福建鄉試錄
text:
成公三年
王希旦
同考試官教諭尹批此題當合二傳意場
中士子多用後傳姝戾聖人尊王抑伯本旨是篇體貼
傳註明白雅宜錄出以冠多士
考試官教諭沈批得傳意
考試官學正魏批謹嚴
望國復地而未請於王春秋既貶之事伯而
未覲乎王春秋尤貶之此成公恃晉以取汶
===
陽如晉以拜私惠皆不知周室之爲尊也春
秋得不書取書至以貶之哉且汶陽魯之故
田也成公積憾齊國之見奪今勝齊師而得
歸土地入其舊疆人民從其故主本非瘠齊
以肥魯也春秋貶之蓋曰諸侯之地天子所
掌故疆里之限如天建地設未有得地而不
請正於王者矧周公之封儉於百里邦域之
中果有是耶成不知此仗晉兵威致敵人之
敗北反齊侵奪收版籍以歸東司空未考於
punctuated:
成公三年。
王希旦。
同考試官教諭尹批：此題當合二傳意，場中士子多用後傳，姝戾聖人尊王抑伯本旨。是篇體貼傳註，明白雅宜，錄出以冠多士。
考試官教諭沈批：得傳意。
考試官學正魏批：謹嚴。
望國復地而未請於王，春秋既貶之；事伯而未覲乎王，春秋尤貶之。此成公恃晉以取汶陽，如晉以拜私惠，皆不知周室之爲尊也。春秋得不書取、書至以貶之哉？且汶陽，魯之故田也。成公積憾齊國之見奪，今勝齊師而得歸，土地入其舊疆，人民從其故主，本非瘠齊以肥魯也。春秋貶之，蓋曰諸侯之地，天子所掌，故疆里之限，如天建地設，未有得地而不請正於王者。矧周公之封，儉於百里，邦域之中果有是耶？成不知此，仗晉兵威，致敵人之敗北，反齊侵奪，收版籍以歸東。司空未考於
translation_en:
Third year of Duke Cheng.
Wang Xidan.
Comment by Associate Examiner Yin, Instructor: This topic should combine the meanings of the two commentaries. Most candidates in the examination relied on the latter commentary, thereby departing from [?] the Sage’s fundamental intention of honoring the king and restraining the hegemon. This essay closely follows the commentaries and annotations; it is clear, elegant, and appropriate. It is transcribed here to stand foremost among the candidates’ essays.
Comment by Examiner Shen, Instructor: It grasps the meaning of the commentary.
Comment by Examiner Wei, School Instructor: Careful and rigorous.
When a prominent state [?] recovers territory without seeking the king’s approval, the Spring and Autumn Annals already censures it; when it serves a hegemon without attending an audience with the king, the Annals censures it still more. Duke Cheng relied on Jin to take Wenyang and went to Jin to give thanks for a private favor. Both acts showed his failure to recognize the supremacy of the Zhou royal house. How could the Annals fail to record “took” and “arrived” to censure him?
Now Wenyang was formerly territory of Lu. Duke Cheng had long resented its seizure by Qi. Having now defeated Qi’s army, he secured its return: the land rejoined its former boundaries, and the people returned to their former ruler. This was not, in itself, impoverishing Qi to enrich Lu. The Annals censures him because the territories of the feudal lords fall under the authority of the Son of Heaven. Their boundaries are therefore as fixed as if established by Heaven and Earth. No one may acquire territory without asking the king to confirm the settlement. Moreover, the Duke of Zhou’s enfeoffment was restricted to a hundred li: was this land actually within its boundaries?
Duke Cheng did not understand this. Relying on Jin’s military might, he brought about the enemy’s defeat, reversed Qi’s seizure of territory, and gathered the population and land registers to return east. The Minister of Works had not yet consulted …

title: 正德八年福建鄉試錄
text:
建邦之圖天子莫遣乎治地之吏是成公徒
知侵地之得爲榮而不恤擅命之刑莫贖矣
見利忘義與奪人之有者奚異乎故取乃得
非其有之稱今不曰復而特謂之取者所以
貶成公之不請王命也如此若晉國中夏盟
主也成公素託晉好以自安今懷晉惠而脩
朝玉帛以將其恭匍匐以展其勤固可諂晉
以翼魯也春秋貶之蓋曰諸侯之國天子所
封故德賜所被如天覆地載未有朝禮而不
===
先脩於王者矧宣公之服制已畢三年受命
之期非在是耶成不知此汶陽之惠視若九
鼎之重故絳之朝不憚千里之遥玄黃不篚
於納貢之庭圭冕未受於入覲之日是成公
徒知歸田之私惠當拜而不知襲封之大恩
已忘矣媚伯慢王其行事不亦悖乎故至乃
反國飲至之常今不憚煩而特書至自晉者
所以貶成公之不脩王禮也又如此吁土地
不由於王命不以得地爲能君朝聘不先於
punctuated:
建邦之圖，天子莫遣乎治地之吏，是成公徒知侵地之得爲榮，而不恤擅命之刑莫贖矣。見利忘義，與奪人之有者奚異乎？故取乃得非其有之稱，今不曰復而特謂之取者，所以貶成公之不請王命也如此。
若晉國，中夏盟主也。成公素託晉好以自安，今懷晉惠而脩朝，玉帛以將其恭，匍匐以展其勤，固可諂晉以翼魯也。《春秋》貶之，蓋曰：諸侯之國，天子所封，故德賜所被，如天覆地載，未有朝禮而不先脩於王者。矧宣公之服制已畢，三年受命之期非在是耶？成不知此，汶陽之惠視若九鼎之重，故絳之朝不憚千里之遥。玄黃不篚於納貢之庭，圭冕未受於入覲之日，是成公徒知歸田之私惠當拜，而不知襲封之大恩已忘矣。媚伯慢王，其行事不亦悖乎？故至乃反國飲至之常，今不憚煩而特書至自晉者，所以貶成公之不脩王禮也又如此。
吁！土地不由於王命，不以得地爲能君；朝聘不先於
translation_en:
…against the map establishing the domains, nor had the Son of Heaven dispatched an official responsible for administering the land. Thus Duke Cheng knew only to glory in obtaining the occupied territory, without considering that the punishment for arrogating authority could not be redeemed. Forgetting righteousness at the sight of profit—how was this different from seizing another’s possessions? Thus “taking” denotes obtaining what is not rightfully one’s own. That the text here does not say “recovered,” but specifically calls it “taking,” is how it censures Duke Cheng for failing to request the king’s command.
As for Jin, it was the leader of the covenant among the central states. Duke Cheng had long relied on friendly relations with Jin to secure his position. Now, grateful for Jin’s favor, he paid court there, presenting jade and silk to convey his reverence and bowing low to display his diligence. Certainly, he could flatter Jin to protect Lu. Yet the Spring and Autumn Annals censures him. Its meaning is this: the states of the feudal lords were enfeoffed by the Son of Heaven, and the reach of his gracious gifts was like heaven sheltering and earth sustaining all things. Never should the rites of a court visit be performed without first performing them before the king. Moreover, the prescribed mourning for Duke Xuan had ended: was this not the time, after three years, to receive the royal mandate? Duke Cheng did not understand this. He regarded the favor of receiving Wenyang as weighty as the Nine Tripods, and so did not shrink from traveling a thousand li to pay court at Jiang. Yet he had not presented baskets of dark and yellow silks at the court where tribute was offered, nor received the jade tablet and ceremonial cap on the day of a royal audience. Thus Duke Cheng knew only that he must give thanks for the private favor of having his lands restored, unaware that he had forgotten the great favor of succeeding to his fief. Was it not perverse to flatter the hegemon and slight the king? Thus “arrived” refers to the customary return to one’s state and the drinking ceremony marking that return. That the text here does not shrink from repetition but expressly records “arrived from Jin” is likewise how it censures Duke Cheng for failing to perform the rites owed to the king.
Alas! When land is obtained without the king’s command, its acquisition does not make one an able ruler; when court visits and diplomatic missions are not directed first toward …

title: 正德八年福建鄉試錄
text:
王室不以事伯爲能國聖人義利王伯之際
嚴矣大抵恃伯不可以爲安媚伯不可以爲
榮汶陽復矣何不免來言之歸如晉勤矣何
自貽不敬之侮向使以所仗晉者而仗周以
所事伯者而事王則汶陽之地誰得而奪之
京師之行誰得而侮之哉後之爲人臣者其
鑒於斯
莒去疾自齊入于莒〔昭公元年〕
林炫
===
同考試官教諭尹批題本平易作者
率多陳腐可厭此作說出去疾當時事實意新氣暢
詞嚴誼正盖必老於麟經者讀之令人躍然高薦何忝
考試官教諭沈批美刺明白可錄
考試官學正魏批得書法意
春秋於貴戚之入國也予其正以明大倫誅
其專以明大法此去疾討罪之正有國之專
美刺不相掩也春秋於其入係以國氏而不
稱公子良有以哉且莒公子曰去疾者憫君
punctuated:
王室，不以事伯爲能國。聖人義利王伯之際嚴矣！大抵恃伯不可以爲安，媚伯不可以爲榮。汶陽復矣，何不免來言之歸？如晉勤矣，何自貽不敬之侮？向使以所仗晉者而仗周，以所事伯者而事王，則汶陽之地誰得而奪之？京師之行誰得而侮之哉？後之爲人臣者，其鑒於斯！
莒去疾自齊入于莒。〔昭公元年〕
林炫
同考試官教諭尹批：「題本平易，作者率多陳腐可厭。此作說出去疾當時事實，意新氣暢，詞嚴誼正，盖必老於麟經者。讀之令人躍然，高薦何忝！」
考試官教諭沈批：「美刺明白，可錄。」
考試官學正魏批：「得書法意。」
春秋於貴戚之入國也，予其正以明大倫，誅其專以明大法。此去疾討罪之正，有國之專，美刺不相掩也。春秋於其入，係以國氏而不稱公子，良有以哉！且莒公子曰去疾者，憫君
translation_en:
…the royal house, a state cannot be deemed capable merely for serving a hegemon. How strictly the Sage distinguished righteousness from profit, and kingship from hegemony! In general, dependence upon a hegemon cannot bring security, nor can flattery of one bring honor. Wenyang had been recovered; why, then, could its return at another’s bidding not be avoided? His journeys to Jin were diligent; why, then, did he bring upon himself the humiliation of being treated disrespectfully? Had he relied upon Zhou as he relied upon Jin, and served the king as he served the hegemon, who could have taken the lands of Wenyang from him? Who could have insulted him on a journey to the royal capital? Let those who serve as subjects in later ages take warning from this!
“Quji of Ju entered Ju from Qi.” 〔First year of Duke Zhao〕
Lin Xuan
Comment by Associate Examiner Yin, Instructor: “The topic is straightforward, yet most writers produce stale and tiresome treatments. This composition brings out the actual circumstances of Quji’s time. Its ideas are fresh, its flow vigorous and unimpeded, its language exacting, and its meaning upright. Surely its author must be deeply versed in the Classic of the Unicorn [the Spring and Autumn Annals]. Reading it makes one leap with delight. What cause for shame could there be in recommending it highly?”
Comment by Examiner Shen, Instructor: “Its praise and censure are clear. Worth selecting.”
Comment by Examiner Wei, School Instructor: “It grasps the intent of the principles governing the Annals’ wording.”
When noble relatives enter a state, the Spring and Autumn Annals approves their rectitude to make clear the great moral relationships, and condemns their acting on their own authority to make clear the great governing norms. Here Quji’s rectitude in punishing wrongdoing and his presumption in taking possession of a state are such that neither praise nor censure obscures the other. In recording his entry, the Spring and Autumn Annals attaches the state’s name to his name, rather than calling him a ruler’s son. There is indeed a reason for this! Now the ruler’s son of Ju named Quji, grieving for his lord [?]…

title: 正德八年福建鄉試錄
text:
遠難出亡于齊今而羣弟召之齊鉏納之遂
自齊而入莒焉夫展輿乃莒子而去疾曷爲
又以國氏乎蓋國家之大惟知有人倫者能
居之展輿與聞國人之變泯亂君父之倫所
謂雖有粟不得而食者矣幸而去疾仗義以
問密州之故假齊以討展輿之罪亂賊去矣
而君親無將之法以嚴倫理正矣而臣子上
侵之令以熄以若所爲豈爭利其國而不顧
君親者乎去疾宜有莒國也明矣故國本無
===
二君也聖人於是退展輿而進去疾則無二
君之義明而國家豈有不定于一者乎若去
疾乃公子而入莒曷爲止稱名氏乎蓋統系
之重惟知有王法者能承之周室四海之所
推戴列國之所稟命所謂有父兄在不得聞
斯行之者矣詎意去疾自謂公子而可立專
有莒國而無疑周冕服矣而鞏洛錫封之使
未臨子爵襲矣而城陽更立之命未請以若
所爲豈謹守王度而可保社稷者乎去疾自
punctuated: 遠難，出亡于齊。今而羣弟召之，齊鉏納之，遂自齊而入莒焉。夫展輿乃莒子，而去疾曷爲又以國氏乎？蓋國家之大，惟知有人倫者能居之。展輿與聞國人之變，泯亂君父之倫，所謂雖有粟不得而食者矣。幸而去疾仗義以問密州之故，假齊以討展輿之罪，亂賊去矣，而君親無將之法以嚴；倫理正矣，而臣子上侵之令以熄。以若所爲，豈爭利其國而不顧君親者乎？去疾宜有莒國也明矣。故國本無二君也，聖人於是退展輿而進去疾，則無二君之義明，而國家豈有不定于一者乎？若去疾乃公子，而入莒曷爲止稱名氏乎？蓋統系之重，惟知有王法者能承之。周室，四海之所推戴，列國之所稟命，所謂有父兄在不得聞斯行之者矣。詎意去疾自謂公子而可立，專有莒國而無疑。周冕服矣，而鞏洛錫封之使未臨；子爵襲矣，而城陽更立之命未請。以若所爲，豈謹守王度而可保社稷者乎？去疾自
translation_en:
…fled danger and went into exile in Qi. Now his younger brothers summoned him, and Chu of Qi brought him back, so he entered Ju from Qi. Since Zhanyu was the Viscount of Ju, why was Quji also designated by the state name as his clan name? A state is a weighty charge: only one who recognizes the bonds of human relationships can occupy its throne. Zhanyu was privy to the uprising of the people of the state and obliterated the bonds owed to ruler and father. He was what is meant by someone who, though possessing grain, may not eat it. Fortunately, Quji upheld righteousness to demand an accounting for what had happened to Mizhou, and enlisted Qi to punish Zhanyu’s crime. The rebels were removed, and the rule forbidding even an intention of harming one’s ruler or parent was sternly enforced; proper relationships were restored, and the ‘command’ for ministers and sons to encroach upon their superiors was extinguished [?]. Acting thus, could he have been someone who contended for the advantages of ruling the state without regard for ruler or parent? Clearly, Quji ought to possess the state of Ju. A state fundamentally cannot have two rulers. Thus the Sage demoted Zhanyu and advanced Quji, making clear the principle that there cannot be two rulers. How, then, could the state fail to be united under one?

Yet if Quji was a ruler’s son, why, when recording his entry into Ju, was he called only by his personal and clan names? The line of succession is a weighty matter: only one who recognizes royal law can inherit it. The house of Zhou was upheld by all within the Four Seas, and the various states received their commands from it. This is what is meant by saying that, while one’s father and elder brothers are still present, one may not immediately act upon something one has heard. Who could have expected Quji to think that, because he was a ruler’s son, he could take the throne, and to claim sole possession of Ju without hesitation? He had donned Zhou’s ceremonial cap and robes, yet no envoy conferring investiture had arrived from Gong and Luo; he had succeeded to the rank of viscount, yet had not requested a command authorizing the installation of a new ruler in Chengyang. Acting thus, could he be someone who scrupulously observes royal ordinances and can preserve the altars of soil and grain? Quji himself …

title: 正德八年福建鄉試錄
text:
絕先公也明矣故土本無二王也聖人於是
重王命而絕去疾則無二王之義明而天下
豈有不定于一者乎吁與去疾者所以正一
國之大倫誅去疾者所以正天下之大法一
筆削間其關繫豈小小哉抑攷鄭齊嘗爭國
矣忽白係國而突糾不與則鄭齊忽白所宜
有也吳楚嘗僭號矣周室稱王而吳楚不葬
則王號惟周所宜稱也必如是然後國無二
君而奪宗妨貴之禍熄土無二王而改玉改
===
步之念絕此春秋所以爲春秋而非聖人莫
能脩也歟
禮記
流而不息合同而化而樂興焉
葉竒
同考試官教諭方 批 不息同化處塲中士
子講多分析不明此作獨能得之
考試官教諭沈 批 詞氣舂容平淡殆有
得於樂者
punctuated:
絕先公也明矣。故土本無二王也，聖人於是重王命而絕去疾，則無二王之義明，而天下豈有不定于一者乎？吁！與去疾者，所以正一國之大倫；誅去疾者，所以正天下之大法。一筆削間，其關繫豈小小哉！抑攷鄭齊嘗爭國矣，忽白係國而突糾不與，則鄭齊忽白所宜有也。吳楚嘗僭號矣，周室稱王而吳楚不葬，則王號惟周所宜稱也。必如是，然後國無二君，而奪宗妨貴之禍熄；土無二王，而改玉改步之念絕。此《春秋》所以爲《春秋》，而非聖人莫能脩也歟！

《禮記》
流而不息，合同而化，而樂興焉。
葉竒

同考試官教諭方批：不息同化處，塲中士子講多分析不明，此作獨能得之。

考試官教諭沈批：詞氣舂容平淡，殆有得於樂者。
translation_en:
…had plainly severed himself from the former duke. Thus, the realm fundamentally admits of no two kings. Here the Sage upholds the king’s command and repudiates Quji. With the principle that there can be no two kings made clear, how could All under Heaven fail to be united under one ruler? Ah! To approve Quji is to rectify the cardinal relationships within a single state; to condemn Quji is to uphold the fundamental law of All under Heaven. Could the implications of a single act of inclusion or deletion be slight?

Consider also that Zheng and Qi once experienced struggles for their thrones. Hu and Bai are linked to their states by name, whereas Tu and Jiu are denied this recognition: Zheng and Qi were therefore rightfully the possessions of Hu and Bai. Wu and Chu once usurped the royal title. Yet the house of Zhou is styled royal, while the burials of the rulers of Wu and Chu go unrecorded: thus, only Zhou was entitled to use the title of king. Only in this way can a state have no two rulers, extinguishing the calamity of usurping the legitimate line and encroaching upon superior rank; and only in this way can the realm have no two kings, ending thoughts of changing jade insignia and ceremonial gait—that is, changing allegiance. Is this not what makes the Spring and Autumn Annals what it is, and why none but the Sage could have compiled it?

Book of Rites
“Flowing without ceasing, uniting in harmony and bringing about transformation, music thus arises.”
Ye Qi

Comment by Associate Examiner Fang, Instructor: On the passage concerning ceaselessness and transformation through union, most candidates in the examination hall fail to distinguish and explain the meanings clearly. This composition alone grasps them.

Comment by Examiner Shen, Instructor: The language and its cadence are ample and unhurried, plain and mild. The writer seems to have attained an understanding of music.

title: 正德八年福建鄉試錄
text:
考試官學正魏批如太羹玄酒遺味深長
論造化之和肇聖人之樂蓋樂以和爲主也
孰謂聖人之樂而不肇於造化自然之和哉
記樂記者謂夫樂之作雖在於聖人樂之情
則肇於天地是故天地之間陰陽而已變而
爲四時之錯行也往者過來者續其出有源
而不窮播而爲五氣之順布也靜之終動之
始其運有常而不已然天地訢合混融而無
間以煦以嫗萬物於是乎發育也陰陽妙合
===
和洽而相通以敷以受庶類於是乎露生也
絪縕化醇而不容以獨異如此孰非天地自
然之和乎是和也雖曰寂乎其無聲而有聲
之樂已胚胎於其中雖曰杳乎其無形而有
形之樂已權輿於其内五聲六律之相宣人
知爲聖人精神之運用也而不知所以相宣
之妙則始於是和之充周焉終始小大之相
生人知爲聖人心術之流通也而不知所以
相生之妙則原於此和之宣泄焉是則樂之
punctuated:
考試官學正魏批：如太羹玄酒，遺味深長。

論造化之和肇聖人之樂，蓋樂以和爲主也。孰謂聖人之樂而不肇於造化自然之和哉？記《樂記》者謂夫樂之作雖在於聖人，樂之情則肇於天地。是故天地之間，陰陽而已。變而爲四時之錯行也，往者過，來者續，其出有源而不窮；播而爲五氣之順布也，靜之終，動之始，其運有常而不已。然天地訢合，混融而無間，以煦以嫗，萬物於是乎發育也；陰陽妙合，和洽而相通，以敷以受，庶類於是乎露生也。絪縕化醇而不容以獨異，如此，孰非天地自然之和乎？是和也，雖曰寂乎其無聲，而有聲之樂已胚胎於其中；雖曰杳乎其無形，而有形之樂已權輿於其内。五聲六律之相宣，人知爲聖人精神之運用也，而不知所以相宣之妙，則始於是和之充周焉；終始小大之相生，人知爲聖人心術之流通也，而不知所以相生之妙，則原於此和之宣泄焉。是則樂之
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Wei, an Instructor: “Like the unseasoned broth and plain water used in sacrifice, it leaves a profound and lingering savor.”

The harmony of creation gives rise to the music of the sages, for harmony is the governing principle of music. Who could say that the sages’ music does not originate in the spontaneous harmony of creation? The author of the Record of Music maintains that although music is made by the sages, its essential character originates in Heaven and Earth. Between Heaven and Earth there are simply yin and yang. In their transformations they become the alternating courses of the four seasons: what has gone passes away, and what comes succeeds it; their emergence has a source and is inexhaustible. In their diffusion they become the orderly distribution of the five vital energies: stillness ends and movement begins; their circulation follows a constant pattern and never ceases. Heaven and Earth unite joyfully, blending without separation; through warming and nurturing, the myriad things develop and grow. Yin and yang unite wondrously, harmoniously communicating with each other; through imparting and receiving, the many kinds of beings emerge into life. Intermingling, they transform things into their fullest substance, allowing none to stand apart. Which of these processes is not the spontaneous harmony of Heaven and Earth?

Although this harmony may be called silent and soundless, audible music already takes embryonic form within it. Although it may be called obscure and formless, music possessing form already has its beginnings within it. People recognize the mutual expression of the five tones and six pitch standards as the working of the sages’ spiritual powers, but they do not recognize that the wonder of this mutual expression begins in the all-pervading fullness of this harmony. People recognize the mutual generation of endings and beginnings, the small and the great, as the free flow of the workings of the sages’ minds, but they do not recognize that the wonder of this mutual generation originates in the outpouring of this harmony. Thus, music’s…

title: 正德八年福建鄉試錄
text:
所由興者如此聖人本之以作樂豈非天地
之和也哉雖然此以自然之樂情而言也上
文所謂天高地下萬物散殊而禮制行矣則
以自然之禮制言之夫一和一序固禮樂之
本然必序之以禮乃可和之以樂是猶一動
一靜固天地之分而動者又未甞不本於靜
也周子曰萬物各得其理而後和故禮先而
樂後其深知禮樂之本者歟
天子者與天地參故德配天地兼利萬
===
物與日月並明明照四海而不遺微
小其在朝廷則道仁聖禮義之序燕
處則聽雅頌之音行步則有環佩之
聲升車則有鸞和之音居處有禮進
退有度百官得其宜萬事得其序詩
云淑人君子其儀不忒其儀不忒正
是四國此之謂也
林繼顯
同考試官教諭方批題雖無傳詩證甚
punctuated:
所由興者如此。聖人本之以作樂，豈非天地之和也哉？雖然，此以自然之樂情而言也。上文所謂「天高地下，萬物散殊，而禮制行矣」，則以自然之禮制言之。夫一和一序，固禮樂之本然；必序之以禮，乃可和之以樂。是猶一動一靜，固天地之分，而動者又未甞不本於靜也。周子曰：「萬物各得其理而後和，故禮先而樂後。」其深知禮樂之本者歟！
天子者，與天地參，故德配天地，兼利萬物；與日月並明，明照四海，而不遺微小。其在朝廷，則道仁聖禮義之序；燕處，則聽雅頌之音；行步，則有環佩之聲；升車，則有鸞和之音。居處有禮，進退有度，百官得其宜，萬事得其序。《詩》云：「淑人君子，其儀不忒。其儀不忒，正是四國。」此之謂也。
林繼顯
同考試官教諭方批：題雖無傳，詩證甚
translation_en:
…such is the source from which music arises. When the sage takes this as his foundation in creating music, is it not the harmony of Heaven and Earth? Nevertheless, this speaks of the inherent character of music in the natural order. The preceding statement, “Heaven is high and Earth is low; the myriad things are dispersed and distinct, and the ordering of ritual operates,” speaks of the ordering of ritual in the natural order. Harmony and order are indeed intrinsic to music and ritual; yet things must first be ordered through ritual before they can be harmonized through music. This is like movement and stillness: although they are distinct aspects of Heaven and Earth, movement invariably has its basis in stillness. Master Zhou said, “Only after the myriad things each attain their proper principle do they achieve harmony; therefore ritual comes first and music afterward.” Surely he understood profoundly the foundation of ritual and music!
The Son of Heaven forms a triad with Heaven and Earth; thus his virtue matches Heaven and Earth, and he benefits all things alike. He shines alongside the sun and moon, his light illuminating all within the Four Seas and overlooking nothing, however small. At court, he follows the ordered principles of benevolence, sagacity, ritual propriety, and righteousness; in private repose, he listens to the music of the Odes and Hymns. When he walks, his jade pendants sound; when he mounts his carriage, its luan and he bells chime. His conduct in his dwelling accords with ritual, and his advances and withdrawals observe due measure. The hundred officials each occupy their proper place, and the myriad affairs each attain their proper order. The Book of Odes says: “The good man, the gentleman—his deportment is without fault. His deportment is without fault, and he sets right the states in the four quarters.” This is what it means.
Lin Jixian 林繼顯

title: 正德八年福建鄉試錄
text:
明作者務於穿鑿而各持一說殊戾本旨此篇卓
有定見而詞足以發之故錄之以破羣疑
考試官教諭沈批語和而莊
考試官學正魏批簡而文
記者詳人君治已而成化必引詩以明之也
甚矣君身所繫之大也身有不治其何以成
天下之化哉記者引詩以明之其旨切矣記
經解者謂夫君身為天下之本治身為萬化
之源彼天子也者中天地而為主與天地而
===
相參故其德之廣大配乎天地合萬物以曲
成之而小大各足其明之高遠並乎日月合
四海以照臨之而微小不遺其在朝廷也則
道乎仁聖禮義之序而非法不道焉其在燕
處也則聽乎二雅三頌之音而非禮弗聽焉
懼夫鄙詐之萌也行步節以環佩之聲升車
和以鸞和之音而自能養其心矣慮夫惰慢
之設也居處必有品節之禮進退必有揖揚
之度而自能制其外矣然君為之則臣必行
punctuated:
明，作者務於穿鑿，而各持一說，殊戾本旨。此篇卓有定見，而詞足以發之，故錄之以破羣疑。
考試官教諭沈批：語和而莊。
考試官學正魏批：簡而文。
記者詳人君治已而成化，必引詩以明之也。
甚矣，君身所繫之大也！身有不治，其何以成天下之化哉？記者引詩以明之，其旨切矣。記《經解》者謂夫君身為天下之本，治身為萬化之源。彼天子也者，中天地而為主，與天地而相參。故其德之廣大配乎天地，合萬物以曲成之，而小大各足；其明之高遠並乎日月，合四海以照臨之，而微小不遺。其在朝廷也，則道乎仁聖禮義之序，而非法不道焉；其在燕處也，則聽乎二雅三頌之音，而非禮弗聽焉。懼夫鄙詐之萌也，行步節以環佩之聲，升車和以鸞和之音，而自能養其心矣。慮夫惰慢之設也，居處必有品節之禮，進退必有揖揚之度，而自能制其外矣。然君為之，則臣必行
translation_en:
…clear. Writers strain after contrived interpretations, each maintaining a different explanation, greatly at odds with the original meaning. This essay displays a firm and outstanding interpretation, with language adequate to express it. We therefore record it to dispel the many doubts.
Examiner Shen, Instructor, comments: “The language is harmonious yet dignified.”
Examiner Wei, School Instructor, comments: “Concise yet elegant.”
The recorder explains in detail how a ruler cultivates himself and brings about moral transformation, necessarily citing the Odes to make this clear.
How great are the consequences that depend upon the ruler’s own person! If he fails to govern himself, how can he bring about the moral transformation of all under Heaven? The recorder cites the Odes to illuminate this point: his intent is indeed pressing. The author of “Explanation of the Classics” holds that the ruler’s person is the foundation of all under Heaven, and that governing himself is the source of every moral transformation. The Son of Heaven occupies the center between Heaven and Earth as sovereign, forming a triad with them. Thus the breadth and greatness of his virtue match Heaven and Earth: he embraces all things and brings each to fulfillment according to its particular nature, so that great and small alike attain sufficiency. The loftiness and reach of his illumination equal the sun and moon: he encompasses and shines upon all within the Four Seas, leaving out nothing, however minute.
At court, he speaks of the ordered principles of benevolence, sageliness, ritual propriety, and righteousness, saying nothing that fails to accord with proper standards. In his private quarters, he listens to the music of the Lesser and Greater Odes and the three collections of Hymns, hearing nothing contrary to ritual propriety. Fearing the first stirrings of baseness and deceit, he regulates his steps by the sound of his pendant jades and, when mounting his carriage, harmonizes his movements with the sounds of its luan and he bells; thus he can nurture his heart. Concerned that indolence and arrogance might become established [?], he ensures that his daily conduct follows the graded restraints of ritual and that his advances and withdrawals observe the proper measure of ceremonial gestures; thus he can regulate his outward bearing. Yet when the ruler practices these things, his ministers will certainly follow…

title: 正德八年福建鄉試錄
text:
上好之則下必從由是百官以治而貴賤各
得其分不相侵越也萬事以理而先後各順
其次無有紊亂也人君能治巳而成化如此
彼鳲鳩之詩有云淑人君子有常度而心一
則見其儀之不忒矣儀不忒而可觀則足以
正夫四國矣今天子巳既正而軌範以肅下
自化而政務亦脩詩之所言非即此之謂歟
是則身者化之所本化者身之所致君人者
可不知所務哉大抵治身莫要於禮樂也慨
===
自三代以還禮樂之廢久矣而欲持是以治
身不幾於迂遠乎先儒之論學固有所謂持
敬之說矣朝廷居處進退之間而必節之以
禮者此敬也燕處行步升車之時而必和之
以樂者亦此敬也誦經解之文而兼考先儒
之說則治身之道盡之矣
第貳塲
論
君子莫大乎與人爲善
punctuated:
上好之，則下必從。由是百官以治，而貴賤各得其分，不相侵越也；萬事以理，而先後各順其次，無有紊亂也。人君能治巳而成化如此，彼《鳲鳩》之詩有云：「淑人君子，有常度。」而心一，則見其儀之不忒矣；儀不忒而可觀，則足以正夫四國矣。今天子巳既正，而軌範以肅；下自化，而政務亦脩。詩之所言，非即此之謂歟？是則身者，化之所本；化者，身之所致。君人者，可不知所務哉？大抵治身莫要於禮樂也。慨自三代以還，禮樂之廢久矣，而欲持是以治身，不幾於迂遠乎？先儒之論學，固有所謂持敬之說矣。朝廷居處進退之間，而必節之以禮者，此敬也；燕處行步升車之時，而必和之以樂者，亦此敬也。誦《經解》之文，而兼考先儒之說，則治身之道盡之矣。
第貳塲
論
君子莫大乎與人爲善
translation_en:
…When those above delight in it, those below will surely follow. Thus the hundred officials are well governed, and the noble and the lowly each keep to their proper station without encroaching upon one another; all affairs are put in order, and each follows its proper sequence, without confusion. Such is the transforming influence a ruler can achieve by governing himself.
